about: The one capability ledger for RunMat simulation. Status, requirement ids, verification cases and docs pages live here; ANALYSIS_IDENTITIES, the docs' pending flags, Validation → Status and the per-family Validation pages (from its reference checks) are generated from it. See docs/schema/ledger.schema.json.

capabilities.title: Modal residual vectors and applied-load static correction for modal-reduced structural steps
Electromagnetic transient (eddy-current A–φ time stepping)
capabilities.acceptance: `runmat check` and `runmat run` admit `electromagnetic transient` through ANALYSIS_IDENTITIES; a canonical example runs to completion on the release CLI with a receipt compared to a reference.

checks.title: Cantilever bending against beam theory
checks.problem: A 1 m steel cantilever (E = 200 GPa, ν = 0.3) with a 100 mm × 100 mm section is fully fixed at x = 0 and carries a 1,000 N downward traction resultant on the free end face. It is the cantilever of the [linear static](../guides/linear-static.md) and [mesh refinement](../guides/mesh-refinement.md) guides, run as a public study on Tet10 meshes at 150, 75, 50 and 25 mm and Tet4 meshes at 150 and 50 mm.
checks.reference: Euler–Bernoulli beam theory: tip deflection $\delta = FL^3/3EI$ = 0.2000 mm and top-surface bending stress $\sigma = Mc/I$ with $M = F(L - x)$, 5.40 MPa at x = 100 mm. The support reaction equals the applied 1,000 N. Timoshenko theory adds the shear deflection $FL/\kappa GA \approx$ 0.0016 mm (0.8 %), so a converged solid model lies between the two theories.
checks.quantity: Largest displacement on the loaded end face; nodal von Mises stress on the top surface at x = 100 mm, one section depth from the clamp; support reaction. The largest element stress at the clamped edge is recorded to show the singularity of the fully fixed face.
checks.tolerance: None set; the receipts record each value. Tet10 tip deflection is expected between the Euler–Bernoulli and Timoshenko values.
checks.result: Tet10 tip deflection converges to 0.2007 mm, 0.34 % above Euler–Bernoulli theory and below the Timoshenko value. The stress at x = 100 mm settles at 5.41 MPa, 0.2 % above beam theory. The largest element stress at the clamped edge does not settle (5.39, 5.45, 5.27, 5.76 MPa), as expected at a singularity. The reaction balances 1,000 N on every mesh. Tet4 locks in bending: −50 % at 150 mm and −19 % at 50 mm.
checks.citation: (J. M. Gere and B. J. Goodno, *Mechanics of Materials*, 8th ed., Cengage Learning, 2013.)

checks.title: Tet4 patch test under an affine displacement field
checks.problem: Connected patches of linear tetrahedra (Tet4) under an affine displacement field, the standard patch test for solid elements.
checks.reference: The exact uniform strain and stress of the affine field (strain 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 in x, y and z; stress 32, 40 and 48 in the fixture's units), its strain energy, and nodal forces equal to the independent boundary tractions.
checks.quantity: Recovered strain and stress at elements and integration points, strain energy, internal nodal forces.
checks.tolerance: Absolute 1e-12 on strain and 1e-11 on stress and energy; relative 1e-12 on nodal forces and energy.

checks.title: Tet10 nodal stress recovery under a linear stress field
checks.problem: Two quadratic tetrahedra (Tet10) sharing a face carry a linear stress field; the two elements belong to different regions.
checks.reference: The linear stress field evaluated exactly at every corner and midside node, with no averaging across the region interface node.
checks.quantity: Recovered nodal stress components.
checks.tolerance: Absolute error at most 1e-12 × (1 + |σ|) per component.

checks.title: Shell membrane patch under biaxial plane stress
checks.problem: A one-layer shell patch in uniform biaxial membrane stress.
checks.reference: Plane-stress membrane resultants $N_x = \sigma_x t$, $N_y = \sigma_y t$, $N_{xy} = 0$, no bending or shear resultants, and von Mises stress $\sqrt{\sigma_x^2 - \sigma_x\sigma_y + \sigma_y^2}$.
checks.quantity: Membrane force resultants, bending and shear resultants, von Mises stress.
checks.tolerance: Relative 1e-11 on resultants; bending and shear resultants below 1e-12.

checks.title: Simply supported plate under sinusoidal load
checks.problem: A simply supported plate meshed with triangular shell elements carries a sinusoidal transverse pressure; the mesh is refined.
checks.reference: Navier's series solution for the center deflection of a simply supported plate.
checks.quantity: Center transverse displacement.
checks.tolerance: The center displacement approaches the Navier value with refinement; the finest-mesh error is below 8 %.
checks.citation: (S. P. Timoshenko and S. Woinowsky-Krieger, *Theory of Plates and Shells*, 2nd ed., McGraw-Hill, 1959.)

checks.title: Fundamental frequency of an axial rod
checks.problem: A solid slab rod, fixed at one end and free at the other, in axial vibration on Tet4 meshes (2, 4 and 8 cells) and Tet10 meshes (1, 2 and 4 cells). The retained one-mode response is also compared with a direct harmonic solve.
checks.reference: Fixed–free rod fundamental frequency $f_1 = c/4L$ with $c = \sqrt{E/\rho}$.
checks.quantity: First natural frequency; modal-truncation response against the direct harmonic response.
checks.tolerance: Frequency error falls by more than 3× (Tet4) or 6× (Tet10) per refinement; finest-mesh error below 2e-3 (Tet4) and 2e-4 (Tet10).

checks.title: Axial rod under harmonic end traction
checks.problem: A Tet4 slab rod, fixed at one end, carries a harmonic axial traction on the free end at three frequencies on both sides of the first resonance; 2, 4 and 8 cells.
checks.reference: The continuum complex displacement of the driven rod and the support reaction $-F/\cos kL$.
checks.quantity: Complex displacement field and support reaction; mean input power of the undamped response.
checks.tolerance: Displacement and reaction errors fall by more than 2.5× per refinement and are below 2e-2 on the finest mesh; mean input power below 1e-9.

checks.title: Undamped free vibration under average-acceleration integration
checks.problem: An undamped oscillator in free vibration, integrated with the Newmark average-acceleration rule, both directly and in modal coordinates, with the time step halved twice.
checks.reference: The exact harmonic free response.
checks.quantity: Displacement and velocity at the final time.
checks.tolerance: Error ratio above 3.8 per halving of the time step (second order) on both paths; finest direct Newmark error below 2e-3; modal relative residuals at most 2e-15.

checks.title: Rod under affine forcing in time
checks.problem: A Tet4 and a Tet10 rod under a physical forcing that is affine in space, integrated with 20, 40 and 80 time intervals, with and without damping.
checks.reference: The independent continuum response of the rod and its work–energy balance.
checks.quantity: Displacement, velocity and acceleration fields; work–energy balance.
checks.tolerance: Spatially exact quantities below 1e-12; time-discretization errors fall by more than 3× per halving and are below 2e-4 at 80 intervals.

checks.title: Fixed–free column against Euler's buckling load
checks.problem: A solid column, 1 m long with a 100 × 50 mm section, fixed at the base and free at the top, carries a 250 kN axial preload; Tet10 mesh.
checks.reference: Euler's critical load for a fixed–free column, $P_{cr} = \pi^2EI/4L^2$.
checks.quantity: First buckling load factor; eigenpair residuals.
checks.tolerance: First load factor within 1 % of $P_{cr}$/250 kN; eigenpairs converged to a relative tolerance of 1e-8.
checks.citation: (S. P. Timoshenko and J. M. Gere, *Theory of Elastic Stability*, 2nd ed., McGraw-Hill, 1961.)

checks.title: Modal combination rules
checks.problem: Two signed modal responses with set frequencies and damping are combined by SRSS, absolute sum and CQC.
checks.reference: The SRSS, absolute-sum and CQC formulas evaluated independently, including an independently computed CQC correlation coefficient.
checks.quantity: Combined peak response.
checks.tolerance: Relative 2e-13.
checks.citation: (A. Der Kiureghian, "A response spectrum method for random vibration analysis of MDF systems," *Earthquake Engineering & Structural Dynamics* 9(5), 419–435, 1981.)

checks.title: Uniaxial bar beyond yield
checks.problem: A bar in uniaxial tension loaded past yield, with J2 plasticity and linear hardening, solved by Newton iteration on Tet4 and Tet10 meshes and restarted cold from its persisted state.
checks.reference: The closed-form uniaxial elastoplastic stress at the final load (5.6 in the fixture's units).
checks.quantity: Axial stress at every integration point; restart state.
checks.tolerance: Axial stress within 2e-10 of the closed form.
checks.citation: (J. C. Simo and T. J. R. Hughes, *Computational Inelasticity*, Springer, 1998.)

checks.title: Manufactured fully yielded cube
checks.problem: A cube under body force and surface traction yields completely; J2 plasticity, Tet4 and Tet10 meshes, applied in one increment and in eight.
checks.reference: A manufactured polynomial J2 solution: quadratic terminal strain with an exact radial return on its proportional path.
checks.quantity: Displacement, stress, hardening variable, plastic history, energies and reaction.
checks.tolerance: Tet10 in one increment: displacement, stress, hardening variable and energy errors below 1e-7 under the Keast15, Duffy5 and Duffy8 rules. In eight increments the yield front crosses elements mid-step; that path error falls at order 1.5 or better with refinement. Tet4: every quantity refines.

checks.title: Two-layer slab in series
checks.problem: A slab of two half-meter layers with k = 1 and 4 W/(m·K), held at fixed temperatures on its outer faces; Tet4.
checks.reference: One-dimensional series thermal resistance: piecewise-linear temperature and a uniform flux of 160 W/m².
checks.quantity: Nodal temperature; element heat flux; dependence on the order in which the materials are authored.
checks.tolerance: Temperature within 1e-7 K; flux within 1e-6 W/m²; reordering the materials changes the result by less than 1e-10.

checks.title: Bar between two fixed temperatures
checks.problem: A bar held at a hot and a cold end temperature with insulated sides.
checks.reference: Fourier's law through the bar, $Q = kA\,\Delta T/L$.
checks.quantity: Heat entering and leaving through the prescribed ends; net prescribed reaction.
checks.tolerance: Heat flow within relative 1e-8 of $kA\,\Delta T/L$; the net reaction cancels to 1e-8 of it.

checks.title: Tet10 conduction patch test
checks.problem: A single quadratic tetrahedron under a linear temperature field.
checks.reference: Constant-gradient patch: conductivity rows sum to zero, the gradient is exactly (2, 3, −1), the flux is $-k\nabla T$, and the integrated capacity equals $\rho c_p V$.
checks.quantity: Conductivity row sums, temperature gradient, heat flux, integrated capacity.
checks.tolerance: Relative 1e-12.

checks.title: Radiating bar
checks.problem: A 1 m steel bar ($k$ = 45 W/m/K) takes 1000 W/m² on one end and radiates from the other ($\varepsilon$ = 0.8, 300 K surroundings). The public example is [radiating-bar.fea](../examples/radiating-bar.fea); the test runs the same bar on Tet4 and Tet10 meshes.
checks.reference: Gray-surface radiation at the radiating end, $q = \varepsilon\sigma_{SB}(T^4 - T_\infty^4)$, and conduction $qL/k$ across the bar.
checks.quantity: Temperatures at both ends and along the bar; applied and radiated power.
checks.tolerance: Nodal temperature within relative 1e-8 of the closed form; applied power equals radiated power.
checks.result: RunMat gives 416.6790 K at the radiating end and 438.9013 K at the heated end; the closed form gives the same values to 1e-12. 10 W applied, 10 W radiated.

checks.title: Slab radiating from a fixed hot face
checks.problem: A slab held at 400 K on one face radiates from the opposite face; Tet4 and Tet10.
checks.reference: The scalar gray-surface equilibrium of the slab, solved independently by bisection.
checks.quantity: Nodal temperature, gradient and flux; radiated power against conducted power.
checks.tolerance: Temperature, gradient and flux within relative 1e-8; radiated power equals the prescribed-face power within 1e-8.

checks.title: Uniformly heated insulated body
checks.problem: An insulated body with uniform volumetric heating, integrated with backward Euler on Tet4 and Tet10 meshes.
checks.reference: The continuum temperature history of the heated body and its stored-energy law: storage rate equals applied power.
checks.quantity: Temperature at every step; applied, stored and boundary power.
checks.tolerance: Discrete solution within 1e-8; error equals the backward-Euler term $B\,t_f\,\Delta t$ within 1e-8 and falls at first order (ratio below 0.56 per halving); storage rate equals applied power within 1e-8; energy residual below 1e-10.

checks.title: Manufactured radiative cooling
checks.problem: A body cooling by surface radiation under a manufactured solution, on Tet4 and Tet10 meshes with 8, 16 and 32 backward-Euler steps.
checks.reference: The manufactured temperature history and its gradient, flux and stored heat.
checks.quantity: Temperature, gradient, heat flux and storage; power closure.
checks.tolerance: Every error falls by more than 1.8× per halving of the step (first order); power closes.

checks.title: Homogeneous slab capacitor and conductor
checks.problem: A homogeneous slab between two terminals, solved as a capacitor (electrostatics) and as a conductor (steady current) on Tet4 and Tet10 meshes.
checks.reference: Parallel-plate closed form: linear potential, uniform field, terminal charge or current, stored energy and Joule power.
checks.quantity: Nodal potential, field, terminal flux, energy, Joule power.
checks.tolerance: Potential and field within 1e-8; flux imbalance and energy identity below 1e-8; energy and displacement field within relative 1e-8.

checks.title: Two-material slab in series
checks.problem: A slab of two aligned materials between two terminals, on Tet4 and Tet10 meshes.
checks.reference: Series capacitance and series resistance, with continuous normal flux across the interface.
checks.quantity: Potential, energy, Joule power, interface flux.
checks.tolerance: Relative 1e-8.

checks.title: Harmonic polynomial potential
checks.problem: The harmonic potential $x^2 - y^2$, solved with both the electrostatic and the conduction equation; Tet10 on one mesh and Tet4 on three.
checks.reference: The exact field $(-2x, 2y, 0)$ and energy of the harmonic polynomial.
checks.quantity: Field and energy.
checks.tolerance: Tet10: field and energy exact to relative 1e-8. Tet4: field error falls below 0.6 of the previous mesh at each refinement.

checks.title: Uniformly charged dielectric slab
checks.problem: A dielectric slab with uniform volume charge on three Tet4 meshes.
checks.reference: Closed form: quadratic potential, linear field, conserved charge and energy $\varepsilon/6$ in the fixture's units.
checks.quantity: Potential, field and energy errors; flux imbalance.
checks.tolerance: Per refinement: potential error order above 1.7, field order above 0.8, energy error below 0.35 of the previous mesh. Finest mesh: potential below 0.005, field below 0.1, energy below 0.025. Flux imbalance below 1e-9.
checks.result: Potential error 4.6e-2, 1.1e-2, 2.9e-3; field error 0.29, 0.14, 0.072; energy error 0.25, 0.063, 0.016.

checks.title: Steady current in a copper bar
checks.problem: A 1 m copper bar ($\sigma$ = 59.6 MS/m) with 1 mV across its ends; Tet10.
checks.reference: Uniform current density $J = \sigma V/L$ and Joule power $P = V^2/R$.
checks.quantity: Current density; Joule power from the loss density and from the terminal current.
checks.tolerance: Relative 1e-9.
checks.result: Peak current density 59 600.000 A/m² against 59 600 A/m² (relative difference 1e-13); Joule power 0.596000 W against 0.596 W (1e-14).

checks.title: Magnetic field of a square conductor
checks.problem: A square conductor carries a uniform axial current density and is grounded on every exterior face; Tet4 and Tet10 geometry with the lowest-order edge basis, three meshes per order.
checks.reference: An independent Fourier-series solution for the vector potential, flux density and energy; the series tail is bounded by $8/(3\pi^4N^3)$ at N = 255 terms.
checks.quantity: Vector potential, flux density and magnetic energy.
checks.tolerance: Each error falls by more than 1.4× per refinement. Finest mesh: potential below 0.02, flux density below 0.10, energy below 0.25. Physical and gauge residuals below 8e-10.
checks.result: Flux-density error 0.166, 0.116, 0.064 and energy error 0.80, 0.39, 0.12 on 1, 2 and 4 cells.

checks.title: Skin effect in a driven conductor
checks.problem: A conducting strip ($W$ = 1 mm, $L$ = 2 mm, $t$ = 1 mm, $\sigma$ = 1 MS/m) under an air gap $g$ = 0.5 mm, returned through a grounded plane, is driven by a 2 A terminal current at $t/\delta$ = 0.5, 2 and 4 with 8, 16 and 32 cells through the thickness and along the current.
checks.reference: Parallel-plate line impedance $Z = \frac{L}{W}\left[\frac{k\coth(kt)}{\sigma} + i\omega\mu_0 g\right]$ with $k = (1+i)/\delta$ and $\delta = \sqrt{2/\omega\mu_0\sigma}$.
checks.quantity: Terminal impedance $Z = U/I$; Joule loss against delivered power; Poynting balance and charge continuity.
checks.tolerance: Impedance error below 2e-3 at 32 cells and reduced by more than 3× from 8 to 32 cells; Joule loss equals $\tfrac12\mathrm{Re}(U\bar I)$ within 1e-8; Poynting and charge-continuity residuals below 1e-8.
checks.result: Relative impedance error at 8, 16 and 32 cells: 4.2e-4, 1.0e-4, 2.6e-5 at $t/\delta$ = 0.5; 7.3e-3, 1.8e-3, 4.5e-4 at 2; 1.6e-2, 3.9e-3, 9.8e-4 at 4. The error falls fourfold per refinement.
checks.citation: (S. Ramo, J. R. Whinnery and T. Van Duzer, *Fields and Waves in Communication Electronics*, 3rd ed., Wiley, 1994.)

checks.title: Low-frequency limit of a driven strip
checks.problem: The strip of the skin-effect check, voltage driven at 1 Hz.
checks.reference: DC resistance $L/(\sigma W t)$ and the low-frequency gap inductance.
checks.quantity: Real and imaginary parts of the terminal impedance.
checks.tolerance: Resistance within relative 1e-6; reactance within relative 2e-2.

checks.title: Microstrip impedance against Hammerstad–Jensen
checks.problem: A zero-thickness surface microstrip on a 0.2 mm substrate over a reference plane, open above, with w/h = 0.5, 1 and 2 on εr = 4.4, w/h = 4 on εr = 2.2 and w/h = 1 on εr = 9.8, on the default graded mesh.
checks.reference: Hammerstad and Jensen's closed forms for Z0 and εeff of a zero-thickness microstrip; the authors state Z0 in air within 0.01 % (w/h ≤ 1) and 0.03 % (w/h ≤ 1000) and εeff within 0.2 % (εr ≤ 128, 0.01 ≤ w/h ≤ 100) of exact quasi-static values.
checks.citation: E. Hammerstad and Ø. Jensen, "Accurate models for microstrip computer-aided design," IEEE MTT-S International Microwave Symposium Digest, 1980, pp. 407–409.
checks.quantity: Z0, εeff and delay per length of the line.
checks.tolerance: 0.5 % on Z0 and εeff; the delay follows from εeff.

checks.title: Stripline and coupled stripline against Cohn's exact forms
checks.problem: Zero-thickness strips centred between planes 0.5 mm apart in εr = 3.0: single strips with w/b = 0.2, 0.5 and 1.0, and edge-coupled pairs with (w/b, s/b) = (0.5, 0.2), (0.5, 0.5) and (0.3, 1.0).
checks.reference: Cohn's conformal-mapping solutions, exact for zero-thickness strips between infinite planes: Z0 = (30π/√εr) K(k)/K(k′) with k = sech(πw/2b), and the even- and odd-mode impedances with k_e = tanh(πw/2b) tanh(π(w+s)/2b), k_o = tanh(πw/2b) coth(π(w+s)/2b).
checks.citation: S. B. Cohn, "Characteristic impedance of the shielded-strip transmission line," IRE Trans. Microwave Theory Tech., vol. MTT-2, pp. 52–57, 1954; S. B. Cohn, "Shielded coupled-strip transmission line," IRE Trans. Microwave Theory Tech., vol. MTT-3, pp. 29–38, 1955.
checks.quantity: Z0 of single strips; even- and odd-mode impedances of pairs, with Zdiff = 2 Zodd, Zcommon = Zeven / 2, εeff = εr and zero far-end coupling in the homogeneous dielectric.
checks.tolerance: 0.3 % on each impedance; the identities hold to 1e-9.

checks.title: Microstrip and stripline against IPC-2141A
checks.problem: 35 µm copper. Surface microstrips (w, h, εr) = (0.35 mm, 0.2 mm, 4.1), (0.2 mm, 0.15 mm, 4.3) and (0.15 mm, 0.25 mm, 3.5); centred striplines (w, b, εr) = (0.15 mm, 0.6 mm, 4.2), (0.1 mm, 0.5 mm, 3.6) and (0.2 mm, 0.8 mm, 4.4). Every case is inside the forms' stated ranges.
checks.reference: IPC-2141A surface microstrip Z0 = 87/√(εr + 1.41) · ln(5.98h/(0.8w + t)) for 0.1 < w/h < 2.0 and 1 < εr < 15, and symmetric stripline Z0 = 60/√εr · ln(1.9b/(0.8w + t)) for w/b < 0.35 and t/b < 0.25.
checks.citation: IPC-2141A, Design Guide for High-Speed Controlled Impedance Circuit Boards, IPC, 2004.
checks.quantity: Z0 of each line.
checks.tolerance: 5 %: the IPC-2141A forms are empirical fits, so this check bounds agreement with the board-industry forms; Hammerstad–Jensen and Cohn are the tight references.

checks.title: Mesh and enclosure convergence of Z0
checks.problem: A 0.35 mm, 35 µm-thick surface microstrip on 0.2 mm of εr = 4.1, meshed with edge sizes of 7, 3.5, 1.75 and 0.875 µm, then with the default mesh in an enclosure twice the default width and height.
checks.reference: Self-convergence: the change in Z0 between successive refinements, and the change from doubling the enclosure.
checks.tolerance: Successive changes decrease and the last is below 0.1 %; the enclosure changes Z0 by under 0.05 %.

checks.title: Rigid rectangular cavity modes
checks.problem: A rigid-walled cube cavity. The kernel test uses quadratic meshes with 2, 3 and 4 cells per side and a linear mesh with 2 and 4; the public-study test runs a 1 m cube through the command line.
checks.reference: Rectangular-cavity frequencies $f_{lmn} = \frac{c}{2}\sqrt{(l/L_x)^2 + (m/L_y)^2 + (n/L_z)^2}$, including the zero-frequency uniform mode and degenerate triplets; for the 1 m cube the first axial mode is $c/2L$ = 171.5 Hz.
checks.quantity: First eight natural frequencies; residuals and mass orthogonality.
checks.tolerance: Quadratic: error ratio above 2.5 per refinement and below 4e-3 at 4 cells, residuals at most 1e-8, mass orthogonality below 1e-8. Linear: error ratio above 3 from 2 to 4 cells. Command line: uniform mode below 1e-3 Hz and the three axial modes within 2 % of 171.5 Hz.
checks.citation: (L. E. Kinsler, A. R. Frey, A. B. Coppens and J. V. Sanders, *Fundamentals of Acoustics*, 4th ed., Wiley, 2000.)

checks.title: Open–open duct modes
checks.problem: A duct with pressure-release ends; Tet10.

checks.quantity: First five natural frequencies; modal pressure on the released nodes.
checks.tolerance: Relative 4e-3; released-node pressure exactly zero.

checks.problem: A plane wave travels down a duct to an anechoic (matched) end.

checks.quantity: Power through the matched end; accounted input power.
checks.tolerance: Relative 1e-3 (0.1 %).

checks.problem: A plane layer between an incident port and an anechoic port, at several frequencies, on two meshes.
checks.reference: Closed-form plane-wave transmission loss of the layer at each frequency.
checks.quantity: Transmission loss.
checks.tolerance: Below 0.05 dB on the finer mesh at every frequency, and no larger than on the coarse mesh.

checks.problem: A plane wave crosses the interface between two fluids in an aligned slab. The public example runs the same interface with impedance ratio m = 4 at 500, 1000 and 2000 Hz.

checks.tolerance: Kernel: power residual below 1e-8; finest-mesh pressure error below 0.004 of the incident amplitude and velocity error below 0.01. Public example: within 0.1 dB of 1.938 dB.

checks.problem: A duct with loss factor 2ζ driven at one end.

checks.quantity: Nodal complex pressure; dissipated against input power.
checks.tolerance: Pressure error ratio above 3 per refinement and below 0.004 on the finest mesh; power error below 1e-9.

checks.problem: A duct terminated by a tabulated complex impedance; Tet4.

checks.quantity: Nodal complex pressure; dissipated against input power.
checks.tolerance: Pressure error ratio above 3 per refinement and below 0.004 on the finest mesh; power error below 1e-9.

checks.quantity: Pressure phase and amplitude; acoustic energy.
checks.tolerance: Finest-mesh pressure error below 0.10; energy RMS error below 0.15; power error below 1e-8.

checks.title: Incident wave on an impedance boundary
checks.problem: A planar incident wave meets an impedance boundary with reflection coefficient 7/13.

checks.tolerance: Pressure error below 0.004 of the incident amplitude; velocity below 0.01; intensity terms below 0.005; power error below 1e-8.

checks.problem: An anchored slab carries a plane wave across declared pairs of periodic planes.
checks.reference: The exact plane wave with Bloch phase across each periodic pair.
checks.quantity: Pressure, mean velocity and signed intensity.
checks.tolerance: Pressure error below 0.004; velocity below 0.01; intensity below 0.005.

checks.problem: A slab closed by a local plane-wave radiation boundary.

checks.problem: A bar with resistivity $\rho(T) = \rho_0(1 + \alpha(T - T_0))$ carries a fixed current with its ends held at $T_0$ and its sides insulated: $\sigma_0$ = 3 S/m, $\alpha$ = 0.004 /K, $k$ = 1 W/m/K, $I$ = 34.64 A on a unit cube, Tet10 with 2, 4 and 8 cells.
