requirements.title: Exact geometry, persistent topology and engineering exchange
requirements.acceptance: Each named criterion is independently mandatory in its required scope; component witness linkage does not establish full acceptance.

obligations.criterion: A geometry declaration has exactly one closed source form: imported file, declarative construction, immutable derivation, or materialized RunMat generator. All forms produce the same typed canonical geometry asset and exact-revision boundary consumed by region resolution and meshing.

The file form admits one inspectable exact-geometry source: STEP is the primary documentation and production example format. Other admitted exact-CAD and canonical geometry sources remain registry-governed rather than accepted as arbitrary extensions.

The construction form is a typed feature graph, not an imperative CAD macro: The initial production feature set should remain deliberately bounded: dimensioned primitives, rigid transforms and instances, extrude/revolve, governed booleans, holes/pockets, and qualified fillet/chamfer operations. Fully constrained sketching, mating, advanced surface construction, healing, and arbitrary kernel commands are added only with typed semantics, persistent-topology evidence, and independent geometry verification. There is no generic string opcode or raw OCCT escape hatch. The language's closed operation set and an exact-kernel provider's qualified profile are separate facts. Static checking resolves every operation and quantity without loading a kernel. Before a materialization task starts, provider-neutral planning compares the entire resolved graph with one explicit capability set and bounded feature, dependency, instance, Boolean-operand, and live-artifact counts. A graph containing an operation outside that profile fails before execution; there is no approximate implementation, alternate host fallback, or partial artifact. Each provider operation is promoted only after its exact topology, mass properties, canonical closure, failure behavior, and history semantics have direct fixtures. This permits the language to retain one stable typed vocabulary while native providers grow only through evidence-backed profiles. The qualified native exact profile must cover all bounded operations in this acceptance specification. Extrusion and revolution retain profile lineage; holes and pockets require positive volumetric overlap rather than accepting a no-op cut; and fillet/chamfer consume a typed edge selection whose target membership and cardinality are resolved before kernel dispatch. Kernel history joins its final result to the ordinary importer through the private canonical B-rep shape-table key. That key is transport-local and never becomes public identity: the imported result still publishes the same digest-based, occurrence-qualified persistent entity ids used by regions, meshes, and analysis.

Geometry is never changed in place. A derived declaration creates a new revision with explicit lineage: Source edits may feel like CAD mutation, but semantic evaluation is an immutable dependency graph. The base geometry remains addressable and cacheable. The derived revision records the source revision, operation graph, inputs, kernel capability cohort, persistent-entity history, validation, and resulting exact digest. Parameter sweeps over geometry inputs correctly invalidate geometry, mesh, projection, operator, and result identities while reusing unaffected upstream artifacts. A study binds geometry parameters explicitly with the same named-argument form used for a model: Each argument must name a declared geometry input and must have its exact physical type. Required geometry inputs have no implicit value; optional inputs retain their declaration default. The realized study contains canonical SI geometry bindings, not references back into the case scope, so workers never reinterpret source expressions. Missing, duplicate, unknown, or dimensionally incompatible bindings fail during study checking. Mesh refinement or p-order change is not geometry derivation. Large-deformation configuration, ALE motion, contact motion, and other evolving solver configurations are typed analysis states, not source-level CAD mutation.

General procedural construction remains in `.m` and materializes through the same bounded, source-resolvable generator boundary as signals: The imported function must return exactly one immutable `geometry.Generated` value. It builds that value with the ordinary typed RunMat geometry API (`geometry.box`, `geometry.cylinder`, `geometry.sphere`, transforms/instances, Boolean operations, `geometry.finish`, and typed region outputs); it cannot return a kernel handle, tessellation, `geometry.Asset`, or provider-specific object. The checker validates the exact named signature, immutable scalar output class, effects, captures, and capabilities. Execution freezes the source revision and arguments, runs one portable callable task, content-addresses its provider-neutral feature program and region outputs, then runs the ordinary bounded exact-geometry materialization workload. No worker calls live RunMat code from inside meshing or a solve. Geometry realization uses one portable workload for imported, constructed, derived, and generated sources. Its immutable request binds the exact definition and parameter values, source-object closure, import/healing policy, provider id/version/kernel ABI and operation capability set, planning limits, and CPU/memory/scratch/time/artifact/transfer envelope. Imported source chunks are content verified before kernel admission; a derived request names the exact prior definition, document, manifest root, and complete exact-object closure. Results publish that same canonical exact-geometry closure used by meshing plus a typed receipt containing resolved regions, feature history, resource facts, and request identity. Scheduler placement does not enter geometry-definition identity, while worker selection requires the exact provider capability. Generated sources bind an independently revalidated admission receipt containing the exact program revision, callable, source digest, function ordinal, capabilities, ordered SI arguments, and derived identities. The result reference is transport-scoped and therefore excluded from geometry-request identity; its content digest, schema, length, and access authority are verified separately. Supplying geometry bytes in place of generator evidence is not a fallback.

Feature-derived selection must solve the topological naming problem explicitly. Stable feature identity, complete provider-proven source-to-result lineage, semantic feature roles, persistent entity digests, cardinality, and ambiguity diagnostics are part of geometry realization evidence. Face or edge vector position is never persistent identity. A feature parameter change that splits one selected face into several is accepted only when the selector's declared cardinality and role allow it; otherwise realization fails with both revisions and the affected feature path.

Every feature result publishes the complete final entity inventory grouped by topology role, the entities introduced by that operation, and a canonical typed lineage record for every source entity. A lineage record maps its source to all provider-proven descendants in that operation's final result; an empty descendant set means that no source entity survived. Unchanged, modified, split, merged, generated, and extinguished outcomes therefore share one closed contract instead of parallel created/modified/deleted interpretations. `boundary_introduced_by` is legal only when the inventory and lineage are explicitly complete; missing kernel history never degrades to proximity matching. Selection through later features composes these provider-proven relations and intersects the result with the declaration's final exact topology. A feature's transient intermediate entities are not a region merely because they once existed.

Imported, constructed, derived, and generated sources all end at the same immutable exact-geometry closure. Constructed graphs have no hidden source. Derived graphs receive exactly their declared source revision. Generated calls receive already-resolved typed arguments and execute once as a bounded materialization task; downstream feature execution and meshing consume the published closure rather than invoking RunMat code. Revisions bind all parent geometry digests, the resolved operation graph, provider cohort, result digest, and region-resolution evidence.

A region is a typed, geometry-owned selection, not a free-standing FEA label. Import first creates an exact geometry asset with an identity, revision, persistent entities, and imported semantic metadata. Each nested region selector is then evaluated against that exact asset. The resolved region retains the geometry identity/revision, selector and selection digest, matched persistent entity ids, topology role, cardinality evidence, and source provenance. Meshing carries those persistent ids into boundary and volume provenance, so a model assignment reaches solver entities without matching names again after meshing.

A mesh declaration either references an immutable canonical mesh artifact or describes a meshing request against exact geometry. These are closed alternatives. Quality and partition controls are optional and validated only when present.

The initial selector surface maps directly to imported geometry metadata and persistent ids: `name` and `tag` refer to metadata actually imported from the source—such as STEP/XCAF product, body, component, assembly, layer, color, or material ownership—or to explicit annotations in a supported geometry source. `id` selects the role-scoped source alias reported by geometry inspection, such as `face_000001` or `solid_000001`. `persistent_id` selects the complete canonical entity identity when a durable machine-produced reference is required. These are deliberately distinct: a convenient import ordinal is not represented as immutable topology identity. A name is not inferred from the local alias such as a local housing alias, and a tag does not mean a geometric heuristic. Users inspect or pick the admitted geometry before authoring selectors.

The inspection result and interactive geometry view expose selectable ids, names, tags, topology roles, and grouping provenance. If the CAD file contains no meaningful boundary grouping, RunMat may still expose exact face ids, but it cannot invent names such as `Fixed_Base`. The durable choices are to add semantic names/layers/groups in CAD, author a separately persisted geometry annotation revision, or deliberately select inspected source aliases or persistent ids. Spatial predicates such as "lowest face" are not silently substituted; if introduced later, they will be explicit bounded queries with cardinality and stability evidence.

Consumers cannot reinterpret a declared role. A face cannot become a solid material domain merely because an assignment asks for one. A selector that matches the wrong kind, no entities, or an unexpected cardinality fails during checking. Editing/reimporting CAD creates a new geometry revision; a stale resolved region or incompatible mesh cannot be reused silently.

RunMat should treat STEP AP242 as more than a source of boundary representation when the exchange file actually contains richer product data. ISO 10303-242:2025 includes parametric and constrained geometry, sketches, manufacturing features, part properties, composite definitions, and material specifications/properties in its scope. That scope does not guarantee that a particular CAD exporter wrote those objects, that it wrote a regenerative feature history, or that the active geometry kernel implements every AP242 representation. Admission therefore publishes an exact capability inventory for each file rather than treating `AP242` as one boolean. OCCT/XCAF import retains label ownership, layers, colors, and physical material name/description/density evidence. Retention is not a claim of general AP242 parameter, constitutive-property, composite, or regenerative-feature support. The surface inventory must distinguish present translated data, raw discoverable AP242 data, unsupported data, and data that was absent from the export.

Imported parameters have stable source identity, declared physical type, units, value, bounds or constraint facts where present, ownership path, edition/profile, and read/write capability: Textual names and external identifiers are selectors at the file boundary; successful resolution produces a strongly typed parameter reference. Duplicate names, missing units, incompatible dimensions, ambiguous ownership, unsupported constraint graphs, and conflicting values fail with source attribution.

Changing an imported parameter is an immutable derivation, not in-place mutation: This checks only when admission proves that the selected parameter is writable and that RunMat has a qualified evaluator for the complete dependent parametric/constraint representation. A flattened B-rep with a nominal dimension annotation remains readable metadata; it is not promoted to a writable parameter. Unsupported regeneration fails during checking/planning rather than silently editing topology or falling back to a geometric guess.

AP242 material and product properties are imported as typed, provenance-bearing candidates. They do not silently become FEA constitutive laws, because a CAD material may be only a name, a visual material, a density, a specification reference, a composite constituent, or a property qualified by temperature or another operating environment. Adoption is explicit:

The primary physical-material graph follows the CAx-IF recommended practice: stock material is a `PRODUCT` in a recognized material `PRODUCT_RELATED_PRODUCT_CATEGORY`; material properties point to its `PRODUCT_DEFINITION`; a part-to-material callout is a `MAKE_FROM_USAGE_OPTION`; applicable specifications are `APPLIED_DOCUMENT_REFERENCE` relationships; and each dependent environment is resolved through typed `DATA_ENVIRONMENT.elements` property definitions and measure representations. `MATERIAL_DESIGNATION` remains a supported legacy STEP alternate, but it is not treated as the preferred or only AP242 material model. Free-form descriptions such as `"20 C"` never become typed environment evidence.

Every adopted property retains its AP242 entity/persistent id, source association, units, specification/document reference, environment, uncertainty/validation facts where available, and conversion evidence. Missing required capabilities reject before analysis. Visual materials are never accepted as physical materials. Geometry-to-material associations may create selectable material domains, but the FEA model still makes the typed material assignment explicit so that coverage and conflicts remain reviewable. `use` property paths and `require ... = <quantity>` clauses are typed syntax nodes. Requirements use the same unit catalog, affine-temperature rules, expression checker, and SI normalization as the rest of `.fea`; material import does not maintain a private string parser or unit table. An environment requirement must hold for every adopted property, not merely one property in the candidate.

For CAD round trips, RunMat retains the immutable admitted source and emits a typed change set plus an export-conformance report. A qualified AP242 writer may update supported parameters, properties, associations, persistent ids, and validation properties. Unsupported or lossy content must be reported; RunMat must not claim a lossless round trip merely because it can write another STEP file. Sidecar change sets remain available when the source representation cannot be safely regenerated or rewritten. Implementation follows the applicable AP242 edition and the public CAx-IF/MBx-IF Recommended Practices for persistent ids, user-defined attributes, materials/composites, validation properties, PMI, and product/assembly structure. Conformance is feature/profile-specific and fixture-tested across producing CAD systems. Apply ISO 10303-242:2025 and the applicable MBx-IF CAx Recommended Practices for profile-specific conformance.

Material, section, layup, orientation, and other physical-property assignments are distinct typed forms. Bulk materials normally target solids or cells; shells and beams additionally require their relevant section/layup/orientation contracts. Boundary faces do not own a solid's bulk material. Beam-section, shell-layup, and orientation assignments use the same geometry-qualified shape but require regions declared with their compatible edge or face roles. Definitions live inside the reusable model that owns them. Their formulation is a closed nested block, not a string-valued `kind`, and every quantity is unit checked. Assignment references are canonically qualified by source module, model, and local definition identity even though source code uses the concise model-local name:

Sections initially admit general, rectangular, circular, and tubular beams plus homogeneous shells. Layups require an ordered, uniquely named ply sequence; every ply names its material, thickness, and angle. Ply order is `along_surface_normal` or `opposite_surface_normal`. A layup reference surface is its mid-surface, first-ply surface, last-ply surface, or an explicit length offset from the mid-surface. Homogeneous shells independently name their mid-surface, positive-normal surface, negative-normal surface, or an explicit mid-surface offset. Linear through-thickness constitutive terms are integrated analytically, so neither form exposes a fictitious integration-point count. Drilling stabilization belongs to the shell formulation, not physical section authoring. Orientations admit global Cartesian, explicit Cartesian, cylindrical, and spherical frames. A laminate owns shell constitutive behavior, so assigning both a homogeneous material and a layup to the same shell target is an error. Section, layup, and orientation coverage are each independently single-owner; composition rejects conflicting included-model assignments.
Every active material-bearing entity must have exactly one compatible owner. Gaps, overlaps, wrong topology roles, stale geometry revisions, and missing material capabilities fail before assembly.

dependencies: Shared physical, numerical, identity, resource, accuracy and release acceptance remains mandatory.

requirements.title: Typed source queries, recovery and retained result objects
requirements.acceptance: Each named criterion is independently mandatory in its required scope; component witness linkage does not establish full acceptance.

obligations.criterion: Outputs are typed named queries over analysis results: The field path names its recovery location explicitly: `field.node`, `field.element`, `field.integration_point`, `field.constraint`, and the other closed location kinds are distinct typed namespaces. This is required even when one location looks conventional, because quantities such as reaction force and von Mises stress may be available at more than one location. Recovery or interpolation between locations is an explicit operation, never a hidden field-name default. The first executable transfer is deliberately narrow: `recover` accepts scalar element von Mises stress and requires `to = node, using = volume_weighted_average`. The family kernel weights every incident element contribution by its exact physical volume. The source location, output location, method, topology incidence count, and operation ceiling are retained in the canonical recovery request; the published field definition also retains this derivation, so it cannot be confused with a quantity evaluated natively at nodes. Operation order is semantic: `recover(von_mises(stress), ...)` is supported, while `von_mises(recover(stress, ...))` is rejected until a true nodal tensor-recovery kernel exists.

`max` is intentionally the ordinary RunMat operation name, not a parallel FEA-only `maximum` builtin. RunMat has one canonical operation catalog with one public semantic identity and documentation entry per operation. The catalog may contain several strongly typed overloads and lowering bindings: - `max(numeric_tensor, ...)` lowers to the ordinary RunMat array/runtime implementation; - `max(scalar_field<Q, L>, over = region<L>)` lowers to a canonical partitionable FEA spatial observation and returns `spatial_extremum<Q, L>`; - `max(history<Q>, over = time)` returns `series_extremum<Q, time>`; - `max(case_values<Q>, over = cases)` returns `case_extremum<Q>`; and - unsupported vector, tensor, complex, statistical, topology, or coordinate combinations have no matching overload and fail statically.

An extremum is not merely a number. It retains `value`, canonical location or independent-domain coordinate, owning region/entity or case, tie policy, source field/sample, and reduction evidence. For example, `output.peak_stress.value` has type `stress`, while `output.peak_stress.location` is a topology-compatible location. Vector fields require an explicit projection such as `magnitude`, `component`, or a governed invariant before scalar extrema. Complex and statistical fields similarly require an explicit representation whose physical meaning is valid.

The shared catalog owns, for every overload: - stable operation and overload identity; - source name, aliases, availability by frontend, and documentation category; - typed parameters, named arguments, defaults, return type, units/dimension transform, and shape; - permitted quantity domains, scalar/complex/statistical forms, topology locations, frames, and coordinates; - purity, determinism, differentiability, and effect facts; - partitionability, associativity/order constraints, tie behavior, equivalence policy, and resource-cost shape; and - lowering binding to a runtime implementation, FEA observation plan, provider operation, or compile-time constructor.

The `.fea` compiler and RunMat compiler query that same catalog, but choose different overloads from their input types and frontend context. Runtime bindings remain runtime-owned and FEA observation execution remains FEA-owned; sharing a semantic catalog does not force both domains through the same implementation. New FEA-specific operations such as `resultant` or a governed surface `moment` still register in the same catalog and can expose compatible object overloads in `.m`; there is no second hidden list.

The initial output-expression surface is closed and documented: - projections and representations: `component`, `magnitude`, `real`, `imag`, `phase`, `principal`, and `von_mises` where dimensionally and physically defined; - location transfer: `recover`, with a closed output location and field-transfer method whose executable family implementation, provenance, and topology-resolved cost must exist; - spatial evaluation: `sample`, `interpolate`, `integral`, `mean`, `rms`, `norm`, `min`, `max`, `resultant`, and `moment`; - series evaluation: `sample`, `min`, `max`, `absmax`, `mean`, `rms`, `variance`, and `envelope`, with explicit independent-domain weighting where required; and - sweep evaluation: `collect`, `min`, and `max`, preserving typed case coordinates and attribution. Spatial operations keep their physical dimensions explicit. For example:

`principal` accepts only a real symmetric stress or strain field and requires `maximum` or `minimum`; it is not a string-dispatched tensor expression. An integral multiplies the source dimension by the selected edge, face, or volume measure. A surface stress or pressure resultant has force dimensions, while `moment` adds exactly one length dimension. Discrete reaction forces and moments already carry their integrated dimensions and are not integrated a second time.

Spatial selection, interpolation, and independent-domain sampling are separate operations. The first keeps a field over an exact typed region, the second evaluates shape functions at physical positions, and the third creates a history on an explicit domain: The domain is not a label: `time` requires time coordinates, `frequency` requires frequency coordinates, `mode` requires positive integer mode indices, and `load_factor` is dimensionless. `input.<name>` binds a history to a declared study parameter. A series reduction must repeat the history's domain, and weighted statistics must choose either `uniform_samples` or `trapezoidal_independent_domain`; there are no alternate spellings or hidden weighting defaults. Variance squares the sample dimension. Extrema and envelopes retain their source coordinate and attribution rather than collapsing to unlabelled numbers. The assignment form uses the documented output defaults: representation-compatible 64-bit precision, lossless compression, canonical retention, chunk-addressable partial access, and publication purpose. An output block changes policy without mixing storage decisions into `sample`, `interpolate`, or a physical reduction: The closed retention choices are `canonical`, `until_dependents_complete`, `latest_samples`, and `explicit_samples`. The latter two require a positive `maximum_samples`; the former two reject it. Compression is `lossless`, `none`, or `error_bounded`; error-bounded compression requires a finite `maximum_relative_error` strictly between zero and one and is forbidden for solver-control or downstream-state outputs. Partial access is `manifest_and_chunks` or `whole_artifact`. Purpose is `publication`, `visualization`, `solver_control`, or `downstream_state`. Real results accept `real64` and complete complex results accept `complex128`; representation and precision mismatch fails while compiling the study. These policies change the typed observation/resource/publication plan and its identity; they do not silently change the selected physical quantity or domain. This list is generated from or mechanically checked against the catalog. An operation cannot appear in parser completion, documentation, or execution unless a matching catalog overload and lowering exist. Conversely, catalog overloads admitted for `.fea` automatically supply completion, hover types/units, named-argument completion, signature help, diagnostics, go-to documentation, and reference examples to the LSP. The expression graph checks quantity, dimension, scalar/complex/statistical domain, topology location, frame, coordinate, sampling, and reduction compatibility. It remains a closed query language, not general code embedded in the solver.

Field and history outputs are lazy manifest-backed objects. Reading or plotting them requests bounded chunks. Global reductions execute partition-locally and merge deterministically. A sweep collecting scalar outputs produces a typed table/tensor keyed by its axes. Retaining every large case field must be explicit: Intermediate procedure state is published only when explicitly retained or required by a downstream analysis. Output requests and retention affect planned compute, storage, and transfer costs, but placement does not alter their physical or reduction semantics.

dependencies: Shared physical, numerical, identity, resource, accuracy and release acceptance remains mandatory.

requirements.title: Declarative source semantics and product tooling
requirements.acceptance: Each named criterion is independently mandatory in its required scope; component witness linkage does not establish full acceptance.

obligations.criterion: RunMat `.fea` files are declarative source files for finite-element and coupled-physics work. The language describes physical models, studies, parameter spaces, requested results, and optional execution policy. It resolves to the same strongly typed canonical analysis contracts used by the RunMat API, native workers, cluster workers, persistence, and result tooling. The language is deliberately smaller than RunMat's `.m` language. It has declarations, references, dimensioned literals, immutable inputs, bounded pure expressions, and closed domain-specific forms. It has no mutation, loops, arbitrary evaluation, ambient workspace, filesystem operations, or live callbacks. Numerical generation and general programming remain in `.m` files and enter an FEA study through explicit typed imports and materialization. The `.fea` extension selects this language. Source files do not contain a version banner, format marker, or `kind` line. If a future incompatible syntax edition is ever required, the project selects it once in `Runmat.toml`; it is not repeated in every file.

1. **Physical meaning is visible.** Materials, assignments, constraints, loads, procedures, transitions, and output requests are explicit. The compiler may derive bookkeeping, but may not invent physical content. 2. **Requiredness is semantic and minimal.** A declaration requires only the information needed to make that declaration unambiguous. A local one-off study does not declare a sweep, execution policy, cluster, GPU, retry policy, or outputs it does not use. 3. **Nesting follows ownership.** A declaration is nested only when its identity and lifetime belong to its parent. Models own reusable physical content; studies own runnable procedure graphs; sweeps own study-input cases; execution policies own optional placement and resource preferences. 4. **Closed choices are typed.** Procedure kinds, topology roles, quantities, constraints, interpolation, solvers, placement, and retention policies are grammar or registry-backed choices, not arbitrary strings passed to solver code. 5. **References are source-resolvable.** Imports name a file and a symbol. Editors can navigate, rename, diagnose, and explain every cross-file reference. 6. **Study-definition identity is independent of placement.** Local, cluster, retry, worker count, and physical partitioning are execution facts. They do not change the meaning of a study or sweep case. 7. **Large data stays large-data aware.** Fields and histories are lazy, chunked result objects. The language never implies that distributed fields must be gathered into the driver process. 8. **One lowering boundary.** Source text lowers through a typed FEA AST and semantic model into canonical analysis contracts. Workers never parse `.fea` source and solvers never dispatch on source strings.

A file is a module and may contain any number of peer top-level declarations. There is no artificial one-study or one-model limit. Imports have an explicit symbol kind, local name, and source file. A function import names a function file directly; a package folder is not required. The imported `.m` file must define a compatible named function entrypoint. Scripts are rejected because they have no stable typed input/output contract and depend on ambient workspace state. The supported import kinds are initially `geometry`, `mesh`, `material`, `model`, `study`, `sweep`, `execution`, and `function`. A source file may export multiple declarations. Importing a symbol does not import all declarations in that file, and wildcard imports do not exist. Paths are relative to the containing source file, confined to the admitted project/dependency source graph, cycle-checked, and recorded by logical path and content digest. Installed project dependencies may provide `.fea` modules, but a reference always resolves to inspectable source; there are no hidden Rust-side model templates. Top-level declaration namespaces are separate and explicit in references: Inside an owning declaration, unqualified references first resolve in that declaration's lexical scope and then in the module's imported/top-level scope. Ambiguity is an error. Stable identity is derived from the declaration path and canonical content, never from source order.

| Declaration | Purpose | Required members | Optional members | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `geometry` | Admit CAD or canonical geometry | exactly one source | authored units, admission assertions | | `mesh` | Name an existing mesh or a meshing request | geometry plus source/request | quality goals, partition hints | | `material` | Reusable capability aggregate | name or at least one capability | density, mechanical, damping, thermal, electrical, magnetic, acoustic, fluid capabilities | | `model` | Reusable physical definitions | only what its consuming analyses require | typed region inputs/references, materials, assignments, sections, constraints, interfaces, signals, excitations, initial conditions | | `study` | Runnable semantic procedure graph | model, geometry/mesh binding, at least one analysis | inputs, execution reference, outputs, accuracy requirements, assessments | | `sweep` | Named cases over study inputs | target study, at least one axis or case | combination mode, collected outputs, execution reference | | `execution` | Reusable placement/resource policy | no members; an empty policy is useless but valid | placement, backend, resources, fanout, cooperative solve, resilience | Required members in this acceptance specification are structural minima. Physics-specific semantic validation supplies the real requirements. For example, linear elasticity requires compatible stiffness on every active structural material domain; dynamics additionally requires mass. A material is not forced to declare capabilities irrelevant to every consuming analysis. `sweep` and `execution` declarations are never globally required. A study without either is a complete study. Output declarations are also optional: procedures always publish their canonical terminal result and evidence, while authored outputs request additional fields, histories, reductions, or retained intermediate states. A material name is a structural syntax minimum only: realized physical material admission requires at least one compatible physical capability and each consuming formulation requires complete capability coverage.

A minimal standalone study implies neither remote execution nor a parameter sweep. No empty `execution`, `sweep`, `outputs`, or scaling block is needed. Formulation admission is physics/numerics admission, not placement policy. A study has no formulation setting: the registry admits exactly the realization the authored model and mesh select, and that exact realization survives in realized study identity, portable workloads, accuracy evidence, and published results. Execution profiles and CLI placement overrides cannot change it, and a stale `formulation` line is a checker error.

A `model` owns reusable physical intent: typed inputs (including typed region inputs), materials or material references, property assignments, constraints, natural boundaries, connectors, interfaces, signals, excitations, load cases, initial conditions, spectra, and family-domain declarations. Geometry declarations own the selectors that produce regions; a model either refers to those regions explicitly or accepts them as typed inputs. It does not own solver placement, worker resources, retries, or scheduler topology. Models compose explicitly by reference: Composition is additive by typed stable identity. Equal definitions deduplicate. Conflicting definitions fail with both source locations. There is no last-writer-wins override order. A model may be parameterized rather than copied and edited: An `include` does not import geometry, mesh, study analyses, output requests, or execution policy. The study binds every required region input to a region from its exact geometry. A model that names a module-level geometry region directly is deliberately geometry-specific; one that accepts typed region inputs is reusable across compatible geometries.

Spectral environments are named model-owned physical inputs. They are not untyped procedure options and are not placement policy. A procedure refers to them through the bound model, so the reference is navigable and the compiler can prove that the selected model actually owns it. A response spectrum declares exactly one monotonically increasing abscissa (`frequencies` or `periods`), ordinates whose physical dimension follows the selected response quantity, exactly one damping representation, and a nonzero direction. Solver policies are closed enums. Defaults are limited to conventional representational policy: `maximax`, interpolation matching the abscissa, `reject` extrapolation, CQC modal combination, SRSS directional combination, 90% minimum cumulative mass, no truncation correction, disabled rigid-response separation, authored construction, and a sampling-adequacy ratio of one. The response, damping, and direction have no defaults because they change the physical meaning: `response` is one of `relative_displacement`, `relative_velocity`, `relative_acceleration`, `absolute_acceleration`, `pseudo_velocity`, or `pseudo_acceleration`. Modal combination is `cqc`, `srss`, `ten_percent`, or `absolute_sum`. Directional combination is `srss`, `absolute_sum`, or `percentage`; percentage combination alone requires its two coefficients. Truncation correction is `none`, `residual_mode`, or `missing_mass`; missing mass requires a compatible zero-period acceleration. Rigid response is `disabled`, `gupta`, or `lindley_yow`, and each enabled form requires its method-specific physical parameters. Incompatible response quantities and policies fail during model checking. A random excitation carries the full cross-power spectral-density matrix at every frequency. It does not accept a diagonal-only shortcut as a different domain object: diagonal environments use zero off-diagonal entries in the same contract. The real and imaginary tensors have shape `frequency × channel × channel`; a single unit suffix applies recursively to the regular tensor. Omitting the imaginary tensor means an all-real spectrum. Every matrix must be Hermitian and positive semidefinite, every channel id is unique, and matrix width must equal the channel count: The initial random-excitation quantity and density convention are respectively `base_acceleration` and `one_sided_per_hertz`; the explicit names remain in the typed contract so future quantities or conventions cannot silently reinterpret existing files. Interpolation is `linear_frequency`; extrapolation is `reject` or `hold_endpoint`. Frames default to `global` until a channel explicitly names a supported typed frame. Either numerical payload may instead be generated by an imported pure `.m` function. The axis, channels, dimensions, interpolation, combination policy, and evidence remain in `.fea`; only the ordinates or CPSD tensor are generated. The function's first required input is the numeric sample axis, its remaining inputs are closed named arguments, and it returns one numeric array with the shape required by the declaration: Checking resolves the exact source module, symbol, source digest, signature, effects, and ordered arguments. Execution freezes and runs that callable as a bounded portable materialization task, validates the output shape and physical spectral invariants, and replaces the generator with content-addressed numerical data before assembly. No live function or runtime capture enters a solver kernel or cluster rank.

Inputs are immutable, strongly typed, and scoped to the declaration that consumes them: An input without a default must be bound by its caller. A study may expose model inputs, and a sweep may bind exposed study inputs. CLI or RunMat-language invocation may bind study inputs using the same typed contract. Bounds and allowed sets are validation constraints, not clipping rules. `let` introduces an immutable derived value: Expressions initially support literals, references, records, lists, arithmetic, comparisons in validation clauses, and a closed set of dimensionally typed pure constructors/reductions. They do not support mutation, recursion, loops, reflection, I/O, arbitrary function calls, or implicit unit conversion that changes physical dimension. The type system includes booleans, integers, real and complex scalars, strings where human labels or source paths are genuinely textual, dimensioned quantities, fixed-size vectors/tensors, domains, topology roles, materials and other declaration references, fields, histories, result tables, and closed domain enums. Unit checking occurs during semantic analysis.

A study binds one model instance to geometry and mesh, declares an ordered semantic procedure graph, and names requested outputs. It is the normal runnable root. Analyses own procedure-specific options, active model content, accuracy obligations, and named state retention. A dependency such as `after analysis.modes` is semantic state flow, not merely a scheduler edge. The procedure kind determines admissible input/output state kinds. Incompatible transitions fail during checking. Physical procedure domains are explicit. Modal extraction requires a positive `modes` count; transient procedures require `start_time` and `end_time`; harmonic procedures require a non-empty, strictly increasing `frequencies` list; and nonlinear load-factor procedures require `start_load_factor` and `end_load_factor`. Modal-reduced and prestressed procedures additionally name the exact upstream state they consume. These values have no hidden language defaults because changing one changes the analysis definition. Procedure-specific physics and numerical controls are a closed typed union on the canonical procedure step; they are not string-keyed solver options and are not placement policy. For example, random response requires both values in this acceptance specification rather than obtaining either from a runtime default: Modal response-spectrum procedures similarly use `spectra = [model.response_spectrum.<name>, ...]`. These paths are checked against the exact bound model and are retained as typed stable ids in the procedure graph; a similarly spelled load, signal, or random excitation cannot satisfy the reference. `modal_damping_ratio` is finite and in `(0, 1)`; `minimum_cumulative_mass_ratio` is finite and in `[0, 1]`. These values participate in study-definition identity. Frequency-interval grouping, iteration ceilings, retry, placement, and worker resource limits remain execution policy and may change without changing the study definition. The compiler derives internal activation records, task graphs, state manifests, checkpoint dependencies, and publication bookkeeping. Users do not write `lifecycle: activate` or internal state-transfer records. When a file contains one study, `runmat run file.fea` selects it. With several studies the caller specifies `--study name`. `check` resolves and type-checks without executing user code; `plan` additionally produces the canonical logical graph and resource requirements; `run` executes it.

An imported `.m` function is a source-resolvable generator, not a live solver callback: The semantic checker resolves the imported symbol through the ordinary RunMat project graph, checks its typed inputs/outputs and effects, and records source/capture provenance. Before a solve, the function is frozen and evaluated in a bounded preprocessing task. Its result is validated and published as a canonical signal or field artifact. Local, remote, distributed, and GPU solves consume that artifact; none calls back into `.m` during quadrature or iteration. Base acceleration is support kinematics, not a force-like excitation. It therefore names the constrained support region, translational degree of freedom, initial displacement and velocity, and reconstruction rule. The acceleration signal is a global vector history; the selected degree of freedom chooses its component. Ordinary loads and source terms remain under `excitation`. Named file imports are intentionally simple. Package-qualified RunMat functions remain available when a project already uses them, but examples do not require a `+folder` merely to establish provenance.

Initial conditions describe physical state at the beginning of a procedure. They belong to a reusable model, while the consuming analysis selects which named conditions apply before that step. A model therefore does not embed a study-step name: The closed initial-condition kinds are structural displacement, velocity, and angular velocity; thermal temperature; electric potential; magnetic vector potential; acoustic pressure; and fluid pressure and velocity. Vector states require an explicit coordinate frame. Scalar states have no directional frame input and lower in the global scalar convention. Each condition has exactly one value source: - `uniform` is a finite scalar or three-component vector with the exact physical dimension; - `sample` names a declared signal with the exact quantity and shape plus a typed time or study- parameter coordinate and explicit `at`, `left_limit`, or `right_limit` discontinuity approach; frequency-domain signals are not initial state; or - `field_artifact` names immutable artifact, content, topology, and field identities. Admission validates the field's quantity, shape, frame, topology, and completeness before execution. The study-binding pass creates the canonical `applies_before_step` identity and corresponding state input. A compatible upstream state takes precedence unless the receiving procedure exposes an explicit typed replacement policy; conflicting initial state is never combined implicitly.

A sweep is optional and wraps a parameterized study without changing the study's physical definition: Axes bind declared study inputs and have named values. Names give cases stable identities that do not change when source order changes. `product` forms the Cartesian product and `zip` pairs named positions. Correlated or sparse combinations use explicit cases: Every case is independently identifiable, cacheable, restartable, and schedulable. Sweep fanout is independent-task parallelism; it is not evidence of a cooperative distributed sparse solve. When an axis feeds a geometry argument, the case first realizes a complete immutable geometry binding and then constructs the ordinary exact-geometry request. Equal bindings reproduce the same request and exact result root. Changed bindings produce distinct geometry roots and therefore distinct mesh-stage, projection, operator, and result identities. A derived-geometry sweep keeps the same content-addressed source closure in every case, so the unaffected ancestor is reused rather than copied or regenerated. These rules are part of canonical identity construction and do not depend on whether cases run inline, in worker processes, or as independently scheduled cluster tasks.

Execution policy is optional. With no policy in the source, CLI/project defaults choose local or remote placement and automatic backend selection. The study remains runnable and portable. `fanout` controls independent schedulable work such as cases, frequencies, directions, or independent recovery partitions. `cooperative` requests tightly coupled distributed numerical work with shared operator ownership, halos, and collectives; it is admitted only for formulations and providers that implement and qualify it. The distinction must remain visible in plans and evidence. Placement values are `auto`, `local`, `cluster`, or a project-defined profile reference such as `profile.engineering`. Infrastructure addresses, credentials, keys, and worker secrets never appear in `.fea` source. Accelerator policy is closed and truthful: `disabled`, `preferred`, or `required`. `preferred` may fall back only when the admitted procedure permits it and must record what actually executed; `required` fails if unavailable. Resource ranges permit elastic execution without changing logical identity. Physical attempts record actual workers, partitions, devices, retries, transfers, and timing separately. Study-definition identity, logical execution identity, and physical attempt identity remain distinct. Callers may override placement without editing the study: Source policy, project policy, and CLI override combine through a typed precedence contract. Overrides may choose an equivalent placement or tighten resources; they may not silently relax a authored accuracy requirement or select an unqualified numerical implementation.

The concrete grammar will be frozen with parser implementation, but its structural contract is: module          := import* declaration* import          := "import" import_kind identifier "from" string declaration     := geometry | mesh | material | model | study | sweep | execution geometry        := "geometry" identifier ("from" geometry_ref)? geometry_block geometry_source := file_source | construct_block | derive_block | generated_source model           := "model" identifier parameter_list? block study           := "study" identifier parameter_list? block sweep           := "sweep" identifier "over" study_ref block execution     := "execution" identifier block block           := "{" statement* "}" statement       := declaration_member | local_declaration | assignment | include | output | retain local_declaration := constraint | load | load_case | signal | excitation | response_spectrum | random_excitation | initial | section | layup | orientation | interface | connector expression      := literal | reference | list | record | unary | binary | call call            := operation_name "(" argument_list? ")" reference       := identifier ("." identifier)* quantity        := number unit_expression Each geometry block has exactly one source form. `derive` requires `from`; the other forms reject it. Calls resolve through the canonical operation catalog by typed overload rather than parser hard-coding, except for the small set of structural declaration forms required by the grammar. Semicolons are not required. Newlines and closing delimiters terminate declarations where the grammar is otherwise unambiguous. Comments use `//`. Commas are required inside same-line lists, records, and argument lists and optional after a final multiline item. Formatting is canonicalized by `runmat fmt`. The grammar must preserve error recovery for editor use, retain source spans on every authored node, and avoid context-sensitive interpretation that prevents incremental parsing.

The implementation reuses RunMat infrastructure but keeps the FEA language as its own frontend: .fea text -> FEA lexer tokens -> lossless/syntax AST with source spans -> module and symbol resolution -> typed semantic FEA model -> authored-contract validation -> geometry and callable resolution -> canonical analysis contracts -> planning, execution, persistence, and evidence - `runmat-lexer` may host a separate FEA token module. - `runmat-parser` may host a separate FEA parser and AST entrypoint. - `runmat-analysis-core` owns canonical authored physical/study contracts, physical quantities, units, and domain validation without depending on source syntax. - the narrow `runmat-analysis-language` crate owns module binding, source-level semantic and unit checking, operation resolution, diagnostics, and lowering into analysis-core contracts; - `runmat-types` owns dependency-neutral operation/overload facts shared across frontends, while remaining independent of runtime `Value`; - the canonical RunMat builtin/operation catalog owns shared public operation identities, signatures, documentation facts, and frontend applicability; analysis contributes typed FEA overloads and lowering bindings without creating a parallel catalog; - `runmat-runtime` implements project, function, geometry-inspection, and execution-profile host interfaces and adapts resolved results to public values. - `runmat-lsp` dispatches by extension and shares the project symbol graph for cross-language navigation. - FEA, execution, and worker crates consume canonical resolved contracts only. The `.m` grammar and HIR are not extended with FEA-only syntax. The FEA parser does not duplicate the RunMat project graph, callable type facts, unit authorities, artifact system, scheduler, or provider capability registry. Required editor behavior includes syntax diagnostics, semantic and unit diagnostics, completion from closed registries and local symbols, hover types/units, formatting, find references, rename, go-to-definition across `.fea` and imported `.m`, signature help for imported functions, and an explain view for derived state flow and execution plans. Before the public surface is treated as stable, its complete machine ledger is reviewed for a single consistent declaration pattern. A block label always names the declared object; arguments state properties; nested blocks exist only for repeated or structurally distinct child objects; references use one qualified-symbol form; physical values carry statically checked dimensions; and execution state is not presented as authored lifecycle commands. Any inconsistent spelling, unnecessary wrapper, accidental synonym, or compiler-owned field is corrected across grammar, formatter, diagnostics, LSP, examples, and reference in the same change. This is a clean cut, not an alias migration.

The compiler/runtime publishes one typed study-presentation projection from the resolved study and canonical geometry. It contains no source syntax decisions and no rendering instructions. Each presentable declaration carries its stable authored identity, source span, activation, exact geometry/topology targets, role, physical quantity, units, frame, direction or normal semantics, distribution, schedule summary, and named function identity where applicable. The projection covers constraints, prescribed values, boundary conditions, connectors, interfaces, initial conditions, loads, excitations, and generated inputs. Unsupported or unresolved presentation is a typed diagnostic; Desktop does not guess from names or re-evaluate source. Desktop source mode uses the shared LSP. Preview mode initially uses an equal top/bottom split. The upper half shows CAD and mesh geometry with study overlays. Known vector inputs use arrows or vector glyphs with typed magnitude and units; distributed inputs visibly cover their target; generated inputs use a distinct excitation color plus a code/function marker and the resolved function name. Selection links overlays, study entries, and source spans in both directions. Overlay density is view-dependent and deterministic: 1. close views show target extent, glyph, complete quantity/unit or function label, and direction; 2. intermediate views retain the glyph and a compact value or function label; 3. distant or crowded views aggregate declarations by target and role into count/summary markers; 4. selected, erroneous, or ambiguous declarations remain individually inspectable at every level. The lower half is a study outline rather than a generic software dependency diagram. Its primary hierarchy is geometry and regions, properties and assignments, constraints and boundaries, analysis sequence, inputs and cases, requested outputs, execution policy, and validation status. Typed detail panels show units, frames, targets, activation, provenance, and source navigation. Compact toolbar toggles reveal inactive declarations and applicable but unset options so an analyst can discover supported choices without mixing them into the authored contract. The initial 50/50 split is resizable.

The DSL must be designed from the true implementation surface, not only from old documentation or example YAML. Before replacing authoring, build a machine-checkable inventory of: - every currently accepted document field and variant; - every `runmat-analysis-core` authored type and validation rule; - every runtime/CLI/Desktop study construction field; - every value that survives into canonical identity, execution requests, workers, results, persistence, and evidence; and - every implicit default, expansion, inferred activation, compatibility path, and unused field. For each item, record one disposition: 1. **authored DSL** — genuinely user intent and represented explicitly in the standing language specification; 2. **derived** — deterministic compiler output that users should not write; 3. **project/execution policy** — optional nonphysical policy, outside the model or absent unless requested; 4. **internal** — canonical execution/result bookkeeping with no source syntax; 5. **removed** — obsolete, duplicate, misleading, or unsupported behavior, with the reason and replacement; or 6. **gap** — required capability with no satisfactory language or implementation owner yet. The inventory records source type/field, cardinality, current default, target syntax, target typed owner, identity effect, validation, and tests. It is reviewed family by family and procedure by procedure. No field is preserved merely because it existed, and no behavior disappears merely because it was undocumented. Migration verification uses checked-in representative studies and compares their resolved typed contracts, semantic identities, procedure graphs, material/property coverage, signals, observations, accuracy obligations, and execution-independent results. Differences must be either zero or an explicitly reviewed correction. Negative fixtures prove that formerly implicit, ambiguous, or invalid behavior now fails with a source diagnostic. The migration is one clean cut. The runtime does not retain parallel YAML and DSL authorities, compatibility flags, dual canonicalization, dead schema types, or a conversion tool. The product has not shipped this authoring format, so no user compatibility surface exists to preserve. Internal parity fixtures may use the canonical implementation as an oracle while the replacement is built, but they are not a public reader and are deleted with the old loader after the atomic cutover. Production loading has one parser and one lowering path.

The public FEA documentation gains this structure: The language documentation contains a landing page, conceptual module/type/geometry/state/input/output/execution/function/diagnostic pages, complete grammar/declaration/procedure/constraint/operation/geometry references, and runnable static/parameterized/transient/modal/sweep/scaling/large-result guides. Reference tables are generated from, or mechanically checked against, the compiler's closed registries where practical. Every `.fea` block in documentation is parser- and type-checked in CI; runnable guides execute against checked-in STEP assets. The scaling guide distinguishes local parallelism, independent cluster fanout, and cooperative distributed numerical work. The language pages use four distinct jobs rather than blending them: - the landing page explains what a `.fea` module declares, the resolved-study object model, and the edit/check/plan/run workflow before presenting a minimal complete study; - concept pages introduce blocks, arguments, labels, references, types, quantities, units, modules, dependency resolution, and derived state with small examples tied to the same study; - guides solve concrete engineering tasks from source through checked result and explain the consequential choices at the point they occur; and - reference pages exhaustively state hierarchy, labels, fields, types/units, requiredness, defaults, exclusions, result types, diagnostics, and complete examples. This follows the useful traits of established configuration-language documentation: a small syntax vocabulary introduced through the domain model, clear module/input/output boundaries, task guides separate from specification, and reference tables that make requirements explicit. It does not copy Terraform terminology where FEA has a more precise term. Public FEA pages outside the language folder include corresponding `.fea` and `.m` examples wherever both routes can express the same operation. Prose is direct and technical; it avoids promotional filler and formulaic generated writing.

FEA-mode agent context is derived from the standing language specification, checked examples, and the canonical procedure and operation registries. It supplies a bounded language summary, relevant project symbols and importable `.m` signatures, and the exact edit/check/plan/run workflow. The primary action is editing the `.fea` source and responding to structured checker diagnostics. Broad typed tools that mirror the expanding language are removed; focused tools may remain for file access, inspection, execution, cancellation, and result retrieval when their contract is narrower than source authoring. The prompt contains no independently maintained field inventory.

The language is ready to replace the current authoring surface only when: - the current/target surface inventory has no unexplained fields or gaps; - grammar, formatter, parser recovery, semantic typing, units, imports, and cross-language symbol resolution have focused and adversarial tests; - imported, constructed, derived, and `.m`-generated geometry share one canonical artifact, immutable revision, persistent-topology, region, execution, and evidence contract; - AP242 parameters and engineering properties are capability-inventoried, strongly typed, provenance-bearing, explicitly adopted, and writable only under qualified regeneration; - all planned physical families can be expressed without string-dispatched escape hatches; - minimal local studies require no sweep or execution boilerplate; - optional sweeps and execution policies lower to the existing generic scheduling and placement authorities rather than parallel FEA-specific infrastructure; - output expressions and ordinary RunMat operations resolve through one catalog with typed frontend-specific overloads, complete LSP support, and mechanically checked reference docs; - all checked-in examples use direct, inspectable sources and STEP geometry where appropriate; - local and cluster runs of one resolved study retain identical study-definition identity; - legacy parsing and dead authoring contracts are removed; - the language reference and guides in this acceptance specification are complete, runnable, and release-checked; - Desktop source and preview modes, complete zoom-aware study overlays, the typed study outline, and bidirectional source/geometry navigation pass component, screenshot, and end-to-end tests; - every supported geometry-targeted declaration is represented by the canonical presentation projection and no Desktop code infers physics from source text; and - the FEA agent authors files through edit/check/plan/run with canonical generated context and no duplicate schema-sized mutation tool surface.

dependencies: Shared physical, numerical, identity, resource, accuracy and release acceptance remains mandatory.

requirements.title: Compiler passes and host ownership
requirements.acceptance: Source authoring, semantic lowering, geometry realization, tooling and product admission satisfy every direct criterion within their named owner. A syntax or fixture pass never closes whole language, execution, geometry or release acceptance.

obligations.criterion: 1. Add one narrow `runmat-analysis-language` crate. A real dependency boundary requires it: source syntax must depend toward canonical analysis contracts, while `runmat-analysis-core` and every numerical consumer must remain independent of lexer/parser code. Putting this compiler in core, runtime, parser, or execution would reverse or confuse a domain boundary. 2. Add a separate FEA frontend inside the existing lexer and parser crates. Do not add FEA syntax to the MATLAB token stream, AST, HIR, or MIR. 3. Put solver-neutral semantic compilation in `runmat-analysis-language`. It depends on `runmat-parser`, `runmat-analysis-core`, geometry-core contracts, and dependency-neutral operation facts in `runmat-types`; it must not depend on `runmat-builtins`, which currently owns runtime-value bindings. A narrow catalog-view trait supplies the composed catalog during compilation. 4. Put normalized geometry-authoring and exchange contracts in `runmat-geometry-core`, pure feature planning/validation in `runmat-geometry-ops`, and OCCT/AP242 translation and exact feature-kernel implementations behind `runmat-geometry-io` provider boundaries. 5. Extend the existing `runmat-builtins` catalog so `.m` and `.fea` resolve one public operation identity with typed frontend-specific overloads. Do not create `fea_builtins`, a parser-local function table, or a second documentation registry. 6. Keep filesystem, project, package, callable compilation, credentials, placement, and process concerns outside analysis core. Runtime, LSP, CLI, and native execution implement narrow host traits. 7. Workers consume canonical typed contracts and content-addressed artifacts. They never receive source ASTs and never parse `.fea` files. 8. The cutover removes the runtime YAML authoring authority. There is no dual parser, compatibility mode, or conversion command: the product has not shipped this authoring format, so preserving it would create dead product surface rather than protect users. Do not add any further crate unless implementation proves another real dependency cycle or separately deployable boundary that cannot be solved by the interfaces in this acceptance specification. File count, compile time, or a desire for a convenient dumping ground are not sufficient reasons.

A -> B means A depends on B. runmat-parser -> runmat-lexer -> runmat-types runmat-builtins -> runmat-types + runmat-value runmat-geometry-ops -> runmat-geometry-core runmat-geometry-io -> runmat-geometry-ops + runmat-geometry-core runmat-analysis-core -> runmat-types + runmat-geometry-core runmat-analysis-language -> runmat-parser + runmat-analysis-core + runmat-types + runmat-geometry-core runmat-analysis-fea -> runmat-analysis-core + canonical geometry/mesh contracts runmat-analysis-execution -> runmat-analysis-fea + generic execution/artifact contracts runmat-runtime and runmat-lsp -> runmat-builtins + runmat-analysis-language + runmat-analysis-core -> compose and supply the one catalog view CLI / Desktop / native runner -> public runtime/LSP/execution adapters Additional permitted edges: - `runmat-analysis-core -> runmat-geometry-core` already exists and remains solver-neutral. - `runmat-analysis-language -> runmat-parser` owns syntax-to-domain lowering. - `runmat-analysis-language -> runmat-analysis-core` targets canonical authored contracts rather than redefining them. - `runmat-analysis-language -> runmat-types` uses dependency-neutral operation/overload facts and exports the explicit FEA extension in those types. - Runtime and LSP, which already depend on the relevant crates, compose the standard `runmat-builtins` entries and the analysis-language FEA extension deterministically and pass a read-only `AnalysisOperationCatalog` view to the semantic compiler. - `runmat-geometry-io -> runmat-geometry-ops` implements provider contracts; neither geometry crate depends on analysis, runtime, CLI, LSP, or execution runners. - LSP depends directly on parser, analysis core, geometry core, and builtins for read-only language services. It must not obtain language semantics by calling runtime operations. Forbidden edges: - parser or lexer to analysis, geometry kernels, runtime, filesystem, or project packages; - analysis core to lexer, parser, analysis-language, `runmat-builtins`, `runmat-value`, runtime, CLI, LSP, native runner, filesystem, or host credentials; - analysis-language to `runmat-builtins`, `runmat-value`, runtime, CLI, LSP, execution runners, filesystem implementations, or host credentials; - geometry core/ops/io to FEA materials, constraints, studies, or solver procedures; - FEA numerical code to syntax AST, source paths, editor state, or AP242 parser entities; - worker code to `.fea` parsing or source-module resolution; - Desktop or Server to Rust physics implementation or plaintext server-side FEA decoding.  - lexer/parser files remain MATLAB authorities; new `fea/` siblings share only genuinely generic   span/source utilities; - analysis-core `problem/` and `study/` remain the canonical destination types; the language   compiler lowers into them rather than cloning them; - existing FEA observation/reduction and execution materialization modules are adapted behind   resolved operation/source contracts rather than replaced; - geometry core/ops/io are extended in their current roles; OCCT and AP242 details do not move up   into analysis or runtime; - runtime `fea_document.rs` and YAML authoring provide the surface ledger and temporary test facts,   then leave the production path and are deleted at cutover; - CLI, LSP, and Desktop become clients of compiler services and typed summaries, not alternate   parsers, registries, validators, or physics owners; and - the existing `runmat-analysis-execution` crate remains the narrow execution bridge justified by   generic task/artifact execution ownership; the new `runmat-analysis-language` crate is exclusively the   source-to-domain compiler and cannot absorb runtime, execution, geometry-kernel, or physics code.

crates/runmat-lexer/src/ lib.rs ... existing MATLAB lexer ... fea/ mod.rs lexer.rs token.rs trivia.rs diagnostic.rs tests.rs `fea/token.rs` owns only lexical categories. Keywords that are genuinely structural are tokens; operation names such as `max`, `resultant`, or `box` remain identifiers resolved by the operation catalog. This prevents grammar edits for every new operation overload.

crates/runmat-parser/src/ lib.rs ... existing MATLAB parser ... fea/ mod.rs span.rs diagnostic.rs syntax/ mod.rs module.rs import.rs declaration.rs geometry.rs material.rs model.rs study.rs sweep.rs execution.rs expression.rs type_syntax.rs parser/ mod.rs cursor.rs module.rs import.rs geometry.rs model.rs study.rs sweep.rs execution.rs expression.rs recovery.rs format/ mod.rs document.rs expression.rs layout.rs tests/ lexer.rs declarations.rs expressions.rs recovery.rs formatting.rs The syntax tree retains source spans and enough trivia for diagnostics and formatting. First extract only the dependency-neutral catalog vocabulary shared by builtin registration and analysis typing: crates/runmat-types/src/operation/ mod.rs identity.rs frontend.rs type_pattern.rs signature.rs quantity.rs topology.rs effect.rs distribution.rs lowering_id.rs extension.rs These are immutable facts and stable identifiers. They contain no runtime function pointer, `Value`, device buffer, analysis model, documentation renderer, registry singleton, or inventory registration. This is an extension of the existing shared type vocabulary, not a second catalog. Keep the existing catalog and extend it rather than layering another registry beside it: crates/runmat-builtins/src/catalog/ ... existing catalog files ... operation.rs overload.rs composed.rs runtime_binding.rs Responsibilities: - `operation.rs`: combines neutral operation facts with shared documentation identity; - `overload.rs`: combines the neutral typed signature and applicability with catalog validation; - `runtime_binding.rs`: owns runtime `Value` invocation only for overloads executable through the ordinary runtime builtin path; - `composed.rs`: deterministic construction of one catalog from the standard definitions plus explicit domain extensions. `runmat-analysis-language::operations` contributes the FEA overload extension through an explicit function returning neutral `runmat-types` descriptors. Runtime and LSP compose that extension with the standard catalog explicitly; there is no inventory-order dependency. Analysis language compiles through an injected read-only view and never imports `runmat-builtins` or `runmat-value`. Catalog validation rejects duplicate operation/overload identities, ambiguous signatures, missing documentation, missing lowering, and an LSP-visible overload without a checker implementation.

Existing `problem/` and `study/` remain the canonical authored domain and receive only genuinely missing typed contracts proven by the surface ledger. Core keeps no source syntax, module graph, compiler coordinator, filesystem trait, or operation registry. Its tests validate domain objects without parsing `.fea` source.

Add one narrow source-to-domain adapter crate. Its modules are compiler passes, not alternate model definitions: crates/runmat-analysis/language/ Cargo.toml src/ lib.rs compiler.rs source.rs diagnostic.rs module_graph/ mod.rs load.rs cycle.rs provenance.rs binding/ mod.rs scope.rs symbol.rs import.rs reference.rs semantic/ mod.rs types.rs units.rs expression.rs requiredness.rs operations/ mod.rs extension.rs resolve.rs result_type.rs attributed.rs lower.rs lowering/ mod.rs geometry.rs material.rs model.rs study.rs sequence.rs sweep.rs output.rs execution.rs validate/ mod.rs references.rs geometry.rs physical.rs transitions.rs outputs.rs execution.rs tests/ modules.rs types.rs geometry.rs models.rs studies.rs sweeps.rs outputs.rs diagnostics.rs `compiler.rs` is a small pass coordinator. It does not contain parsing, per-declaration lowering, or validation rules. `source.rs` defines narrow interfaces: These interfaces return immutable facts. They do not expose a filesystem, runtime `Value`, OCCT handle, compiler session, or scheduler. For editor use they may return `Unavailable` facts that produce bounded diagnostics without preventing syntax services. `AnalysisOperationCatalog` exposes immutable, dependency-neutral facts from the one composed catalog. It cannot invoke runtime builtins or return `Value`. Runtime and LSP use the same composed catalog builder; a catalog fingerprint in semantic output makes accidental composition drift observable and testable. The compiler emits one `ResolvedAnalysisProgram` containing named typed geometry definitions, models, studies, sweeps, output plans, and optional execution policies. It reuses the existing `problem` and `study` contracts; it does not invent a second set prefixed `Dsl` or suffixed `V2`.

The numerical crate receives no parser modules. It gains only the lowering targets required to execute newly typed observation operations and geometry-derived properties: crates/runmat-analysis/fea/src/ results/ observation/ ... existing evaluation ... operation/ mod.rs projection.rs spatial.rs series.rs attributed.rs compatibility.rs properties/ ... canonical property compilation ... imported_capability.rs `operation/*` consumes a resolved `ObservationOperation`, never an operation name string. Existing `SpatialReduction`, `SeriesReduction`, extrema, partition, and publication authorities are adapted instead of duplicated. It does not resolve source imports or interpret language expressions.

Do not implement the compiler here. Remove `serde_yaml` from `runmat-runtime` when no other runtime feature needs it. There is no YAML conversion utility or command. No new implementation goes into `analysis/mod.rs`. Existing public functions move behind the `public/*` facade as they are touched, and `mod.rs` converges to module declarations and narrow re-exports.

The cross-language project graph joins explicit `.fea` function imports to existing `.m` definitions and signatures. FEA completion comes from three typed sources: 1. grammar/declaration context from the syntax tree; 2. symbols/types/units from the analysis-core semantic result; and 3. operation names, overloads, named arguments, and docs from the composed canonical catalog. Do not add `.fea` cases to `core/analysis.rs`. Extract genuinely shared document/workspace behavior as needed. MATLAB semantic analysis may be split later, but FEA delivery must at minimum leave the existing god file no larger and create no new equivalent.

It does not maintain a TypeScript copy of the grammar, procedure registry, output-operation signatures, or AP242 capabilities. Break `fea-study-surface.tsx` into composition and focused panes when the new language surface is connected; do not add another mode to the current component. The runtime owns the typed study-presentation projection. Desktop owns camera-aware rendering, annotation layout, selection, source navigation, and the resizable top/bottom preview composition; it never infers a load, unit, direction, activation, or target from source text or display labels. The agent harness consumes a generated bounded language/context artifact plus structured checker, planner, and runner results. Its FEA tools are organized around source read/edit, check, plan, run, cancel, and result inspection. Delete broad mutation schemas that duplicate declaration fields. The Server remains unchanged except for generic encrypted artifact/workload versions if required. It receives no FEA parser, AP242 decoder, operation catalog, or plaintext schema.

The dependency edits are deliberately small and auditable: | Manifest | Change | | --- | --- | | workspace `Cargo.toml` | Add `crates/runmat-analysis/language` as a member and workspace dependency. | | `runmat-analysis/language/Cargo.toml` | Depend on parser, analysis-core, geometry-core, `runmat-types`, `serde`, and `thiserror`; never builtins, value, runtime, execution, OCCT, CLI, or LSP. | | `runmat-analysis/core/Cargo.toml` | No parser, lexer, builtins, value, or language dependency. | | `runmat-geometry/io/Cargo.toml` | Add geometry-ops for provider-contract implementation; keep native OCCT dependencies target/feature gated. | | `runmat-runtime/Cargo.toml` | Add analysis-language and compose its neutral extension with the standard builtin catalog. | | `runmat-lsp/Cargo.toml` | Add analysis-language and analysis-core directly; use the same explicit catalog composition and fingerprint as runtime. | | CLI/native/Desktop | No parser or analysis-language dependency unless the host is the direct compiler-service owner; ordinary clients use public runtime/LSP/execution facades. | The language crate exposes a narrow facade rather than its modules: `FeaCompilerHost` is a composition of the narrow source/catalog traits; implementations may be partial for editor operation. Parsed, checked, and lowered products are immutable and distinct, so callers cannot accidentally execute a syntax tree or skip semantic validation. Public types do not expose pass contexts, mutable symbol tables, parser cursors, or host implementations.
Input is one source file and a source id. Output is a lossless syntax module plus diagnostics. Parsing never loads another file. Syntax validity and formatter stability are independently testable.

The compiler requests imported symbols through `FeaModuleSource`, canonicalizes logical paths, checks source-root confinement, detects cycles, and retains content digests and source spans. Imports select one declared symbol; there are no wildcard or ambient-path imports.

Binding creates distinct namespaces for declaration kinds and lexical scopes for model/study members. It detects duplicates, ambiguity, invalid qualification, inaccessible symbols, and composition conflicts. It does not yet evaluate geometry or lower physics.

Semantic checking resolves input types, dimensioned literals, immutable expressions, declaration references, region roles, field/history types, and operation overloads. Requiredness is evaluated after the selected procedure/model/geometry is known; optional syntax does not create empty default objects.

Each geometry declaration becomes exactly one `GeometryDefinition` variant. File imports retain logical source identity. Feature graphs retain stable feature paths. Derivations bind source revision plus changes. Generated declarations bind frozen-function requirements, never a live callable. Geometry inspection resolves source parameters/properties/regions into typed candidates. It does not execute expensive construction during `check` unless required metadata is already available; `plan` materializes or schedules the minimum work necessary to prove topology-dependent facts.
