Materials, assignments, constraints, boundaries, connectors, interfaces, signals, excitations, initial conditions, and domains lower into existing analysis-core contracts. Imported engineering properties must pass through one explicit candidate-to-material conversion. Model composition uses stable typed identity and emits no override order.

The compiler binds model parameters and typed regions to one geometry, verifies mesh lineage, constructs the semantic procedure/state graph, validates accuracy and retained state, then lowers sweep axes/cases over declared study inputs. Scheduler tasks are not constructed here.

Operation resolution has already selected a stable overload id. Lowering converts it to typed observation requests and expression nodes. `max(field, over = region)` produces an attributed spatial-extremum contract; no FEA evaluator sees the text `"max"`. Cost and distributability facts enter planning before solve.

The compiler validates only source-authored policy. The runtime later merges it with project and CLI policy through a typed precedence function. The merged policy may change placement/resources, not physical meaning or accuracy. Its logical and attempt identities remain separate from the study-definition identity.

check parse + bind + type/unit check + import/callable signature resolution + available geometry/AP242 capability inspection - no user function execution - no solver or cluster allocation plan check + canonical materialization/mesh/study/observation/resource graphs + provider/capability admission - no claim that generated values or numerical results exist run plan + bounded materialization + geometry + mesh + solve + observation + canonical publication and evidence An editor may run partial `check` with unavailable external facts and report them distinctly from syntax/type errors. CLI/release checking requires complete facts for every selected runnable root.

- Source identity: logical module path plus exact source digest. - Authored declaration identity: bound symbol path plus canonical typed content. - Generator identity: imported function source graph, captures, arguments, and policy. - Geometry-definition identity: source/feature graph/derivation and typed inputs. - Geometry-realization identity: definition plus kernel/profile cohort and exact result digest. - Region identity: geometry revision plus selector/feature-output path and selected persistent ids. - Mesh identity: exact geometry realization plus meshing request/cohort/result. - Study-definition identity: realized physical inputs, geometry/mesh, model, semantic procedures, accuracy, and result-affecting observations. - Logical execution identity: study-definition identity plus admitted logical task/partition plan. - Attempt identity: placement, workers, devices, retries, timing, transfers, and physical chunks. The compiler computes only identities whose inputs exist at its stage. Later realization extends identity; it never rewrites an earlier digest to pretend generated content was already known.

One diagnostic envelope crosses lexer, parser, semantic, geometry, and host boundaries: - stable code and severity; - primary source span and source id; - typed related spans across imported `.fea` or `.m` files; - declaration/symbol/operation identity when known; - concise message and structured facts; - optional safe fix/code action; - phase and completeness (`syntax`, `binding`, `semantic`, `inspection`, `planning`); and - no embedded runtime or provider error string as the sole diagnostic. Kernel, AP242, callable, and execution errors are adapted once at their owner boundary while retaining source attribution. LSP, CLI, Desktop, and JSON output render the same structured facts.

- lexer tokens, trivia, invalid bytes, and recovery; - parser declarations, precedence, incomplete files, diagnostics, and format idempotence; - module resolution, cycle/traversal rejection, symbol namespaces, and composition; - type/unit inference and invalid operation overloads; - every output operation descriptor, result type, lowering, tie rule, and docs entry; - geometry feature-graph validation, identity, resource bounds, and invalidation; - persistent topology under split/merge/delete and ambiguous feature history; - AP242 capability inventory, parameter units/types, property contexts, material candidates, persistent ids, unsupported profiles, and lossy-export reports; - candidate-to-material conversion, coverage, and conflict rejection.

Use small fixtures that cross one real seam rather than giant all-purpose fixtures: tests/fea_language/ syntax/ modules/ geometry/ ap242/ materials/ studies/ sweeps/ outputs/ execution/ diagnostics/ migration/ Each fixture has source, expected diagnostics or resolved summary, and only when applicable a canonical result/evidence expectation. During development, internal parity fixtures compare the new resolved semantics with the canonical implementation; they do not expose or preserve the old format, and they are removed with the old loader once the hard cutover is proved.

Verify completion, hover, signature help, definition, references, rename, formatting, semantic tokens, and diagnostics for complete and incomplete `.fea` files. Cross-language tests navigate from `import function impactPulse from "./impactPulse.m"` to the `.m` definition and report a signature/effect mismatch at the import/call site.

- one minimal local study with no sweep/execution declaration; - one parameterized constructed-geometry study; - one immutable derived-geometry sweep; - one `.m`-generated geometry study; - AP242 read-only parameter/material import fixture; - AP242 qualified regeneration fixture where the supported kernel/profile exists; - local versus encrypted remote identity/result equivalence; - independent fanout versus cooperative-distribution evidence; - bounded field paging and attributed reduction without full gather; and - docs parsing/type-checking plus runnable STEP-backed guides. These extend existing release jobs without renaming their topology and without a nightly lane.

Add source-level architecture checks for: - no `serde_yaml` or YAML document types in the final runtime FEA load path; - no FEA parser/AST imports in numerical, execution-worker, or geometry-kernel modules; - no runtime/CLI/LSP dependencies from analysis core or geometry crates; - no `runmat-builtins` or `runmat-value` dependency from analysis core or analysis-language; - no AP242 raw entity types outside geometry I/O; - no operation-name string matching after semantic resolution; - no direct OCCT types outside geometry I/O provider modules; - no new FEA cases in the existing runtime/LSP god files; - no new production file containing syntax + semantics + execution responsibilities; - no `allow` suppression or `v2` naming added by the migration; and - generated language/operation documentation matches the canonical registries. Review additionally checks that every new module has one named owner, one direction of translation, and no second cache/identity/validation authority.
The slices are deliberately large enough to deliver coherent vertical behavior, but each ends at a real ownership or evidence boundary.

- Create the code-derived current/target surface ledger. - Extract dependency-neutral operation facts into `runmat-types`; add source-host traits, the read-only analysis catalog view, and deterministic catalog composition/fingerprint checks. - Establish architecture checks preventing additions to the known concentration points. - Surface-ledger and catalog-boundary work preserves admitted loader semantics until the atomic public cutover.

- Implement FEA lexer, lossless syntax tree, parser recovery, and formatter. - Add syntax diagnostics and parser/formatter fixtures for the complete grammar. - The syntax frontend owns neither domain lowering nor independent public-loader authority.

- Implement module graph, explicit imports, symbols, types, units, requiredness, and diagnostics. - Lower materials/models/studies/sequences/sweeps/execution into existing typed contracts. - Implement direct `.m` symbol facts without executing functions.

- Extend the canonical catalog and register FEA overloads. - Implement attributed result types and lower existing observation/reduction contracts. - Complete LSP/catalog/reference integration and distributed reduction evidence.

- Add normalized geometry source/feature/lineage contracts and provider-neutral planning. - Implement the bounded OCCT feature provider and persistent history. - The qualified bounded native profile must cover primitives, affine transforms/instances, extrusion, revolution, governed Booleans, holes, pockets, fillets, and chamfers. Removal operations reject zero-volume overlap; edge treatments resolve typed selectors before dispatch; and final history uses a private canonical shape-table join while public persistent ids remain digest-based. Source regeneration remains part of the capability-inventoried AP242 slice rather than a generic kernel operation. - Add canonical geometry materialization tasks and local/remote publication. Required implementation: a dedicated portable workload owns constructed/imported/derived request closure, exact provider admission, bounded resources, deterministic scheduler identity, immutable exact result closure, remote routing, replay-safe checkpoints, and typed region/history receipt. - Execute `.m` geometry through the shared portable callable foundation. The generator admission binds the exact program revision, named callable/source/function, complete static signature, permitted effects/capabilities, ordered SI arguments, and immutable `geometry.Generated` output. The returned provider-neutral feature product is content-addressed behind a self-authenticating receipt, then realized through the same exact provider workload as constructed geometry. Scoped artifact references remain transport data and never enter study-definition identity. Runtime builder, immutable-value codec, metadata, and WASM registration are separate focused modules. - Qualify constructed, derived, generated, and geometry-sweep paths. A study owns a typed geometry instance whose named arguments are constants or exact study-input references. Case realization freezes those arguments into canonical SI `GeometryAuthoringValue` bindings before portable request construction. Qualification must prove equal-case determinism, changed-case geometry and mesh-stage invalidation, reuse of the identical derived-source closure, distinct independently schedulable task identities, and fail-closed missing/unknown/type-incompatible bindings.

- Inventory current XCAF translation and raw AP242 surface. - Add parameters, properties, materials, associations, persistent ids, capabilities, and fixtures. - Add explicit typed material adoption and read-only parameter use. - Add qualified regeneration/change-set/export paths only for proven profiles. Required ownership: geometry I/O owns a bounded Part 21 decoder, SI/derived-unit normalization, exact capability profiling, CAx-IF stock-material/property/callout/specification/ environment graph extraction, the standard legacy designation alternate, and source-attributed unsupported evidence. Geometry core owns normalized exchange, change-set, and truthful export report contracts. The language resolves readable CAD parameters into provenance-bearing typed constants and explicitly adopts physical CAD properties into analysis-owned provenance; typed environment requirements reuse the ordinary expression/unit checker. Exact workers re-inspect AP242 bytes and compare the complete normalized inventory before materialization. Writes and regeneration require qualified writer and evaluator profiles; otherwise they fail closed and a validated change set truthfully reports sidecar-only disposition rather than claiming a STEP round trip.

- Route runtime, CLI, LSP, and Desktop through the new compiler. - Migrate examples and compare resolved semantics/results across implemented procedures. - Publish language/reference/guides and make docs executable in release. - Delete YAML loading, duplicate schema/default/template logic, and dead compatibility code. - Split touched runtime/LSP/Desktop concentration points and verify no net replacement god file. No slice is complete with duplicated old/new production authority. The new path may be exercised directly from tests while unfinished, but there is no public feature flag, compatibility mode, or conversion surface; the public cutover is atomic.

- Every current field and behavior has a reviewed surface-ledger disposition. - Lexer/parser own syntax; analysis-language owns compiler passes; analysis-core owns authored contracts; geometry core/ops/io own normalized contracts, pure planning and provider translation; execution adapts generic tasks; runtime/LSP/CLI/Desktop own their host and presentation roles. - One parser/lowering path produces the existing canonical typed analysis contracts. - One operation catalog drives `.m`, `.fea`, LSP, lowering, and reference documentation. - All four geometry source forms produce one immutable canonical geometry artifact contract. - AP242 capability, parameter, property, regeneration, and round-trip claims are profile-specific and evidence-backed. - Runtime, numerical kernels, workers, Desktop, and Server contain no duplicate language/schema implementation. - Runtime analysis/document/figure coordinators, LSP analysis and Desktop study composition do not grow into mixed-responsibility files; touched concentrations are reduced or split. - Old YAML production loading and dead authoring contracts are removed. - Focused, cross-layer, local/remote, documentation, architecture, lint, and release gates pass.

Compiler modules own one named responsibility and direction of translation. Production modules normally remain below roughly 600 lines and orchestration facades below roughly 250; review must split a concentration of responsibilities rather than arbitrarily fragment one owner. Existing runtime analysis coordinator, LSP analysis coordinator, document loader, figure renderer and Desktop study surface must not grow to absorb parser, semantic, geometry, physics or query behavior. Facades retain declarations, re-exports and small coordination only. Language loading has one compiler and no YAML authority. Figures render selected typed values and never decide recovery. Desktop splits composition, editor, diagnostics, plan, geometry, execution and result views.

dependencies: Shared physical contracts, numerical qualification, resources, identity, accuracy and release acceptance remain independently mandatory.

requirements.title: Typed declarative authoring and explicit composition
requirements.acceptance: Typed declarative authoring and explicit composition requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: The target authoring surface is the purpose-built declarative language specified in the canonical typed declarative language contract, not YAML deserialization into execution contracts. The `.fea` extension selects the language. Files have no repeated version/kind preamble and may declare multiple peer models, studies, sweeps, geometries, meshes, materials, and execution policies. Nesting follows domain ownership and lifetime: a `geometry` declaration owns typed region selectors resolved against one exact admitted geometry revision and its imported names, tags, and persistent entity ids; a `model` owns reusable physical intent: inputs (including typed region inputs), region references, materials and assignments, constraints, natural boundaries, connectors, interfaces, signals, excitations, load cases, initial conditions, spectra, and family domains; a `study` binds a model instance to exact geometry and mesh and owns its semantic procedure graph, accuracy requirements, retained states, and requested outputs; a `sweep` owns named cases over declared study inputs; and an `execution` declaration owns optional placement, resource, fanout, cooperative-distribution, accelerator, and resilience preferences. Requiredness is semantic and minimal. A basic local study does not need `sweep`, `execution`, GPU, cluster, retry, or explicit output declarations. Physics-specific validation requires only the material capabilities, geometry/mesh roles, constraints, excitations, states, and numerical choices needed by the selected procedures. No empty scale-oriented boilerplate is required.

Composition uses explicit source-resolvable imports and named declarations, for example `import model bracket from "./models/bracket.fea"`. Equal definitions deduplicate by typed stable identity; conflicts fail with both source locations. There is no last-writer-wins override order, hidden template/default expansion, or Rust-side builtin that manufactures physical objects. Geometry-bound selectors resolve only after a study binds exact geometry identity and revision. RunMat generators use explicit function imports such as `import function impactPulse from "./impactPulse.m"`. Package folders are supported when projects use them but are not required by the FEA language or its examples. The imported file must expose a compatible named function; scripts and ambient-workspace behavior are rejected. The callable is resolved through the ordinary project graph and materialized into a canonical artifact before any solver runs. Before parser replacement, implementation must inventory the true current study/configuration surface across document types, core authored contracts, runtime/CLI/Desktop adapters, canonical identity, execution, results, persistence, and evidence. Every current item receives an explicit disposition: authored DSL, compiler-derived, optional project/execution policy, internal-only, removed with rationale, or unresolved gap. The inventory records cardinality, current default, target syntax/type owner, identity effect, validation, and coverage. Migration fixtures compare the resolved semantic contracts and results, not merely source spelling. No field survives only because the old YAML exposed it, and no behavior disappears merely because it was undocumented.

The migration is a clean cut with one FEA lexer/parser/semantic lowering path. There is no YAML conversion command or compatibility tooling: the product has not shipped this authoring format, so the old implementation is only an internal inventory/parity source while the replacement is built. No dual YAML/DSL authority, compatibility switch, duplicate canonicalization, or dead schema remains. Verification covers multi-declaration files, imports, composition, cycles/traversal, diagnostics, minimal requiredness, geometry revisions, function provenance, local/remote identity, and the absence of implicit physical content.

requirements.title: Immutable exact geometry and truthful engineering exchange
requirements.acceptance: Immutable exact geometry and truthful engineering exchange requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: The `.fea` language supports four closed geometry source forms that all lower to the existing canonical exact-geometry contract: imported STEP/IGES/BREP or another admitted file/artifact; a bounded declarative typed feature graph; an immutable derived revision of another geometry; or a materialized typed geometry result from an explicitly imported `.m` function. There is no in-place geometry mutation. Construction and derivation form immutable dependency graphs with typed dimensioned inputs, exact result identity, kernel-capability cohort, validation, and source/result lineage. Geometry-changing sweep inputs are explicitly bound by a study's named geometry instance and materialize to canonical SI values before worker submission. They invalidate the geometry, mesh, projection, operator, and result layers while allowing unaffected content-addressed ancestors to remain cached. Equal case bindings must reproduce the same exact result root; distinct bindings must seed distinct canonical meshing-stage identities. Missing, duplicate, unknown, or dimensionally incompatible geometry arguments fail before execution. Adaptive remeshing changes discretization, not geometry; nonlinear deformation, ALE motion, and contact configuration remain analysis state rather than authored CAD revisions. The first production feature set is intentionally bounded to qualified primitives, transforms, instances, extrude/revolve, booleans, holes/pockets, and supported fillet/chamfer operations. Each operation is strongly typed and registry-backed. Arbitrary kernel commands, free-form string opcodes, and heuristic healing are not escape hatches. Sketch constraints, mating, advanced surfaces, and broader CAD behavior are admitted only with exact semantics and verification.

The bounded native provider must qualify that entire set through the same exact-import boundary. Profile sweeps retain complete source lineage; removal features prove positive target/tool volume overlap and reject no-op cuts; and local edge treatments receive only provider-neutral selections already checked for target membership and authored cardinality. Internal kernel history may join to the reimported final B-rep through its canonical private shape-table key, but public topology identity remains digest-based and occurrence-qualified. Kernel ordinals never enter authored, mesh, analysis, or cache identity. Persistent topology is part of correctness. Every feature operation records stable feature identity, a complete final entity inventory, introduced entities, and canonical typed source-to-final-descendant lineage. The provider composes its kernel's generated, modified, unchanged, and deleted evidence through post-processing before publication; downstream feature execution composes those relations again and intersects them with the declaration's final exact topology. Regions may select semantic feature outputs such as an introduced boundary, but never a face-vector ordinal. Splits, merges, extinguished entities, role changes, and cardinality changes are checked against the authored selector and fail when ambiguous. Missing history never falls back to geometric proximity. The resulting persistent entities flow through the existing geometry-to-mesh provenance so assignments, constraints, interfaces, and observations retain exact ownership.

RunMat-generated geometry follows the same frozen-callable boundary as generated signals. The function returns a typed geometry asset/builder result and declared region outputs; bounded preprocessing validates effects, units, exact topology, region outputs, and resources, then publishes a canonical geometry artifact. Meshing and solvers never call live `.m` code. STEP AP242 admission is profile- and capability-specific. ISO 10303-242:2025 includes parametric and constrained geometry, sketches, manufacturing features, part properties, composites, and material specifications/properties, but a concrete export may contain only flattened B-rep or a subset. Admission inventories actual edition/profile, persistent ids, parameters, constraints, features, PMI, user attributes, product/assembly ownership, materials, property sets, validation properties, and supported read/write/regeneration capabilities. `AP242` is not one capability boolean. Imported parameters resolve from source names or persistent ids into typed references carrying dimension, units, value, ownership, constraints/bounds, source provenance, and access capability. They are readable in expressions. Updating one creates a derived geometry and is accepted only when the imported representation is genuinely regenerative and RunMat has a qualified evaluator for its complete dependency/constraint graph. A nominal dimension annotation on flattened B-rep remains read-only metadata.

Imported engineering properties are typed provenance-bearing candidates, never implicit FEA laws. Users explicitly adopt the desired density, elastic, thermal, electrical, magnetic, acoustic, fluid, composite, or other supported capabilities and state required operating environment and conflict policy. Units, specification references, associations, uncertainty or validation facts, and conversion evidence are retained. Visual materials never become physical materials. CAD material associations may define selectable geometry domains, but the typed FEA assignment remains explicit. The normalized material graph follows CAx-IF recommended practice rather than assuming that every material is a `MATERIAL_DESIGNATION`: categorized stock-material products own product definitions and typed properties, `MAKE_FROM_USAGE_OPTION` carries the part callout, `APPLIED_DOCUMENT_REFERENCE` carries specifications, and typed `DATA_ENVIRONMENT.elements` carry property conditions. Legacy material designations remain discoverable as an explicit alternate. Malformed or only partially readable facts are retained as source-attributed unsupported evidence and cannot be silently dropped from a partially successful profile. Round-trip work retains the immutable source and produces a typed change set plus export report. Qualified AP242 export preserves or updates supported persistent ids, parameters, properties, associations, and validation properties. Unsupported/lossy content is reported; a newly written STEP file is not described as a lossless round trip without evidence. Implementation follows the applicable AP242 edition and CAx-IF/MBx-IF Recommended Practices and is fixture-tested across producing CAD systems.

requirements.title: Complete authoring surface and one compiler authority
requirements.acceptance: Complete authoring surface and one compiler authority requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: Complete source-authoring admission is required before a family is promoted to production or a public `.fea` example is treated as canonical. Existing verified numerical work remains valid while this stage is open, but the current YAML authoring form is not the target public interface. The concrete code layout, dependency direction, pass products, host traits, extraction/deletion points, test layout, and anti-god-file rules for this stage are fixed in the canonical compiler boundary and pass-product contract. Source-authoring implementation must update that blueprint deliberately when code evidence requires a boundary change; it must not silently drift into a different architecture. Build the current-to-target surface ledger from code, not documentation alone. Inventory every accepted document field/variant, core authored field, runtime/CLI/Desktop constructor field, canonical identity input, worker input, result/persistence field, implicit default, expansion, compatibility path, and unused field. Give each item one reviewed disposition: authored DSL, compiler-derived, optional project/execution policy, internal-only, removed with rationale/replacement, or unresolved gap. Record cardinality, current default, target syntax and typed owner, identity effect, validation, and positive/negative coverage. Resolve every gap against the planned family, constraint, assignment, excitation, sequence, sweep, observation, accuracy, scaling, GPU, restart, and result-access surfaces. Do not freeze a grammar that needs an untyped escape hatch for a planned production capability.

Freeze the source grammar, declaration ownership, name resolution, import semantics, units and expression subset, semantic types, diagnostics, and canonical formatting described in the canonical typed declarative language contract. Keep `.fea` version-free; a future incompatible edition belongs once in project configuration. Implement a separate FEA lexer/parser/AST using the existing RunMat lexer/parser foundations and put semantic checking/lowering in the narrow `runmat-analysis-language` crate. This keeps source dependencies out of analysis core and numerical consumers while letting runtime and LSP share one compiler. Do not contaminate the MATLAB grammar/HIR or add any further crate without another proven dependency boundary. Implement explicit symbol/file imports, including the simple production form `import function impactPulse from "./impactPulse.m"`, cross-language signature/effect checking, project-graph provenance, and go-to-definition/reference/rename support. Extend the existing canonical operation catalog with strongly typed FEA field/history/case overloads and lowering bindings. Use ordinary identities such as `max` where semantics agree; retain attributed extremum results; drive LSP and reference docs from the same descriptors; and do not create an analysis-private builtin set. Implement imported, constructed, derived, and `.m`-generated geometry over one immutable canonical artifact contract. Add feature-history persistent topology, typed region outputs, geometry-parameter sweep invalidation, and fail-closed ambiguity/cardinality behavior.

Add capability-inventoried STEP AP242 parameters, constraints/features, persistent ids, material/property candidates, explicit typed property adoption, qualified regeneration, and truthful export/change-set evidence. Do not equate an AP242 header with full capability. Implement model composition, parameter binding, study graphs, sweeps, typed outputs, and optional execution policies. A minimal local study must not declare a sweep, execution policy, cluster, GPU, retry policy, or unnecessary output block. Lower into the existing canonical typed contracts. Keep study-definition, logical-execution, and physical-attempt identity separate; reuse generic placement, artifacts, scheduler, distributed values, accelerators, retries, and publication rather than adding FEA-private infrastructure. Migrate checked-in studies, runtime construction, CLI/Desktop adapters, examples, and docs. Prefer STEP geometry in examples where exact CAD is part of the workflow. During implementation, compare representative target-language sources with the current implementation at the resolved-contract and result levels across every implemented family/procedure. Review every delta as either an intended correction or a defect. These are internal parity fixtures, not a supported old-format reader. Add negative fixtures for behavior that was formerly hidden, ambiguous, or invalid. Remove the production YAML parser, schema, compatibility switches, duplicate lowering, obsolete defaults/templates, dead tests, and any temporary parity harness that depends on the retired loader. Do not retain a standalone conversion tool.

Publish the complete `docs/simulation/language/` reference and guides defined in the canonical typed declarative language contract; parse and type-check every code block and execute runnable guides in the existing release workflow without renaming its jobs or adding a nightly lane. Complete a final language-surface review before treating `.fea` as stable. Review every declaration, label, reference form, nesting rule, required field, optional field, unit-bearing value, and diagnostic for consistency and directness. Remove accidental synonyms, opaque lifecycle verbs, redundant nesting, context-dependent meanings, and fields that merely expose compiler or execution internals. Update the surface ledger, grammar, formatter, examples, LSP, and reference together; no compatibility spelling is retained. Replace the initial language pages with a deliberate documentation set modeled on proven configuration-language documentation: begin with the purpose and object model, show a minimal checked study, introduce blocks/arguments/references/types/units in that context, then separate task-oriented guides from exhaustive reference. Every declaration reference states its parent, labels, fields, types and units, requiredness, defaults, mutual exclusions, result, diagnostics, and a complete example. Add corresponding `.fea` workflows beside `.m` workflows throughout the public FEA documentation wherever both authoring surfaces apply. Avoid slogans, filler conclusions, anthropomorphism, and other formulaic generated prose.

Publish a canonical runtime study-presentation projection for Desktop. It resolves every constraint, prescribed value, boundary condition, connector, interface, initial condition, load, excitation, and function-backed signal to exact geometry/topology targets and supplies typed quantity, units, frame, direction, distribution, schedule/function identity, activation, and source spans. This is a presentation projection of the checked study, not a second parser, physics model, or TypeScript interpretation of `.fea`. Implement `.fea` source and preview modes in Desktop. Source mode uses the shared LSP for highlighting, diagnostics, completion, hover, units, references, rename, formatting, and cross-file `.m` navigation. Preview mode initially divides the pane equally top-to-bottom: the upper pane renders geometry with the canonical study overlays, and the lower pane renders a study outline with typed details. The lower pane favors a navigable hierarchy and relationship details over a software-oriented node-link graph, shows quantities with units and source navigation, and offers compact toolbar toggles for inactive declarations and applicable but unset options. The divider may be resized without changing the initial 50/50 layout. Make file authoring the primary FEA agent workflow. Generate or inject a bounded canonical `.fea` language guide, current procedure/operation facts, relevant project symbols, and exact `check`/`plan`/`run` commands into FEA-mode context. The agent edits source, runs the checker, repairs source diagnostics, plans, and runs. Retire schema-sized typed mutation tools and any prompt-local language copy; retain only focused read/inspect/run tools whose contracts remain smaller and more stable than the language.

The surface ledger has no unexplained field, default, implicit behavior, or unresolved gap for the planned public production surface. The grammar, formatter, parser recovery, semantic typing, dimensional analysis, modules/imports, model composition, inputs, sweeps, outputs, and optional execution policy pass focused and adversarial tests. Cross-language `.m` imports have source navigation, typed signature/effect validation, frozen provenance, deterministic materialization, and local/remote equivalence. Imported, constructed, derived, and generated geometry share exact immutable identity, feature/entity lineage, region resolution, meshing, cache, remote execution, and evidence; AP242 parameter/property capability and round-trip claims are fixture-qualified by profile. Output operations resolve through the canonical RunMat catalog, have static quantity/unit/shape/ location signatures and attributed results, and drive completion, hover, signature help, diagnostics, execution lowering, and reference documentation without duplicate inventories. Minimal local studies contain no scale boilerplate; studies using sweeps, cluster fanout, cooperative distributed solves, or accelerators opt into only the declarations they need. Every migrated representative study preserves or intentionally corrects its typed semantic contract, study-definition identity, and verified result. Differences have reviewed evidence. The same resolved study runs through local and cluster placement without changing study-definition identity, and execution evidence truthfully distinguishes fanout from cooperative distribution. There is one production parser and lowering path, no hidden model template/default expansion, and no obsolete YAML or string-dispatched solver authority.

A reviewed language-surface ledger has no inconsistent naming, accidental synonym, opaque lifecycle command, redundant nesting, or implementation-owned field exposed as user intent. The language documentation provides a useful first-study path, concept pages, task guides, and exhaustive declaration reference; `.fea` and `.m` examples appear together wherever both are valid authoring routes. All code is checked in CI/release against STEP-backed runnable examples. Desktop source mode is backed by the shared LSP. Preview mode renders the exact checked geometry and study, and its study outline communicates models, assignments, procedures, inputs, outputs, units, activation, and available options without requiring software-graph terminology. Every supported geometry-targeted study declaration has a clean visual representation. Vector quantities use directed glyphs and magnitude/unit labels; distributed quantities distinguish their scope; function-backed inputs show a code/function marker and symbol; colors distinguish declaration roles; selections and source navigation are bidirectional; and zoom-dependent levels of detail reduce labels, then aggregate glyphs, without losing target identity. FEA-mode agent context is derived from the canonical language/catalog authorities and leads the model through edit, check, plan, and run. No duplicate prompt schema or broad typed mutation API remains.

requirements.title: Domain boundaries and shared platform interoperability
requirements.acceptance: Domain boundaries and shared platform interoperability requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: Meshing owns geometric and physical topology. It does not own materials, constitutive laws, loads, boundary conditions, or physics behavior. RunMat's general numerical, signal-processing, control-system, data, callable, and accelerator facilities own general-purpose signal construction and execution. FEA consumes their typed outputs and does not fork those libraries. `runmat-analysis-core` owns solver-neutral authored problem, procedure-sequence, state-transition intent, observation, accuracy, and validation contracts. `runmat-analysis-fea` owns analysis-mesh projection, transition realization, constraint compilation and enforcement, discretizations, assembly, solvers, recovery, observation evaluation, accuracy evidence, coupled iteration, adaptation, and analysis execution contracts. `runmat-runtime` owns public operation adaptation, document handling, runtime composition, result persistence, queries, and plotting integration. It does not own physics kernels. `runmat-execution-runner-native` owns native process, durable, and remote host adapters. Numerical code must not depend on it. The CLI and Desktop choose execution placement and present lifecycle state. They do not implement physics. The Server remains content-blind. It stores and routes encrypted artifacts and generic execution state without learning FEA schemas or plaintext model contents.

Do not add god files. A module that combines contracts, topology, assembly, solution, recovery, and diagnostics must be split before it grows further. Do not duplicate a rule at multiple boundaries. Region resolution, quadrature, material lookup, field topology, and identity derivation each have one owner. Strings may identify authored data such as names and IDs, but must not encode constraint kinds, DOFs, coordinate frames, enforcement methods, physics families, signal domains, excitation kinds, response measures, combination methods, or other closed domain choices after document parsing. Do not retain obsolete implementations behind compatibility switches. The FEA API is breaking; make clean replacements and remove dead paths. Do not introduce names containing `v2` to distinguish replacement types, fields, classes, or modules. Use the final domain name. This is a no-allow repository. Do not suppress warnings or retain unused code with `allow` attributes unless an exceptional, documented compiler boundary makes it unavoidable. Keep modules focused, testable, and named for the domain behavior they own. Name APIs, modules, diagnostics, and documentation for the exact concept they represent: FEA source, study or sweep definition, geometry, mesh, physical input, constraint, numerical field, solver result, execution placement, or evidence. Do not substitute a broad discipline label where a stable domain term exists; numeric exponent formatting is exponential notation. Every significant, measurable slice should be committed separately after its tests and relevant checks pass.

A deterministic output is not evidence of a correct formulation. A small algebraic residual is not enough when the assembled operator does not represent the stated equations. Moving completed arrays to a device is not GPU solver execution. Generated graphs, implicit channels, scalar profiles, extrema-based terminals, and global averages must not substitute for canonical topology in production analyses. Unsupported model combinations must fail explicitly rather than select a convenient fallback.

Keep analysis identity and numerical-object schemas in `runmat-analysis-fea`, but place their projection into generic artifacts, tasks, and host workloads in the narrow `runmat-analysis-execution` peer crate. This mirrors the proven meshing split and keeps the portable bridge reusable by native, remote, and browser hosts without moving it into any one host. Typed contract structure: runmat-analysis-core -> depends only on solver-neutral geometry/contracts runmat-execution + runmat-execution-artifact + runmat-execution-runner -> own portable task, resource, artifact, placement, worker-group, and scheduling contracts runmat-accelerate-api + runmat-accelerate -> own provider-neutral dense/sparse compute capabilities and concrete accelerator placement runmat-analysis-fea -> depends on runmat-analysis-core -> depends on canonical geometry and meshing contracts -> may depend on dependency-light generic execution contracts, but not execution artifacts -> depends on accelerator contracts, never on runtime value implementations runmat-analysis-execution -> depends on runmat-analysis-fea -> depends on generic execution, artifact, and runner contracts -> owns no physics, solver mathematics, storage backend, scheduler, or transport runmat-runtime -> depends on runmat-analysis-language, runmat-analysis-core, and runmat-analysis-fea -> adapts runtime values and operations to analysis APIs runmat-execution-runner-native -> depends on runtime, analysis contracts, and generic execution -> implements native, durable, and remote providers runmat-cli -> composes runtime and native execution providers

This lets us move runtime-owned acoustic, CFD, CHT, and FSI code into `runmat-analysis-fea` without a dependency cycle. Analysis execution identities and numerical-object schemas remain with the analysis domain; task construction and the portable host envelope live in `runmat-analysis-execution`; host-specific process and network behavior remains in `runmat-execution-runner-native`. The `.fea` frontend has a second real dependency boundary: Typed contract structure: runmat-analysis-language -> runmat-parser -> runmat-analysis-core -> runmat-geometry-core -> dependency-neutral operation facts in runmat-types runmat-analysis-core -X-> runmat-parser / runmat-lexer / runmat-builtins / runmat-value `runmat-analysis-language` alone owns module-loading interfaces, symbol binding, semantic checking, and lowering from FEA syntax into canonical analysis contracts. Without it, analysis core would depend backward on source syntax and every numerical consumer would inherit the parser, or runtime and LSP would each grow a competing compiler. The crate owns no physics, solver, scheduler, filesystem implementation, runtime values, OCCT implementation, or UI logic. This is the minimum extraction that preserves dependency direction; it is not a general DSL or analysis dumping ground.

Reuse means extending the existing generic substrate where the missing capability is genuinely cross-domain. FEA must not copy RunMat's placement planner, value transport, content-addressed artifacts, provider capability discovery, device residency, worker pools, retries, cancellation, or publication fencing. Conversely, solver internals must not depend on MATLAB-facing `SparseTensor` or runtime `Value` representations. Those types are language and transport boundaries, not the canonical live numerical operator. Do not create another crate merely to make a directory smaller. Revisit this decision only if one of these concrete conditions appears: a real dependency cycle cannot be removed through an interface or data contract; native-only execution dependencies would otherwise leak into WebAssembly builds; a worker ABI must be versioned and deployed independently of the analysis library; compile-time or binary-footprint measurements show a material release problem; or two components require genuinely independent ownership and release cadence. If one of those conditions is met, document the dependency graph and the smallest proposed extraction before adding the crate.

FEA development overlaps a broad RM-1064 runtime program. The implementation must move forward without either freezing on that work or recreating it. The integration policy is: Merge the current public `origin/dev` into the FEA branch before new implementation begins, resolving CI/release and native-runner overlaps by composing both products' requirements. The `origin/dev` CI and release workflow topology is authoritative: retain its job IDs, display names, matrices, dependencies, action versions, and existing steps. Do not rename jobs or create branch-specific variants. Layer FEA and meshing coverage into the matching existing lanes, adding a dedicated job only when its isolation or blocking release semantics genuinely require one. Record that merge as the FEA platform baseline. Do not cherry-pick or copy unfinished work from the separate `./runmat` checkout. Consume only owner-published design facts and public dev lineage; never inspect the separately owned active checkout. Build analysis-owned authored contracts, topology, constraints, canonical operators, serial CPU references, physics, and verification against narrow public platform interfaces; do not reach into runtime storage representation. Avoid speculative new execution gang, collective, distributed-value, accelerator-assignment, builtin-catalog, or live-value authorities. RM-1064 already owns those domains. At each Stage 1 or Stage 2 platform-facing slice, fetch and audit `origin/dev`. If the required RM-1064 authority has landed, merge it before implementing the adapter. If it has not landed, continue independent analysis work or implement only a narrow replaceable port against the current public contract.

Before remote, distributed, or GPU promotion, perform a mandatory convergence merge from the then-current `dev`, delete superseded compatibility ports, and prove there is one authority for every shared contract. Known incoming contracts that FEA should expect to consume include: the sole `runmat-value::Value` and typed dense, sparse, real, complex, logical, and integer storage model; dependency-light `runmat-types` numeric, storage, shape, residency, and execution facts; `GangHandle`, `SpmdTaskContext`, collective identity/sequence contracts, and gang generation fencing; distributed value handles, partition layouts, codistributors, and distributed-object lifetime; native and encrypted remote SPMD gang execution; typed accelerator providers, devices, allocation domains, features, requests, assignments, and metering; and compiler-bound provider requirements and GPU-aware worker assignment; provider-owned native device context/buffer export and the CUDA provider surface; and pointer-stable, copy-on-write, copy-accounted host buffers at the runtime boundary. The typed runtime storage model changes the runtime adapter, not the analysis operator owner. `runmat-runtime` converts public arrays and sparse values into analysis inputs and converts fields back using typed views and copy-accounted buffers. `runmat-analysis-fea` must not use a live MATLAB `Value` or MATLAB sparse object as its mathematical state or solver matrix. Where static numeric vocabulary is genuinely shared and dependency-safe, use `runmat-types` identities and facts instead of creating an FEA-specific spelling.

A direct pre-`dev` integration is acceptable only if the owning workstream publishes a green, stable checkpoint, confirms that its commit ancestry will be preserved when it reaches `dev`, and agrees on the shared contract surface. Otherwise FEA consumes the current dependency-neutral types, continues analysis-owned work, and merges the completed platform work through `dev`. Do not cherry-pick a hand-selected subset of the value, gang, collective, distributed, or accelerator commits: those slices have cross-cutting invariants and must arrive as one reviewed platform lineage.

FEA uses the RunMat type system directly where a type describes a platform-wide fact, and keeps analysis semantics in the analysis domain. This is a deliberate split: `runmat-analysis-core` may depend on the dependency-neutral `runmat-types` crate. `runmat-analysis-fea` may consume those types directly or through analysis-core. Neither analysis crate depends on `runmat-runtime` or `runmat-value`. The narrowly named interoperability adapters live in `runmat-runtime`, which already owns both the public value boundary and calls into analysis. They must not leak `Value`, COW policy, garbage collection, MATLAB layout behavior, or provider handles into authored models, assembly, operators, solvers, or physics. Interoperability must not imply mandatory copying. Runtime adapters borrow typed immutable views for synchronous admission, move uniquely owned host buffers into analysis-owned inputs when lifetimes permit, and adopt analysis-owned output buffers back into `runmat-value`. Shared or strided inputs use an explicit materialization path with copy accounting. Device-resident inputs remain device-resident only when the chosen provider can admit the buffer under the provider-neutral operator contract; otherwise the placement plan records an explicit transfer or rejects a no-fallback request. Distributed values preserve their distribution identity when it matches the solver partition, or pass through an explicit redistribution plan.

The compiler and runtime should therefore understand the public FEA surface through `ValueFact` and typed class identities, while the solver receives validated analysis types. This gives MATLAB code, AOT execution, remote execution, native extensions, and future language frontends one interoperable boundary without turning the numerical kernel into a dynamic-value interpreter.

The current public baseline and the in-flight RM-1064 platform work must be reconciled before creating any of these surfaces. RM-1064 already defines typed SPMD gangs, collective identities and sequencing, distributed values and codistributors, remote encrypted gang execution, typed accelerator inventories and assignments, and provider-bound execution capabilities. FEA consumes and, where necessary, narrowly extends those authorities; it does not create parallel worker-group, collective, distributed-value, or accelerator-allocation models. The expected existing-crate ownership after that convergence is: The exact generic execution filenames should follow the conventions already present when implemented. Their responsibilities are normative: `runmat-execution` owns portable resource, task, gang, collective, distributed-value, accelerator-assignment, and placement contracts; `runmat-execution-artifact` owns the generic analysis executable form and host-admission envelope, while analysis owns numerical artifact schemas; `runmat-execution-runner` owns deterministic scheduling, gang lifecycle, distributed-object lifetime, and collective coordination; `runmat-accelerate-api` owns provider-neutral sparse capabilities and opaque device handles; and `runmat-accelerate` implements supported providers, feasibility, cost, residency, and truthful fallback evidence.

The existing language-level collective path coordinates typed `ValuePayload` objects and may route through a coordinator. FEA must first measure it for numerical use. If high-frequency Krylov reductions or halo exchanges require a bulk or device-resident data plane, extend the same gang, epoch, identity, security, failure, and transport authorities with typed numerical buffer operations. Do not add a second gang or collective lifecycle merely to obtain faster payload movement. No generic crate may learn FEA physics, mesh-region meaning, element formulations, or field semantics.

This crate owns authored intent only. It must not contain element matrices, mesh indexing, scheduler tasks, runtime values, filesystem paths, or host execution details. The study model must separate: `PhysicsFamily`: structural, thermal, electromagnetic, acoustic, fluid, or coupled composition; `AnalysisProcedure`: static, modal extraction, prestressed modal extraction, eigenvalue buckling, transient response, harmonic response, prestressed harmonic response, modal response spectrum, random response, nonlinear, or adaptive; `SolutionSpace`: direct/full-order or modal-reduced where both are meaningful; `AnalysisSequence`: ordered, typed procedure steps and state-transition edges; formulation-specific options; typed observation and accuracy requests; and numerical backend policy. Execution placement is not authored physics and must not be part of the logical study specification.

There must not be both `pipeline` and `orchestration` implementations for the same family after migration. Move a family, update all callers and tests, and remove its old module in the same measurable slice. Shared topology must be physics-neutral where possible, but it may expose deliberate projections such as structural boundary integration data or finite-volume face metrics. Those projections belong here because they interpret a canonical mesh for analysis; they do not belong in meshing or runtime. Similarly named concepts must remain distinct: If code does not fit one of these definitions, resolve its owner before adding it. Do not solve ambiguity by copying it into both modules.

This crate is only the portable adapter between analysis-owned semantics and generic execution. It maps analysis numerical manifests to `LogicalObject`/`ValueRef` closures, maps typed analysis capabilities and resources to generic worker requirements, creates the `AnalysisWorkload` executable form and host envelope, and projects validated semantic graphs into generic task graphs. It must not implement physics, numerical methods, scheduling, persistence, encryption, transport, or native worker behavior.

`analysis/mod.rs` should become a small module declaration and re-export surface. Runtime operation functions should translate runtime-facing values into analysis contracts, invoke the analysis orchestrator or execution provider, and translate results back. They must not assemble matrices, generate physical fields, or perform coupling iterations. The current runtime-owned `solver_mesh_flow_topology.rs` disappears. Its correct replacement belongs under `runmat-analysis-fea/topology/flow`.

The existing generic driver, durable store, remote transport, worker pool, encryption, and supervisor stay shared. Analysis and meshing adapters translate domain workloads to the generic execution substrate. They must not fork their own schedulers or storage systems.

`execution_target.rs` owns the shared placement arguments used by `runmat run`, `runmat mesh`, and future domain entrypoints. Script arguments and FEA placement arguments must remain unambiguous under Clap parsing.

Desktop FEA orchestration consumes the shared execution lifecycle and maps it into UI sessions. No Desktop physics implementation is added. No FEA-specific Server module, database schema, plaintext request body, or result decoder is added.

Numeric class and domain; Reuse `runmat-types::NumericClass`, `NumericDomain`, and related facts. FEA validates the subset supported by each formulation and backend.. Shape, storage kind, layout, residency, aliasing, and mutation facts; Reuse `runmat-types` when describing public values, compiler facts, workload requirements, and adapter capabilities.. Live MATLAB values and dense/sparse COW buffers; `runmat-value`; accepted and produced by `runmat-runtime` adapters, never used as the analysis model or operator abstraction.. Physical dimensions, units, family DOFs, constraints, regions, frames, operators, and fields; `runmat-analysis-core` and `runmat-analysis-fea`; these are domain semantics, not generic runtime value facts.. Portable numerical artifacts; Analysis-owned typed schemas inside the generic execution artifact envelope. They declare numeric class, domain, shape, layout, partitioning, and checksums without serializing a live `Value`.. Device and distributed storage; Provider- and execution-owned handles selected from typed requirements; analysis owns the mathematical partition and operator semantics..

`topology/transfer_geometry.rs`; Geometry, identities, weights, and measures from which a transfer can be built; no field or coupling policy.. `excitation/`; Interpolation, kinematics, modal participation, response combination, and conservative realization of already admitted typed signals; no VM dispatch or project resolution.. `execution/excitation_materialization.rs`; Analysis-owned materialization task and artifact contracts; execution is delegated through generic program/execution authorities.. `physics/coupling/interface_transfer.rs`; Conservative exchange of physical quantities between already projected domains.. `adaptation/field_transfer.rs`; Transfer of solution and history fields between parent and adapted meshes.. `orchestration/adaptive_study.rs`; The solve/estimate/adapt lifecycle and its stopping decisions.. `execution/adaptive_graph.rs`; Encoding that lifecycle as schedulable, restartable execution tasks.. `orchestration/sequence.rs`; Semantic procedure ordering, state compatibility, activation, and transition decisions; no worker placement or transport.. `execution/graph.rs`; Encoding an already validated semantic sequence as schedulable tasks; no authority to invent physical state transitions.. Family `recovery.rs` modules; Mathematical recovery of that family's physical fields.. `results/observation/`; Evaluation of typed field, history, probe, reduction, and monitor requests over recovered or solver-available quantities.. `results/accuracy/`; Attribution and acceptance of numerical error evidence; no family formulation or solver implementation.. `results/`; Packaging, identity, provenance, and publication of fields and observations already recovered or evaluated by a family..

requirements.title: Canonical analysis topology and deterministic projections
requirements.acceptance: Canonical analysis topology and deterministic projections requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: The analysis projection is the central prerequisite for every family. It consumes a validated canonical `SolverMeshArtifact` and produces immutable, indexed analysis data.

Dense node-index mapping from canonical node IDs. Element index, canonical identity, order, node connectivity, region ownership, orientation, Jacobian data, volume, centroid, and characteristic length. Quadrature points, weights, shape functions, and gradients for each supported element/order. Boundary-face index, canonical identity, adjacent element, local face, orientation, outward normal, area, quadrature, and complete provenance. Physical-region inventories and exact material assignments. Authored load and boundary-condition bindings with zero, one, or multiple match diagnostics. Interface inventories with primary and secondary sides, ownership, orientation, conformity status, and transfer policy. Contact candidate pairs and the geometry needed by the contact implementation, without embedding contact constitutive behavior in the projection. Finite-volume cell-face incidence, owner and neighbour, oriented area vector, centroid distance, interpolation weight, non-orthogonality measure, skewness measure, and boundary ownership. Stable field-location definitions for nodes, elements, integration points, boundary faces, edges, and cells. Stable identities needed for h- and p-adaptation transfer.

Every element has exactly one supported physical-region/material resolution or a typed failure. Every applied boundary condition and load resolves to an allowed topological dimension. Boundary orientation agrees with adjacent element orientation. Interface sides cannot be silently empty, multiply owned, or self-paired. Conservation-oriented topology has reciprocal owner/neighbour relationships. Projection is deterministic and independent of execution placement. The projection is cacheable by canonical mesh digest plus analysis-projection policy digest.

Tet4 and Tet10 geometry and quadrature invariants. Boundary normals and integrated areas on analytic primitives. Multi-region and multi-material ownership. Pressure resultant and moment recovery. Body-force volume integration. Interface side resolution and invalid ambiguity cases. Finite-volume divergence theorem checks. Stable projection identity across serialization and execution shapes.

requirements.title: Element-complete typed constitutive ownership
requirements.acceptance: Element-complete typed constitutive ownership requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: Material declarations, material-domain assignments, section and layup definitions, property assignments, orientations, and boundary/interface laws are distinct authored concepts. They must not be collapsed into one generic property bag or inferred from declaration count. Meshing owns topology and persistent provenance; it does not own constitutive physics. Analysis core owns the portable typed assignment intent. FEA projection compiles that intent against the admitted discretization. Each formulation consumes only the compiled properties it understands.

The material target is a closed sum type with four formulation roles: `beam` selects material-bearing one-dimensional beam domains represented by admitted edges or explicit beam-element regions; `shell` selects material-bearing two-dimensional shell domains represented by admitted faces or explicit shell-element regions; `solid` selects three-dimensional continuum-solid domains represented by exact solid identities and their volume elements; and `cell` selects finite-volume cells for fluid and other cell-centered formulations. The same geometric dimension does not imply the same formulation role. A CAD face bounding a solid is a boundary target, not a shell material target. A solid region used by a structural or heat continuum is not automatically a CFD cell domain. Contact, cohesive, impedance, film, and coupled interface laws are interface or boundary properties, not materials. Point masses, springs, and connectors own their dedicated element or connector properties and do not masquerade as zero- dimensional material assignments. This distinction is also the answer to whether material may be assigned to a face or only to a solid. A face is a material-bearing target only when the admitted formulation creates shell, membrane, cohesive, or another explicitly supported surface element on that face. A face used only as the boundary of a three-dimensional continuum cannot receive a bulk material. An edge is material-bearing only for an admitted beam, truss, or other supported line formulation. A volume used by a Lagrangian finite-element continuum uses `solid`; a finite-volume control-volume domain uses `cell`. The author never selects topology dimension and leaves the solver to guess the role.

The four roles are therefore formulation roles rather than synonyms for raw CAD dimensions. They are sufficient for the planned production families when combined with dedicated boundary, interface, connector, and point-element contracts. New formulations may add a new closed role only when its constitutive ownership and coverage rules differ materially; they must not introduce a generic `face`, `edge`, or `element` escape hatch. Each role has two strongly typed scopes: `all` explicitly selects every compatible active domain in the bound geometry revision; and `region` selects one persistent entity or one authored semantic group resolved through exact geometry and mesh provenance. The RunMat API exposes these as `fea.PropertyRegionTarget.beam/shell/solid/cell(region)` and `allBeams/allShells/allSolids/allCells(geometry)`. A target retains geometry id and revision. `fea.materialAssignment` accepts only a typed target and typed `fea.Material`; raw region and material strings are not an alternate API. `.fea` uses the same closed variants, including scalar whole-domain targets such as `target: all_solids` and selected targets such as `target: { solid: { region: bracket_body } }`. Clean breaking changes are preferred over legacy aliases or string dispatch.

Every active material-bearing element must resolve to exactly one compatible material assignment or one composite constitutive owner before operator assembly. Homogeneous beam, shell, solid, and cell domains use one material assignment. A laminate or other explicitly supported composite definition owns the ordered constituent materials for the elements it covers and therefore replaces, rather than supplements, a homogeneous material assignment on those elements. This applies when the model declares one material as well as many. There is no sole-material fallback. Empty scopes, uncovered elements, overlap between whole-domain and selected scopes, overlap between semantic groups, simultaneous homogeneous and composite ownership, stale selectors, wrong topology roles, unknown materials, geometry-revision substitution, and assignments that select no active element are typed admission failures. A `Material` may carry mechanical, thermal, acoustic, electrical, magnetic, fluid, damping, plastic, and later anisotropic laws, but declaration does not claim that every law is present or valid. Each formulation states its required constitutive capabilities and validates them after assignment compilation. Coupled formulations may reuse one assignment when the assigned material contains every required law; otherwise they reject before assembly. They must not silently use unrelated defaults or average heterogeneous materials.

Material declarations are capability aggregates, not bags of mandatory defaults. Mechanical, thermal, acoustic, electrical, magnetic, fluid, damping, plastic, and anisotropic laws are optional typed capabilities. A material must declare at least one capability. Air does not acquire invented elastic and thermal laws merely so it can be parsed, and a structural material does not silently acquire conductivity. Each formulation declares the exact capability set it consumes; coupled formulations require the union. Missing capabilities fail before planning and unrelated declared capabilities do not enter that operator's numerical identity. Assignment provenance is separate from constitutive semantics. The numerical assignment identifies the selected material or composite definition. Optional importer claims, reconciliation decisions, and confidence belong to an audit record. Confidence never scales a coefficient or otherwise changes the equations. Numerical identity includes the resolved constitutive choice; audit identity also includes the evidence that justified it. Changing evidence without changing the choice cannot invalidate an operator-value cache, although it does produce a distinct realized-study provenance record. Assignment compilation has four explicit representations and no solver performs ad hoc region matching: the authored target contains a closed formulation role and an exact region/group selector; geometry admission resolves that selector to a canonical, occurrence-qualified membership set bound to geometry id and revision, retaining group provenance and rejecting ambiguity or an empty set; analysis projection intersects that set with compatible active elements and produces one canonical compiled property entry per element; and

formulation adapters borrow typed immutable views of those entries and materialize only the coefficient blocks that their operators consume. Named groups may contain multiple compatible entities and may span part occurrences. Exact entity selectors identify one occurrence. Source-topology names, importer ordinals, authored list order, hash buckets, or worker partition order are never used as compiled membership. Direct explicit element groups and geometry-derived groups resolve through the same canonical set contract. The compiled property map is element-complete and contains canonical element identity, formulation role, occurrence-qualified source geometry identity, constitutive owner, required-law identities, optional section/layup/orientation identities, and assignment attribution. It is independent of authored order and worker partition. Its semantic digest binds geometry id/revision, topology digest, canonical membership, constitutive choices, and operator-relevant property definitions. Audit evidence has a separate digest. The semantic digest enters realized-study, operator-value, checkpoint, and result identities. Remote workers receive the compiled map or its content-addressed chunks and revalidate geometry revision, topology digest, coverage, and constitutive capability before numerical work. Partition changes may change physical chunk manifests but never logical assignment identity.

Material coverage is necessary but not sufficient for beams, shells, composites, or anisotropy. These remain separate closed contracts: every beam element requires exactly one beam-section assignment carrying the supported section geometry and recovery locations; every isotropic shell requires exactly one shell-section assignment carrying thickness, reference surface, and transverse-shear treatment; every composite shell requires exactly one ordered laminate layup with typed ply material, thickness, angle, ply-order direction, reference surface, and transverse-shear treatment; anisotropic solid, shell, and beam materials require an explicit material-orientation assignment in a supported global, local, cylindrical, spherical, or geometry-derived frame; and contact, cohesive, connector, acoustic-impedance, thermal-contact, and coupled-interface laws use their dedicated typed assignments and coverage rules.

Explicit beam and shell elements may carry direct required section identities. Geometry-derived beam and shell generation will compile separate typed `BeamSectionAssignment` and `ShellSectionAssignment` scopes; it must not infer sections from material assignments. A direct element section reference and a scoped section assignment cannot both control the same element. The compiler rejects gaps, overlaps, incompatible section kinds, invalid layup orientation, and unused selected assignments. A homogeneous beam or shell composes exactly one material owner with exactly one compatible section owner. A laminate section is itself the constitutive owner and contains its ordered ply-material references, so a separate homogeneous material assignment on the same shell is an error. Property orientation is orthogonal to homogeneous material and section identity; ply angles are relative to the laminate reference orientation. Composition occurs only after material/composite, section, and orientation coverage validate independently.

Section definitions and assignments are distinct. Definitions carry physical geometry and constitutive choices; assignments carry typed coverage. Beam definitions initially support explicit general, rectangular, circular, and tubular sections with canonical area, inertia, torsion, shear, recovery, and reference-axis data. Homogeneous shell definitions carry thickness, an explicit reference surface, and transverse-shear treatment. Laminate definitions carry ordered plies, a typed direction for traversing them relative to the oriented surface normal, an explicit reference surface, and transverse-shear treatment. Linear through-thickness terms are integrated analytically, so neither definition exposes an unused integration-point count. Drilling stabilization is owned and identified by the shell formulation, never authored as a physical material or section coefficient. Raw `section_id` fields on geometry-derived elements are not an alternate scoped-assignment mechanism, and direct element references cannot be combined with a competing scoped assignment. Orientation is a separate closed contract with global, local Cartesian, cylindrical, spherical, and supported geometry-derived frames. Every frame is bound to exact geometry and has deterministic singularity and handedness rules. Isotropic formulations may omit orientation when it cannot affect the equations. Anisotropic materials and laminates require it. A beam reference axis used to build the element basis is not silently reused as material orientation unless an explicit orientation policy says so.

Qualification must include single- and multi-solid exact CAD, repeated part occurrences, semantic groups spanning multiple bodies, explicit and geometry-derived beams and shells, mixed-dimensional models, and finite-volume cells. Positive cases cover selected and explicit all-domain scopes, isotropic and heterogeneous materials, section coverage, laminate ordering, and orientation. Negative cases cover gaps, every overlap class, stale and ambiguous aliases, wrong role/dimension, cross-revision substitution, unused scopes, missing constitutive capabilities, and boundary faces mistaken for shell domains. The same compiled assignment identity and coefficients must be proven for local, process, durable, encrypted remote, retried, repartitioned, CPU, and supported GPU runs.

requirements.title: Typed constraint compilation, enforcement and reactions
requirements.acceptance: Typed constraint compilation, enforcement and reactions requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: Constraints are a first-class system capability, not a special case inside boundary assembly. They affect topology resolution, algebra, nonlinear state, modal admissibility, dynamics, reactions, adaptation, partitioning, and result evidence.

The public and internal models must distinguish: The existing cross-physics `BoundaryConditionKind` must be decomposed. A heat flux is not a kinematic constraint; acoustic impedance is not fixed displacement; contact is not a constrained boolean row.

Strings are permitted for authored identifiers and external lookup data: constraint IDs; region names and tags used to obtain a typed geometry selection; and user-facing labels. Strings are not permitted to choose: constraint kind; physics family; degree of freedom; coordinate frame kind; component selection; enforcement method; pairing method; schedule kind; or value dimension. The RunMat object API must expose concrete family-specific constructors and typed values. For example: Here `"base_support"` and `"Base_Mount"` are data. No string selects the constraint kind, structural DOF, physical dimension, or frame. High-level relations follow the same rule: The ordinary API should not require users to construct a generic object with a string such as `"periodic"`, `"ux"`, or `"global"`. Interfaces follow the same concrete, geometry-bound construction rule: The interface class and constructor fix the coupling family and physical law. Both regions retain admitted geometry identity and revision. Contact selects frictionless or Coulomb behavior; FSI selects physical interface kinematics; and CHT selects exactly one of perfect transfer, conductance, or resistance. Numerical enforcement—penalty scales, stabilization, damping, and coupling relaxation—is typed policy owned by the procedure step and solver. It is not authored as interface physics.

The final object surface should contain these typed roles, with exact class layout adjusted to the capabilities of RunMat's object system: Typed contract structure: fea.Constraint fea.StructuralConstraint fea.ThermalConstraint fea.ElectricalConstraint fea.MagneticConstraint fea.AcousticConstraint fea.FluidConstraint fea.Boundary fea.StructuralBoundary fea.ThermalBoundary fea.MagneticBoundary fea.AcousticBoundary fea.FluidBoundary fea.ProcedureStep fea.StructuralStep fea.ThermalStep fea.ElectromagneticStep fea.AcousticStep fea.FluidStep fea.ThermoMechanicalStep fea.ElectroThermalStep fea.ConjugateHeatTransferStep fea.FluidStructureStep fea.Interface fea.ContactInterface fea.FluidStructureInterface fea.ConjugateHeatTransferInterface fea.ConstraintRelation fea.RigidCoupling fea.DistributingCoupling fea.TieConstraint fea.PeriodicConstraint fea.ConstraintEquation fea.ConstraintValue fea.Displacement fea.Rotation fea.Temperature fea.TemperatureDifference fea.ElectricPotential fea.Pressure fea.Velocity fea.Translation fea.ComplexPhase fea.FrictionCoefficient fea.HeatTransferCoefficient fea.ThermalContactResistance fea.ConstraintSchedule fea.DisplacementSchedule fea.RotationSchedule fea.TemperatureSchedule fea.PotentialSchedule fea.PressureSchedule fea.VelocitySchedule Supporting typed objects include: `geometry.Region` and `geometry.EntitySelection`; `fea.ReferencePoint`; `fea.CoordinateFrame`; `fea.StructuralDof` and family-specific field components; `fea.StructuralDofValue`; `fea.ConstraintEquationTerm`; `fea.PeriodicTransform`; `fea.PeriodicPairing`; and dimensioned values such as displacement, rotation, position, length, temperature, pressure, and potential.

A common interface permits heterogeneous storage and orchestration, but construction remains concrete and family-specific. Invalid combinations should be unrepresentable where practical and otherwise rejected at the earliest typed validation boundary.

`runmat-analysis-core` should use nested typed enums and structures rather than a single large boundary enum or string tag dispatch: Typed contract structure: pub enum AnalysisConstraint { Structural(StructuralConstraint), Thermal(ThermalConstraint), Electrical(ElectricalConstraint), Magnetic(MagneticConstraint), Acoustic(AcousticConstraint), Fluid(FluidConstraint), } pub enum StructuralConstraint { PrescribedDofs(PrescribedStructuralDofs), NormalDisplacement(NormalDisplacementConstraint), Symmetry(StructuralSymmetryConstraint), RigidCoupling(RigidCouplingConstraint), DistributingCoupling(DistributingCouplingConstraint), Tie(TieConstraint), Periodic(StructuralPeriodicConstraint), Equation(StructuralConstraintEquation), } Translation and rotation values should remain distinct types. A rotation must not be constructible where a displacement is required. Family-specific equation terms must carry typed DOFs rather than arbitrary strings. The `.fea` source language necessarily spells closed choices as tokens. Those tokens are resolved once into typed semantic objects.
