The required flow is: Typed contract structure: .fea source text -> FEA lexer and parser -> module, symbol, type, and unit resolution -> authored-contract validation -> typed geometry resolution -> canonical constraint compilation -> algebraic or nonlinear enforcement No analysis or solver layer may compare textual constraint, DOF, frame, or enforcement names.

Resolved constraints must not retain an unqualified `region_id: String`. A typed target carries: admitted geometry identity and revision; persistent region or entity identity; entity dimension; selection digest; expected topology kind; selection/query provenance; and any cardinality or pairing requirements. The type and validation rules distinguish point, edge, face, volume, node, element, cell, and reference-point targets. A surface constraint cannot silently consume a volume selection. Constraints that expand over a region do so deterministically through the shared analysis projection.

Constraint values may be expressed in: the global frame; a typed user Cartesian, cylindrical, or spherical frame; a material or element frame where the formulation supports it; or a boundary-normal/tangent frame. Frame transforms are resolved into canonical evidence. Boundary-normal constraints must reject ambiguous edge/corner selections or use an explicitly documented averaging/pairing policy. Component masks use typed DOF values, not textual axes.

Constraint values may be: constant; step-dependent; a tabulated time history; frequency-dependent, including complex values where the family permits them; parameter-dependent through a portable study parameter; or supplied by a typed field artifact with compatible topology and units. Canonical schedules are serializable data. A live host closure does not enter the analysis model. RunMat callables supplied by language code, or named project callables referenced by a `.fea` document, must be frozen through the ordinary program closure and materialized into a canonical signal or field artifact before solver execution. A time-dependent prescribed displacement must supply or deterministically derive consistent displacement, velocity, and acceleration values for structural dynamics. Modal analysis admits homogeneous kinematic constraints only. Nonzero prescribed values in a modal study are rejected.

The structural production surface includes: fixed support; component-wise prescribed translation; component-wise prescribed rotation where rotational DOFs exist; normal displacement and roller support; symmetry and antisymmetry; rigid coupling to a reference point; distributing coupling to a reference point; ties over matching and supported nonmatching surfaces; general linear multipoint equations; translational periodicity; cyclic symmetry; beam and shell releases and supported joint relations; and spring, dashpot, and elastic-foundation connectors. Connectors are typed constitutive objects and contribute to stiffness, damping, or residual assembly. They are not represented as exact equation rows.
Incompressibility remains part of the mixed fluid formulation. It must not be exposed as a generic user-authored constraint equation.

Authored equality constraints compile into an immutable canonical plan representing: Typed contract structure: C q = d and, where reduction is appropriate: Typed contract structure: q = T q_reduced + q_offset The plan contains: canonical constraint and row identities; typed participating DOFs; sparse equation rows; prescribed values or schedule references; target provenance; coordinate transformations; relation and pairing groups; selected enforcement strategy; rank and conflict evidence; reaction-recovery mappings; and a canonical plan digest. The present boolean constrained-DOF mask may remain as an internal optimized specialization for homogeneous single-DOF constraints. It cannot remain the authoritative constraint model. Constraint-plan identity is deterministic and independent of row insertion order, mesh storage order, execution placement, and partition layout. Formulation-affecting enforcement parameters are included in logical identity.

Use the mathematical structure of the relation to select enforcement: direct elimination or affine lifting for ordinary prescribed values; transformation or null-space reduction for structured ties, periodic relations, rigid couplings, and compatible multipoint equations; Lagrange multipliers for exact general relations where reduction is unsuitable; formulation-specific null-space or gauge handling for singular pressure and potential operators; and penalty or augmented-Lagrangian methods only where the physical formulation requires them, especially unilateral contact. The ordinary user should not need to select enforcement. Expert overrides may be offered only as typed formulation options with clear diagnostics and identity consequences. Constraint enforcement must integrate correctly with stiffness, mass, damping, residual, tangent, eigensystems, transient effective loads, preconditioners, and distributed operators. Applying identity rows after the fact is insufficient for general relations.

Contact remains an `AnalysisInterface` at the authored physical-model boundary and compiles into a nonlinear inequality constraint system. It does not compile into the equality matrix `C`. The contact system owns: surface pairing and search updates; gap and normal definitions; active-set or complementarity state; normal enforcement; tangential/friction state; residual and tangent contributions; history and restart data; and complementarity and penetration evidence. Shared constraint diagnostics may report interactions between contact and equality constraints, such as a tied and contacting surface overlap, but must not erase their mathematical distinction.

Constraint validation has two levels. Before assembly, structural validation detects: empty or unmatched targets; invalid topological dimensions; constraints on unavailable DOFs; ambiguous frames or normals; conflicting prescribed values; obviously duplicate or cyclic relations; invalid or non-bijective periodic pairing where bijection is required; inconsistent transforms around relation cycles; incompatible contact, tie, connector, and essential-constraint overlap; unsupported nonhomogeneous modal constraints; and incomplete schedules. After assembly, numerical validation detects: redundant or linearly dependent equations; overconstraint; remaining rigid-body, gauge, or pressure null modes; constraint-matrix rank loss; excessive conditioning damage; multiplier instability; and excessive relation violation. Diagnostics identify the authored constraint IDs, resolved entities, affected DOFs, and conflicting relation rows. They must not report only anonymous matrix indices.

Constraint results include: nodal reaction force and moment; face, region, and reference-point resultants; multiplier values where applicable; generalized reaction per authored constraint; constraint work and energy; relation violation norms; prescribed-value error; action-reaction balance for ties and couplings; active, redundant, and eliminated row counts; and rank/null-space diagnostics. Reaction recovery uses the original unconstrained equilibrium residual or mathematically equivalent multiplier result. Identity rows inserted into a modified operator are not a valid source of reactions.

Constraints bind to persistent geometry and topology identities rather than incidental node numbers. After h- or p-adaptation, the analysis projection rebuilds the canonical constraint plan, checks target coverage and pairing, transfers necessary state, and records old/new plan lineage. For large-deformation and contact studies, geometry-dependent normals, pairings, and active state update through the owning nonlinear formulation. Authored identity remains stable while current configuration data becomes iteration state.

Every canonical constraint row has one stable identity and one publication owner. Participating DOFs may span partitions; required ghost/halo data is explicit. Distributed assembly rejects missing, duplicate, or conflicting rows. Rigid couplings, global equations, and reference points declare collective communication requirements. Partition-local elimination cannot change the mathematical constraint space. Constraint-plan identity excludes worker count and partition layout. Distributed reactions and violation norms use deterministic or explicitly tolerance-governed reductions. Inline, local-process, durable, and remote shapes are compared against the same serial constraint reference.

Required governed cases include: component-wise zero and nonzero prescribed values; constraints in rotated and boundary-normal frames; rigid-body mode removal without spurious stiffness; intentionally underconstrained and overconstrained systems; duplicate and linearly dependent equations; rigid and distributing reference-point couplings with force/moment balance; matching and nonmatching ties; periodic translation and cyclic rotation; structural symmetry and antisymmetry; beam/shell releases, joints, springs, and dashpots; time-dependent motion with dynamic equilibrium and energy checks; modal homogeneous-constraint behavior; thermal, electrical, magnetic, acoustic, and fluid gauge/periodic cases; contact/equality overlap rejection; reaction and constraint-work recovery; constraint rebuilding after h- and p-adaptation; and partition- and placement-independent constraint results.

Essential field constraint; Prescribed displacement, rotation, temperature, electric potential, pressure reference; Restricts one or more solution DOFs.. Natural or Robin boundary; Traction, heat flux, convection, acoustic impedance, radiation; Adds residual, operator, or source terms on a boundary.. Kinematic relation; Tie, periodicity, rigid coupling, symmetry, multipoint equation; Relates multiple DOFs or a field to a reference entity.. Connector; Spring, dashpot, joint, elastic foundation; Adds constitutive stiffness, damping, force, or release behavior.. Inequality/stateful constraint; Unilateral contact and friction; Adds an active-set or complementarity problem with history.. Internal gauge/null-space condition; Pressure reference, electric or magnetic gauge; Makes a formulation well posed without pretending it is an ordinary support..

Thermal; Prescribed temperature, tied temperature, periodic temperature, and supported affine temperature jumps.. Electrostatic/conduction; Prescribed potential, equipotential terminals, floating conductors, integral charge/current conditions, and gauge/reference handling.. Magnetostatic/Maxwell; Gauge conditions, symmetry, periodicity, and complex phase-shifted relations where supported.. Acoustic; Prescribed pressure and periodic or Bloch/Floquet relations.. CFD; Component velocity constraints, moving walls, symmetry, periodicity, and pressure gauge/reference conditions.. Coupled physics; Typed interface continuity or transfer relations that preserve the distinct conservation law on each side..

requirements.title: Typed signals, frozen generators and conservative actions
requirements.acceptance: Typed signals, frozen generators and conservative actions requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: Excitation is a first-class cross-family system. It must not be implemented independently by structural dynamics, thermal, electromagnetic, acoustic, and fluid modules.

Four layers have distinct ownership: The solver never depends on `runmat-value`, the VM, a session workspace, or callback dispatch. Runtime adapters may accept a callable `Value`; the validated analysis input is data. The authored model keeps these concepts separate: an essential constraint may reference a signal, but remains a constraint; a natural boundary or volume action is a load or source excitation; displacement, velocity, temperature, pressure, and field state at the beginning of a procedure are initial conditions; coupled-physics transfer uses a typed field artifact, not a callback; a load is one physical action, while a load or excitation case groups actions that are activated and combined together; and a state-dependent controller, constitutive law, follower load, user element, or source depending on the current solution is an executable numerical law, not an ordinary excitation signal. Remove the separate thermo-mechanical, electrothermal, and CFD time-profile authorities once the shared signal model is available. Family modules may impose family-specific admissibility rules but must not define another time-history representation.

A signal declares: stable signal identity; independent domain: constant, time, frequency, or portable study parameter; physical quantity and dimensions; scalar, vector, tensor, complex, or topology-field value shape; coordinate frame and component meaning when applicable; representation: constant, tabulated samples, a supported standard waveform, or an immutable artifact; abscissa and ordinate units with one explicit conversion to canonical units; interpolation, breakpoint, discontinuity, and extrapolation policy; valid domain and endpoint behavior; precision and complex-domain requirements; sampling or approximation error evidence; and provenance and content digest. Use quantity-specific Rust types or validated typed wrappers. Do not represent force, acceleration, heat flux, voltage, and acoustic pressure as interchangeable numeric arrays distinguished only by a string. FEA-language tokens and MATLAB-facing names are resolved once into those typed contracts. There is no hidden nominal-amplitude convention. A signal is either dimensioned and absolute, or explicitly dimensionless and applied as a scale to a dimensioned action. Vector direction times scalar magnitude and an absolute vector history are distinct typed forms. Phase is represented by a complex phasor or a declared phase convention, not by unrelated `phase_rad` and `amplitude_scale` fields embedded in selected load variants.

An excitation binds a signal to physical space and declares: stable excitation identity and containing excitation-case identity; typed action such as force, moment, traction, pressure, body force, base displacement/velocity/acceleration, heat generation, heat flux, ambient temperature, current density, terminal voltage, acoustic pressure, normal velocity, inlet velocity, or mass flow; persistent region, entity, reference-point, port, or interface target; coordinate frame, direction, components, and follower/non-follower behavior where meaningful; distribution and normalization policy, including whether an authored resultant or an intensity is preserved; active procedure steps and combination group; associated signal or field artifact; and projection and conservation requirements. Realization produces immutable topology- and operator-compatible data. It records resolved entities, quadrature/integration policy, resultant and moment checks, units, signal digest, projection digest, and any interpolation or transfer error. Mesh-dependent generated spatial fields are materialized after topology projection and before assembly. They may be partitioned preprocessing work, but never callbacks inside element quadrature or a solver iteration.

RunMat code may construct a signal from ordinary arrays or from a function handle or anonymous closure. Array construction is the simplest path and naturally composes with RunMat signal processing, control systems, data access, sparse values, parallel execution, and GPU placement. A callable-backed constructor additionally requires a typed domain and materialization policy. The preferred callable is vectorized over time, frequency, parameter, or canonical sample points. Before the solve: resolve the callable through the normal typed callable system; validate its declared input/output facts and captures; freeze its source project or compiled package closure; reject unsupported effects and capabilities; evaluate it in a bounded preprocessing task; validate shape, quantity, units, finiteness, domain coverage, and continuity claims; materialize a canonical signal or field artifact; and make the solver depend only on that artifact. Adaptive time stepping does not justify a live solver callback. A generator is adaptively sampled ahead of the solve to a declared interpolation tolerance, with discontinuities represented by explicit breakpoints or step interpolation. If a prescribed kinematic history is supplied as displacement, the materializer must receive or deterministically derive compatible velocity and acceleration and record derivative-error evidence. A direct base-acceleration history does not require artificial integration to displacement unless the selected formulation needs it.

The initial production effect policy rejects workspace writes, environment mutation, undeclared filesystem access, network access, UI interaction, uncontrolled randomness, clock dependence, host callbacks, and unknown effects. Immutable portable captures are allowed. Random excitation uses an explicit seed, distribution, PSD/cross-PSD, or frozen realization. Session-bound handles, mutable handle objects, foreign references, and unfenced device handles are rejected. The intended language shape is ordinary numerical preparation followed by a small number of typed FEA constructors. Exact names should follow the builtin/object conventions present after platform convergence, but the semantic shape is: The callable form describes how to produce the same typed history; it does not change what the solver receives: Quantity-specific convenience constructors use documented canonical units. A general constructor, if exposed, requires explicit typed time/frequency axes and dimensioned values; it must not accept an unqualified numeric array plus a free-form quantity string. Typed direction, frame, interpolation, extrapolation, response measure, and combination-policy values replace solver-layer string dispatch.

A data-only `.fea` remains fully standalone. It may contain bounded inline samples or reference a declared data object that is content-hashed and frozen into the study bundle. The declarative form resolves once into the same typed objects. It imports the generating function from its actual `.m` file rather than relying on a magic namespace: Base acceleration is prescribed support kinematics rather than an ordinary excitation. It must identify the support region, driven degree of freedom, initial displacement and velocity, and the governed reconstruction. The referenced acceleration history is a real global vector over time; ordinary forces and source terms continue to use the excitation contract. A code-generated input references an explicitly imported project function plus typed arguments and sampling/materialization policy. It does not embed source text, a live closure, an absolute host path, or base-workspace state. `runmat run study.fea` resolves the enclosing RunMat project, freezes the same source graph and callable inventory used by ordinary program execution, and includes it in the encrypted execution bundle. Without a resolvable project and callable, planning fails before expensive work begins. An explicit relative `.m` import resolves immediately to a project-owned qualified function identity. Package-qualified functions remain supported for projects that use them, but package folders are not required by the language or its examples. Scripts are not excitation generators because they lack an argument/output contract and depend on mutable base-workspace and path state.

Initial conditions are model-owned reusable physical state and are selected by the consuming analysis; a reusable model never hard-codes a study step name. The closed kinds cover structural displacement, velocity, and angular velocity; thermal temperature; electric potential; magnetic vector potential; acoustic pressure; and fluid pressure and velocity. A condition has exactly one strongly typed source: a finite uniform scalar/vector, an exact non-frequency signal sample with a typed coordinate and explicit discontinuity side, or an immutable field artifact whose content, topology, field, quantity, shape, frame, and completeness are checked at admission. Vector state requires an explicit frame. The study-binding pass alone creates `applies_before_step` and its state input; compatible upstream state takes precedence unless the procedure declares a typed replacement policy, and conflicting state is rejected rather than combined implicitly. `check` performs schema, callable-resolution, static signature, effect, capability, unit, and policy validation without executing user code. `plan` constructs the materialization and solve graph without claiming generated values are valid. `run` executes the materialization task, validates and publishes its artifact, then admits dependent mesh/assembly/solve tasks. A separately exposed materialize operation may be added if evidence shows users need to inspect or approve generated inputs before a solve.

Modal eigenvalue extraction has no excitation. Forced use of modes is represented by separate procedures: modal transient response from time histories; modal harmonic response from complex frequency-domain excitations; modal response-spectrum analysis from a typed design or shock response spectrum; and random vibration response from PSD and cross-PSD inputs. Computing a shock response spectrum from a base-acceleration time history is a general signal-processing operation. Consuming that spectrum with structural modes is an FEA modal-response procedure. Do not call both operations `modal analysis` or treat an SRS as an unnamed frequency/value table. A typed response spectrum retains: natural frequency or period abscissa and units; damping ratio or quality factor; response ordinate quantity: relative displacement/velocity/acceleration, absolute acceleration, or an explicitly defined pseudo quantity; positive, negative, or maximax envelope convention; construction method and sampling adequacy evidence when derived from a history; interpolation and extrapolation policy; base direction and frame; spectrum and directional combination rules; modal truncation, participation, residual-mode, rigid-response, and missing-mass policy; and provenance and content digest. Modal-response results include participation factors, effective modal mass by direction, cumulative captured mass, per-mode response, correlation/combination evidence, missing-mass contribution where enabled, and the modes actually used. SRSS is accepted only under its documented separation assumptions. CQC or another explicitly supported correlation method is required where closely spaced modes invalidate those assumptions. Directional combination and modal combination are distinct policies.

Generated physical input has layered identity: Typed contract structure: generator provenance = program revision + callable identity + captures + declared frozen inputs signal realization = canonical samples/field + quantity + units + interpolation + error evidence solver excitation = signal realization + spatial projection + activation + procedure Study provenance includes the generator identity and realization digest. Numerical caches may reuse a realization with identical canonical content while preserving distinct authored provenance. Code changes, capture changes, sampling-policy changes, frozen-input changes, or materialized output changes invalidate the appropriate layer. Materialization uses the existing driver, program bundle, `ValuePayload`, object store, encryption, cancellation, retry, and publication fencing. The Server remains content-blind. A generated artifact is published once per logical identity and reused by sweep entries, load cases, and distributed ranks. Small signals may be broadcast. Large time histories and topology fields use manifest-plus-chunk artifacts, partial transfer, and partition-aware access. Every rank applies the same canonical interpolation contract. GPU-resident generation is allowed when ordinary RunMat placement supports it, but the published artifact still has provider-neutral identity and truthful transfer evidence. A callable does not become a GPU solver kernel merely because it was evaluated on a GPU.

State-dependent executable laws require a separate future contract with a portable compiled ABI, typed state and outputs, derivative/tangent requirements, effect and capability policy, CPU/GPU/distributed implementations, checkpoint semantics, and verification. No family may introduce such callbacks ad hoc through the excitation API.

Required governed cases include: constant, piecewise-linear, step, and complex frequency-dependent signals; discontinuities, domain boundaries, interpolation, extrapolation rejection, and adaptive materialization error; closure capture and named project function equivalence to an explicit table; source/capture changes invalidating identity and identical canonical realizations reusing numerical work correctly; rejection of mutable, nondeterministic, unavailable, or nonportable callable dependencies; inline, isolated-process, durable, and encrypted remote materialization equivalence; retry, cancellation, stale-publication fencing, and artifact reuse; static force/moment resultants and transient work/energy balance; prescribed displacement/velocity/acceleration consistency; base acceleration and modal participation factors; SRS construction references and modal response-spectrum SRSS/CQC, directional-combination, truncation, and missing-mass references; harmonic complex amplitude and phase; thermal, electrical, electromagnetic, acoustic, and fluid source/boundary histories; mesh-dependent spatial field projection and conservation; partition-independent distributed interpolation and source assembly; and explicit CPU/GPU transfer, precision, synchronization, and fallback evidence.

RunMat language and general numerical libraries; Generate, import, filter, resample, transform, and combine arrays using ordinary functions, closures, signal-processing operations, control-system models, data APIs, and accelerator execution.. `runmat-analysis-core`; Own strongly typed signals, physical quantities, excitations, initial conditions, response spectra, targets, frames, activation, and interpolation intent.. `runmat-analysis-fea`; Realize signals and spatial actions on canonical topology, form load/source vectors and boundary terms, compute modal participation and spectral combinations, and publish realization evidence.. Runtime and execution; Resolve and freeze callable code closure, validate captures and effects, execute preprocessing tasks, persist canonical signal/field artifacts, and distribute them through the existing artifact and scheduling infrastructure..

requirements.title: Semantic procedure transitions and immutable completed state
requirements.acceptance: Semantic procedure transitions and immutable completed state requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: An engineering study is an ordered semantic sequence of procedures, not merely one procedure plus an execution task graph. `runmat-analysis-core` owns the authored sequence. `runmat-analysis-fea` validates procedure compatibility, realizes state transitions, and records their evidence. The generic execution graph schedules that already validated sequence; it cannot invent physical dependencies or decide which state is meaningful to transfer. The public model contains: `AnalysisSequence`, with stable step identities and an explicit directed acyclic dependency graph; `ProcedureStep`, with one typed physics family, analysis procedure, solution space, activation set, output requests, accuracy policy, and formulation options; `StateInput`, naming the required upstream state kind and admissible source step; `StateOutput`, naming the state actually published by a completed step; `StateTransition`, defining compatibility, projection, linearization, and reference-state policy between two steps; and `SequenceBranch`, allowing multiple downstream procedures to consume the same immutable persisted state without rerunning or mutating the producer. The inter-step semantic graph is acyclic. Nonlinear iterations, contact active-set updates, partitioned coupling, and adaptive solve/estimate/refine cycles occur inside a governed procedure step and are represented by its checkpointed execution subgraph; they are not back-edges that obscure which completed physical state a later procedure consumes. Closed enums and family-specific types represent procedure and state kinds. Strings may name steps, regions, and authored objects, but do not select transition behavior. At minimum, state contracts distinguish: converged primary fields and their topology;

velocities, accelerations, and time-integrator state; temperature and thermal reference state; stress, strain, geometric-stiffness, and material-history state; contact active-set and friction history where the receiving procedure permits it; fluid state and moving-mesh/ALE state; electromagnetic complex or static field state; modal bases, normalization, participation, and truncation metadata; and coupled-interface state and relaxation history.

Loads, sources, constraints, contacts, interfaces, initial conditions, output requests, and supported material parameters declare step-scoped activation. Activation is a typed lifecycle of `Activate`, `Continue`, `Modify`, or `Deactivate`; absence is not interpreted as an implicit continuation. A modification produces a new authored identity while retaining attribution to the original object. Every step declares its own independent variable and origin. Total study time, step-local time, frequency, eigenvalue parameter, load factor, and iteration count are distinct typed domains. A transition must explicitly map any continuing schedule into the receiving domain. Restarting a transient step does not reset physical time unless the authored sequence says so. Initial conditions apply only where no compatible upstream state supplies the same quantity, unless a typed override policy explicitly replaces or augments that state. Conflicts are rejected before execution.

Initial production transitions include: static structural state to prestressed modal extraction; static or supported nonlinear structural state to eigenvalue buckling; static or supported nonlinear structural state to prestressed direct or modal harmonic response; thermal state to structural temperature, thermal strain, and prestress; completed transient state to a continuation or restart of the same formulation; modal extraction state to modal transient, harmonic, response-spectrum, or random response; converged family states into the supported coupled procedures; and parent-mesh state to an adapted mesh through the separately governed adaptation transfer. Each transition declares whether it reuses a field, projects it, linearizes about it, derives a new operator contribution, or uses it only as an initial guess. These meanings are never conflated. In particular: procedure-specific physics and numerical settings use a closed typed canonical union rather than string maps or runtime defaults. Random response, for example, authors modal damping and the required cumulative modal-mass ratio on the procedure; task interval grouping and iteration ceilings remain placement-neutral numerical execution policy; prestressed procedures consume a converged base state and derive the documented tangent and geometric-stiffness contributions; an initial guess does not become a physical initial condition; a visualization interpolation is never accepted as solver state transfer; stateful plasticity or contact history is transferred only when the receiving formulation and mesh-transfer evidence support it; and unsupported topology, units, frames, formulations, or state revisions fail with an attributable transition diagnostic.

Every state-producing step publishes an immutable, typed state manifest before dependent steps are admitted. The manifest includes producer-step identity, topology and partition identities, physical time or load parameter, field and history digests, reference conventions, linearization point, constraint plan, precision, and completeness evidence. A restart resumes an interrupted procedure from a collectively valid checkpoint. A branch begins a new procedure from a completed immutable state. A retry repeats an execution attempt for the same logical step. These are different operations and have different identities. No checkpoint or partial field may be relabeled as a completed base state. Downstream logical identity includes the complete semantic transition and upstream state digest. Placement, worker count, attempt, and physical chunk boundaries remain execution evidence. Independent downstream branches may run concurrently and reuse the same state artifact. A tightly coupled or stateful step retains the group-level checkpoint and epoch rules required for cooperative execution.

Required governed cases include: static preload to prestressed modal frequency shift; base-state stress to eigenvalue buckling load factors and modes; thermal solution to thermal strain, reaction, and prestressed response; transient continuation matching an uninterrupted reference run; branching one base state into modal, harmonic, and buckling procedures without mutation; correct activation, modification, and deactivation of loads and constraints by step; rejection of incompatible topology, state kind, reference convention, units, or procedure transitions; durable and encrypted remote restart from a complete checkpoint; stale checkpoint and stale upstream-state publication fencing; and sequence identity and results remaining independent of placement and worker layout.

requirements.title: Typed field recovery, bounded observations and monitors
requirements.acceptance: Typed field recovery, bounded observations and monitors requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: Results are requested through a typed observation system. It prevents accidental production of enormous result sets, supports useful answers without full-field transfer, and keeps result selection separate from visualization. Calling `plot` or `mesh` never decides what physical quantity to recover. The authored output contract distinguishes: `FieldOutput`: a spatial field snapshot or governed series over a typed region and topology location; `HistoryOutput`: relatively frequent values for a bounded point, entity set, connector, reference point, interface, or global quantity; `ProbeOutput`: a point evaluation or spatial aggregate intended for inspection or monitoring; `ReductionOutput`: an integral, average, norm, resultant, moment, minimum, maximum, RMS, variance, envelope, or another explicitly supported typed reduction; `DiagnosticOutput`: convergence, balance, constraint, contact, adaptation, and resource evidence; and `Monitor`: a bounded scalar observation evaluated during solution for progress or a typed termination criterion. Every request declares: a stable request identity and producing procedure step; physical quantity and value shape; target region, entity, reference point, connector, interface, or whole-model scope; source location such as nodal, cell, element, integration point, face, edge, modal, or global; requested output location and the governed recovery or interpolation required to obtain it; component, invariant, coordinate frame, sign convention, and complex representation where applicable; sampling domain and schedule: final, every accepted increment, named points, interval, event, frequency set, mode set, or adaptive policy; spatial and series reduction policies, including tie behavior for extrema;

precision, compression, retention, and partial-access policy; whether it is required for solver control, publication, visualization, or downstream sequence state; and an estimate of computation, resident memory, stored bytes, transfer, and collective cost. Quantity and reduction compatibility is validated before solve. A tensor invariant is not a string expression, a complex field cannot silently lose phase, an integration-point value cannot be called nodal without a recovery policy, and an extreme value must retain its value, location, producing step, sample coordinate, and tie policy.

Field recovery belongs to the producing physics family. Observation evaluation consumes those governed fields or explicitly documented solver-available quantities. It may compose typed operations but cannot recreate family equations or reach into private solver storage. Derived quantities use a typed expression or operation graph over admitted physical quantities. It checks dimensions, shapes, topology locations, frames, real/complex domains, and differentiability metadata. Ordinary RunMat functions may construct output data or post-process a published result, but no live language callback executes inside element recovery, a distributed reduction, or a solver monitor. Reusable generated post-processing follows the same freezing and materialization principles as generated excitations. Output expressions do not create a second FEA builtin namespace. Extend the canonical RunMat builtin/operation catalog with typed overloads and frontend applicability. One public operation identity such as `max` may have an ordinary numeric-tensor runtime binding and FEA field, history, or sweep-case lowerings. The FEA compiler selects an overload statically and lowers it to a canonical observation plan; the runtime binding remains runtime-owned. Domain-specific operations such as `resultant` and surface `moment` register in that same catalog and may expose compatible `.m` object overloads. Do not add an untracked parser keyword list, analysis-private name table, or separate documentation registry.

Each overload declares typed inputs/named arguments/output, quantity and unit transformation, shape, scalar/complex/statistical domain, field location/frame/coordinate rules, purity and effects, distributability, reduction ordering and tie policy, equivalence, cost shape, frontend availability, lowering owner, and documentation. The catalog drives parser/LSP completion, hover, signature help, named-argument completion, diagnostics, and generated reference material. Spatial/series/case extrema return typed attributed extrema rather than bare numbers. The value retains its physical quantity; the result also carries canonical entity/location or independent coordinate/case, source, and tie/reduction evidence. Vector/tensor/complex/statistical values need an explicit valid projection or representation before scalar extrema. Therefore the target syntax uses `max`, not a divergent `maximum`, and exposes `.value` or `.location` only where the inferred extremum type supports them. Default output sets are procedure-specific, small, documented, and versioned. Explicit requests replace or extend defaults according to a typed policy; omission never means “store every supported variable.” Requests that affect recovery, solver state retention, checkpoint content, or computation participate in the appropriate logical identity. The runtime-facing separation remains: `fea.field` and `fea.probe` select or evaluate analysis results. Ordinary `plot` and `mesh` render compatible values and remain compatible with their non-FEA MATLAB behavior.

Large field outputs are partitioned and chunked according to canonical ownership. Point probes route to the owning partition. Spatial reductions compute partition-local contributions and use deterministic or tolerance-governed collectives. Global extrema carry location and attribution through the reduction. Surface and volume integrals use the same quadrature, measures, orientation, and topology identities as assembly. History and probe streams are bounded, checkpointable artifacts; they are not unbounded driver messages. Monitors publish rate-limited progress samples separately from the canonical final history. GPU-resident fields may be reduced through provider operations when supported. Any host fallback is selected before evaluation and recorded with transfer and synchronization evidence. A monitor may observe progress or trigger a typed stop condition based on a governed scalar such as residual, balance, target response, or physical time. It cannot mutate loads, materials, constraints, or solver state. Feedback control and state-dependent executable laws require their own future stateful contract.

Required governed cases include: nodal, cell, element, integration-point, face, edge, modal, and global outputs where supported; frame transformations, tensor invariants, complex magnitude/phase, and sign conventions; point, path, boundary, volume, interface, connector, and reference-point observations; final, increment, time-point, frequency, mode, event, and adaptive sampling; integral, resultant, moment, extrema with location, RMS, envelope, and statistical reductions; serial, partitioned, distributed, CPU, and claimed GPU equivalence; bounded storage and transfer under high-rate histories; correct restart without missing or duplicated history samples; partial result access without gathering unrelated fields; output cost admission and rejection of infeasible requests before expensive solve work; and separation of canonical numerical results, monitors, and visualization products.

requirements.title: Placement-independent logical studies and governed scheduling
requirements.acceptance: Placement-independent logical studies and governed scheduling requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: A canonical logical study identity includes: geometry source identity and admitted geometry revision; canonical mesh request or solver-mesh digest; authored problem and material assignments; authored signal, excitation, initial-condition, response-spectrum, and combination contracts; generator provenance for generated authored inputs; materialized signal/field digests enter the downstream realized-study and solver-excitation identities after materialization; semantic analysis sequence, step identities, activation lifecycle, state-transition policies, and upstream state digests; physics family and analysis procedure for every step; formulation and numerical tolerances that can affect the mathematical result; typed observation requests when they affect recovery, retained solver state, computation, or canonical publication; requested accuracy and acceptance policy; and deterministic/numerical backend policy where it can affect accepted result equivalence. It excludes: local, durable, or remote placement; cluster and queue; worker count and partition layout; retry attempts; temporary paths; physical artifact locations; UI session IDs; and attach or detach behavior.

The shared CLI placement surface should preserve local defaults and reuse current cluster vocabulary: The reusable placement options are: project selection; cluster selection; queue, defaulting consistently with `job submit`; worker count, with zero retaining its existing driver-only/automatic meaning; trust identity, preferably supplied by project or named target configuration; idempotency key; attach/detach behavior; and machine-readable output. Do not require users to wrap `.fea` or meshing requests in a synthetic MATLAB script. `job submit` remains the generic MATLAB-program entrypoint. `runmat run file.fea` and `runmat mesh` prepare domain-specific encrypted execution bundles and reuse the lower-level submission lifecycle. An authored execution-policy reference is optional. Its absence means the CLI/project defaults choose placement, backend, and resources; it does not make the study incomplete. If present, the policy may express placement preference, elastic resource bounds, independent fanout, cooperative-distribution requirements, accelerator preference, and resilience. It cannot change physics or accuracy. CLI placement overrides use the same typed policy merge and may choose an equivalent location or tighten bounds without changing study-definition identity.

Execute one complete study on one allocated worker. Materialize and validate callable-backed signals before admitting dependent assembly or solve work. Preserve the existing local inline behavior as the default. Support local process isolation, durable local execution, and remote execution. Publish the same logical result and evidence shape across placements.

Execute independent sweep entries concurrently. Deduplicate shared geometry, mesh, signal, response-spectrum, and realized-excitation artifacts by logical digest. Permit independent frequency points, load cases, parameter samples, sequence branches, observation reductions, and study variants to become tasks when their result composition is deterministic. Honor fail-fast and collect-all policies without losing already completed evidence.

Partition element or cell assembly. Use deterministic sparse contribution composition. Add distributed matrix-vector and preconditioner strategies only after the serial operator is verified. Define capability requirements by formulation, order, scalar type, backend, and required native kernel. Establish strong and appropriately tolerance-bounded result equivalence against the serial reference.

Represent sequence progression, coupled iterations, and adaptive iterations as checkpointed graph progression. Fence iteration publication so stale attempts cannot commit state. Transfer only canonical field/history artifacts between stages. Make convergence decisions deterministic from persisted evidence.

Use driver-owned scheduling already supported by worker allocations. Do not create nested independent schedulers inside FEA solvers. An analysis root job owns a task graph containing only the granularity justified for its level. Initially this is frozen-input admission, any required signal materialization, a mesh prerequisite, excitation realization, validated procedure-step execution, observation evaluation, and result publication. Data-independent materialization and meshing may run concurrently. Independent sequence branches may run concurrently after their immutable producer state is published. Verified solvers can later expand assembly, linear algebra, coupling, adaptation, or distributed reductions into child tasks. The semantic sequence is compiled into the task graph; it is not reconstructed from task edges. Execution retries, repartitioning, or placement changes cannot alter step activation, state meaning, or transition policy. Meshing invoked by a study remains the same canonical meshing graph used by standalone `runmat mesh`; analysis consumes its artifact rather than reimplementing meshing stages.

Independent distribution uses the existing durable task model for whole studies, mesh stages, sweep entries, load cases, frequency points, recovery partitions, and other replay-safe tasks. These tasks communicate through immutable content-addressed artifacts and may be retried independently under the existing effect policy. Cooperative distributed algebra is a different execution class. It requires: gang allocation of a compatible worker group; a stable group and partition epoch; deterministic partition-to-worker ownership; peer routing and authenticated channels; halo exchange and collective reduction contracts; iteration barriers and collective cancellation; topology- and accelerator-aware resource admission; coordinated checkpoint and restart; and group-level failure semantics. The existing driver remains the sole scheduler. The FEA solver supplies a numerical partition/communication plan and participates through the existing `GangHandle`/`SpmdTaskContext` generation and collective identities; it does not start a nested scheduler. The generic execution and runner crates own gang and collective lifecycle semantics, while `runmat-execution-runner-native` implements the native and encrypted remote transport behavior. Language-level `ValuePayload` collectives are the functional baseline, not automatically the high-throughput numerical data plane. Benchmark reduction latency, payload copying, coordinator pressure, halo throughput, and device-resident behavior. Any required bulk extension retains the same gang generation, rank, collective sequence, cancellation, causal failure, authentication, and fencing contracts.

A failed independent task may retry alone. A lost participant in a tightly coupled Krylov, nonlinear, or coupled iteration cannot publish or retry independently. The group either recovers from a collectively valid checkpoint or restarts under a new epoch. Stale epochs are fenced from all state and result publication.

The partition plan defines owned and ghost DOFs, elements/cells, constraint rows, interfaces, and result ranges. It has its own execution identity and evidence but does not alter authored-problem or discretized-problem identity. No worker independently guesses ownership. Distributed assembly emits partition-local canonical contributions. A global matrix is not gathered unless a selected small-problem backend explicitly requires it. Distributed operator application declares halo messages and collective reductions, and preconditioners declare their communication topology and setup/reuse lifetime. Multi-GPU execution is the composition of accelerator-local kernels with cooperative distributed algebra. It is not implied by requesting several GPU workers and is not advertised until halo transfer, collective reduction, failure, and numerical evidence pass.
Parallelism is introduced at natural deterministic boundaries.

Parallel element/cell assembly into partition-local contribution buffers. Deterministic merge ordering for reproducible modes. Parallel recovery and balance evaluation. Bounded memory and cancellation checkpoints.

Partition by canonical element/cell identities. Externalize immutable partition inputs. Produce canonical contribution artifacts with exact ownership. Join contributions deterministically and reject duplicates or omissions.

Begin with embarrassingly parallel studies, load cases, and frequencies. Add distributed sparse matrix-vector work and preconditioning family by family. Define halo/ghost ownership, communication budgets, convergence aggregation, and failure recovery explicitly. Never claim bitwise equivalence when floating-point reduction order makes only tolerance-bounded equivalence meaningful; encode the applicable equivalence policy in evidence. Compare local inline, isolated process, durable, and remote results against the same verified serial reference.

Capabilities should describe actual worker requirements, including: analysis host ABI; physics formulation and implementation revision; element order and supported topology; scalar/complex precision; CPU instruction or accelerator class where required; deterministic platform cohort where strict replay requires it; native exact-CAD kernel only for tasks that perform geometry admission or meshing; and memory, scratch, wall-time, artifact, egress, and relay budgets.

Re-audit current `origin/dev`; consume landed typed value, gang, collective, distributed, accelerator, and provider contracts before adding any platform-facing type. Reuse the already-public `runmat-types` numeric and storage facts immediately where their semantics are exact; do not wait for the broader runtime migration to duplicate them locally. Define canonical study, sequence, step, state-transition, workload, task, observation, accuracy, result, and publication identities in `runmat-analysis-fea`, including layered generator, signal-realization, and solver-excitation identities. Define analysis worker capabilities and artifact media/schema contracts. Include canonical constraint-plan inputs, identities, evidence, and publication ownership in analysis tasks. Define the layered problem, discretization, operator, numerical-plan, execution-plan, attempt, and result identities. Add the analysis workload executable form and typed host ABI through the generic artifact and runner contracts. Define manifest-plus-chunk numerical objects for mesh, signal, response spectrum, realized excitation, field, semantic state, history, observation, accuracy evidence, operator, and checkpoint data. Implement the native analysis provider alongside the existing meshing provider. Split meshing stage execution into one immutable bundle-authorized host program and a run-scoped, externalized invocation descriptor. Dynamically planned stages must reuse the same program artifact; the descriptor and its declared semantic roots are validated together before a kernel runs.

Make the existing meshing-owned exact DAG orchestration awaitable and implement a remote pool executor over the generic runner. Keep the driver as the root-workload orchestrator and workers as stage kernels; do not duplicate the DAG, wrap CAD in MATLAB, or create nested worker-side scheduling. Add a portable exact-meshing root workload with chunked source-CAD admission and a canonical terminal mesh/evidence closure. Remote CAD admission must not require a local OCCT installation, and actual run authority and platform evidence must never be accepted from the payload. Add shared placement arguments to `runmat run` and `runmat mesh` only as their corresponding execution shapes become real. Central validation must reject unsupported combinations before compilation, CAD import, path reservation, or network work. Support whole-study local-process, durable, and remote execution. Compile validated semantic sequences into execution graphs; execute independent sweep entries and immutable sequence branches concurrently and remotely through the same graph. Resolve named `.fea` project callables and language closures through the existing callable and frozen-project machinery; add typed static signature, effect, capability, capture, and portability admission. Implement bounded callable materialization tasks that publish canonical signal or mesh-dependent field artifacts before dependent work, without live solver callbacks. Deduplicate shared geometry, mesh, signal, spectrum, and excitation artifacts. Add progress, cancellation, retry, attach, recovery, and fenced-publication conformance, including materialization tasks.

Add Desktop placement and lifecycle integration using generic execution services and partial result access, including sequence/step state, generated physical inputs, observations, accuracy status, and provenance. Add conformance tests for borrowed, moved, materialized, device-resident, and distributed value admission, including copy-accounting and forbidden implicit-conversion cases. A simple verified study and a standalone mesh produce equivalent logical outputs in inline, isolated-process, durable, and remote shapes. A sweep demonstrates bounded parallel execution and deterministic composition. Explicit tables and equivalent callable-generated inputs produce equivalent canonical realizations in inline, isolated-process, durable, and encrypted remote execution. Callable source, capture, frozen-input, sampling-policy, and realized-content changes invalidate the correct identity layer; retries cannot publish stale generated input. Large inputs and results travel as closed, chunked artifacts rather than inline values or driver-gathered payloads. The Server remains content-blind. Placement is absent from logical study identity. Constraint identity and results are independent of worker count and partition layout. Semantic step ordering, activation, state transitions, and branch results are independent of execution scheduling and retries. Bounded histories and partial observations can be queried without gathering unrelated full fields.

requirements.title: Canonical sparse operators and compatible prepared solves
requirements.acceptance: Canonical sparse operators and compatible prepared solves requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: The analysis system owns the mathematical operator; RunMat's generic compute substrate owns execution representations and placement. This boundary must be explicit before production families proliferate.

Every assembled or matrix-free operator declares: scalar domain and precision; dimensions and block structure; symmetry or Hermitian status; positive-definite, semidefinite, indefinite, or unknown classification; null-space and gauge information; sparse pattern identity and numeric-value revision when assembled; constraint-plan identity; partition plan when distributed; apply, transpose-apply, and adjoint-apply support as applicable; and memory, scratch, and communication estimates. The sparse pattern and its numeric values have separate identities. Geometry, topology, or constraint-structure changes invalidate the pattern. Material, frequency, load-step, or state changes invalidate numeric values only when they actually affect them. Multiple load cases may reuse an operator; nonlinear iterations may reuse a pattern while replacing values. Assembly produces deterministic, canonical contribution records and composes them into one shared sparse representation. Structural, thermal, electromagnetic, acoustic, and fluid families must not create private CSR variants or separate sparse merge rules.

Three sparse representations remain deliberately distinct: MATLAB-facing sparse values, which implement language-visible value semantics; portable execution sparse values and chunked numerical artifacts, which implement transport and persistence; and the canonical analysis operator, which implements numerical semantics and efficient application. Conversions are explicit, validated adapters. `runmat-analysis-fea` does not depend on `runmat-value`, and a live solver operator is never defined by runtime `Value` or MATLAB storage behavior. Transport encodings may use CSC while an operator uses CSR or block CSR; that is not duplication when each has one documented owner. The adapter contract is typed on both sides. Its runtime side accepts `ValueFact` plus borrowed or owned `runmat-value` storage; its analysis side accepts the canonical analysis scalar class, dimensions, layout, index width, and ownership mode. Admission either proves a zero-copy borrow/move, performs and records a conversion, or returns a typed incompatibility. It never silently narrows precision, drops a complex component, changes index width, gathers a distributed value, or transfers between host and device.

Physics assembly returns a `DiscreteOperator`, not a CPU, GPU, or distributed solver object. A typed `LinearSolvePlan` then selects a compatible algorithm, preconditioner, tolerance policy, precision policy, and restart policy. Preparation produces one of: a host prepared operator; an accelerator-provider-owned prepared operator; or a distributed prepared operator over an explicit partition and worker-group epoch. Backend modules implement the same operator and solve contracts. They do not duplicate formulation logic, constraint semantics, convergence policy, or result recovery.

Solver selection is based on declared algebraic properties, not a generic `linear` label: Invalid pairings are rejected before solve. CG is never used for an indefinite multiplier system, Helmholtz operator, Maxwell system, or nonsymmetric CFD operator merely because it is available. Preconditioner setup, reuse, invalidation, application, memory, and evidence are first-class parts of the solve plan.

Real SPD; CG with validated diagonal, incomplete-factorization, or multilevel preconditioning as supported.. Symmetric/Hermitian indefinite; MINRES or an explicitly supported direct method.. Real/complex nonsymmetric; GMRES or another governed Krylov method with restart evidence.. Saddle-point/block system; Block-aware Krylov and Schur-complement preconditioning.. Generalized eigenproblem; Lanczos, LOBPCG, or another residual- and subspace-verified eigensolver.. Nonlinear tangent sequence; A compatible linear method selected per tangent properties, with reuse only when valid..

requirements.title: Operation-level accelerator qualification and honest fallback
requirements.acceptance: Operation-level accelerator qualification and honest fallback requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: Extend `runmat-accelerate-api` with provider-neutral sparse descriptors, opaque sparse handles, capabilities, feasibility queries, and costs. Do not put WGPU objects or `GpuTensorHandle` values into the canonical analysis operator. The accelerator provider owns device buffers and exposes only capability-checked operations. Native CUDA sparse libraries and WGPU implementations may sit behind that same operation contract. Provider-owned native device context and buffer export can avoid redundant copies, but it is an implementation seam rather than a second FEA accelerator API. FEA must not directly own CUDA contexts, streams, allocation, or WGPU devices. The initial sparse operation surface includes: pattern and numeric-value upload with separate reuse lifetimes; real and complex CSR matrix-vector and matrix-multivector products; dot products, norms, reductions, and fused Krylov vector updates; sparse triangular application when natively supported; preconditioner setup and application; supported index widths, block forms, scalar types, and transpose/adjoint modes; allocation, scratch, cancellation, concurrency, and transactional-result behavior; and truthful operation-level timing, transfer, synchronization, and fallback evidence. Provider defaults return unsupported. They never download, execute on the host, and re-upload while reporting successful GPU execution. Fallback may occur only through the shared placement decision before result commitment and must record the reason and the operations that actually ran.

GPU capability is promoted by operation and solver envelope, not as one boolean claim: resident vector operations and reductions; native sparse matrix-vector application; a complete real-SPD Krylov path; a useful production preconditioner path; complex sparse operations and compatible Krylov methods; nonsymmetric, indefinite, and block systems; accelerator assembly and recovery where measurements justify them; and multi-accelerator execution only after single-worker GPU execution is mature. Each promoted envelope governs precision, maximum host synchronizations, transfer bytes, device-resident work ratio, setup cost, iteration time, memory use, convergence, and CPU-reference equivalence. Moving completed arrays to a device or running only vector updates there is not a GPU solve.

Local parallelism uses execution-resource-aware, scoped pools. It must not depend on an unconstrained global thread pool or oversubscribe CPUs through nested sweep, assembly, BLAS, solver, and provider concurrency. Plans account for memory bandwidth, bounded contribution buffers, accelerator queues, and NUMA where material. Deterministic mode fixes contribution and reduction order; throughput mode may use tolerance-governed reductions and records that policy.

requirements.title: Layered identity and closed chunked numerical artifacts
requirements.acceptance: Layered identity and closed chunked numerical artifacts requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: Use distinct canonical identities for: authored problem; semantic analysis sequence and procedure step; upstream state and state transition; discretized problem and solver mesh; constraint plan; operator structure; operator numeric values; numerical solve plan; observation and accuracy plan; execution and partition plan; attempt and worker-group epoch; and published result and evidence. CPU and GPU may realize the same numerical solve plan. Worker count, partition layout, placement, queue, and retry never change the authored or discretized identities, but they are mandatory execution evidence. Solver tolerances and algorithms belong to numerical-plan identity. Provider/device identity belongs to execution evidence unless the authored policy explicitly requests a provider-specific numerical envelope.

Reuse the meshing system's architectural pattern of typed workloads, closed manifests, immutable content-addressed objects, chunking, verified transfer, retry proofs, and fenced publication. Do not duplicate its domain-specific types. Meshes, operator patterns and values, partition maps, fields, semantic states, histories, observations, accuracy evidence, preconditioner checkpoints, and solver checkpoints use manifest-plus-chunk objects with: a logical digest independent of physical chunk boundaries; typed media and schema contracts; bounded chunk and total sizes; partial and partition-local access; complete closure validation; resumable verified transfer; ownership and lineage evidence; and explicit retention and reuse policy. Large matrices and result fields are never passed as ordinary inline task values or forced through the driver. Full-resolution results remain canonical artifacts; plotting and Desktop consume partial fields or separately identified visualization products without replacing the canonical numerical result.

requirements.title: Governed resource admission and scalable FEA lifecycles
requirements.acceptance: Governed resource admission and scalable FEA lifecycles requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: Resource admission occurs again after meshing and analysis projection, when DOF count, nonzero count, constraint structure, contact candidates, requested observations, field sizes, and partition quality are known: Plans estimate host and device resident bytes, pattern and value bytes, vectors, factorization or preconditioner fill, temporary assembly buffers, state/result/checkpoint size, observation recovery and sampling work, reduction collectives, history volume, halo volume, wall time, artifact bytes, egress, and relay use. Infeasible work fails or replans before expensive assembly. All estimates and actual usage feed the existing RunMat resource and placement evidence.

Local CPU admission discovers usable host capacity and respects explicit worker/thread limits. All worker slots share an aggregate CPU and memory budget; sweep fanout and nested numerical parallelism cannot multiply it. Meshing and numerical kernels reuse bounded persistent worker pools with declared stack and scratch demand, efficiently sleeping while idle. Parallel read-only evaluation and owned mutations preserve physical acceptance, deterministic reductions, cancellation and error propagation. Retain identical-input core-count and size-series measurements before claiming throughput scaling; CPU reservation alone proves no speedup.

Assembly, solve, recovery, publication and cold replay declare the original retained inventories and temporary storage that coexist in each phase. Charge live capacities, copies, sparse support, values, point history, codec materialization and transport buffers at their actual ownership boundaries before allocation. A decode workspace estimate is not a typed heap measurement or an encoding workspace estimate. Release reservations only when their original owned inventory is released. Failed admission leaves prior reservations and visible artifacts intact; success cannot depend on uncharged allocations or inflated ceilings.

Geometry, solver mesh, sparse support, compiled physical inputs and source artifacts are reused through governed immutable ownership when their identities and lifetimes agree. Avoid cloning complete inventories for each mode, field, sweep entry, accepted increment or publication adapter. Recover requested outputs in bounded partitions and retain complete original state required for continuation. Reuse never skips source authentication, revision fencing, physical acceptance or complete field bindings; hashing alone does not independently verify a result.

Geometric recovery, location and local topology queries declare their search work and retained state. Repeated local queries use maintained incidence, local traversal or conservative spatial candidates instead of repeatedly scanning the full inventory when locality permits it. Candidate pruning preserves exact predicates, degeneracy handling, deterministic ordering and topology validity. Index construction, mutation, rollback and cycle history remain accounted and cancellable. If a global traversal is necessary, its necessity, frequency and cost are explicit and evidenced; no search-budget exemption is implied. A bounded scheduling window cannot starve other unresolved sources or be treated as exhaustive failure. Cooperative size/shape convergence retains its accepted working state and valid indexes; unavoidable complete handoffs have explicit triggers and measured frequency. Rejection reuse binds the full local topology, metric and protected-boundary dependencies or invalidates conservatively. Useful accepted progress, rejected-candidate work and complete-state reconstructions are measured together. Synthetic scheduling priorities verify scheduling only, not physical convergence. Automatic geometric sizing retains the measured physical directions of curvature, feature and gap constraints. Repeated samples cannot invent additional density in unrelated directions. Conservative source envelopes state their scope and approximation limits; constructive geometric and physical acceptance remain independent.

For each claimed implementation envelope, retain size-series evidence for governing input dimensions: nodes, elements, nonzeros, boundaries, constraints, integration points, modes, increments, sweep entries and coupled histories as applicable. State the algorithmic work and storage model, distinguish unavoidable mathematical costs from duplicate work, and compare predicted demand with measured phase usage and work counts. Evidence identifies sources, backend, measurement method and shared inventory reuse. A small fixture, one successful study or one process sample does not establish scalability; applicable regressions remain open until growth and numerical equivalence are assessed.

Local, native, durable, remote, partitioned and claimed accelerator paths enforce the same physical identities and resource controls. Expensive preparation, hashing, serialization, index construction, assembly and recovery have bounded work and cancellation checkpoints, including failure diagnostics. Cancellation and resource exhaustion preserve transactional publication and accepted state. Cold field inspection loads only its admitted retained data and does not rerun the solver. Optimizations use shared domain owners rather than a guide-specific solver, codec, scheduler or admission path.

requirements.title: Typed numerical accuracy acceptance and bounded refinement
requirements.acceptance: Typed numerical accuracy acceptance and bounded refinement requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: A converged algebraic solve is not automatically an accurate engineering result. Every procedure step therefore owns a typed `AccuracyPlan` and publishes an `AccuracyReport`. These coordinate existing family-specific controls without pretending that unlike error measures can always be collapsed into one rigorous scalar bound. An authored accuracy plan may declare: target quantities or observations whose accuracy matters; absolute and relative tolerances with physical dimensions where applicable; required estimator, convergence-study, balance, or residual evidence; maximum admissible spatial, temporal, frequency, coupling, modal-truncation, stochastic, transfer, interpolation, recovery, and algebraic contributions; deterministic or tolerance-bounded execution equivalence; action when evidence is unavailable or a limit is exceeded: refine, tighten, extend, warn under an explicitly non-production policy, or fail; and resource ceilings that bound automatic refinement or solver tightening. The resulting report attributes, where applicable: geometry-admission and boundary-approximation evidence; mesh quality and spatial discretization estimates; linear residual and conditioning evidence; nonlinear residual, increment, complementarity, and load-step evidence; time-integration or frequency-sampling evidence; modal residual, basis truncation, correlation, residual-mode, and missing-mass evidence; stochastic sampling or spectral-integration evidence; interface projection, field transfer, and coupled-iteration closure; observation recovery, interpolation, sampling, and reduction evidence; and precision, reduction-order, backend, and placement-equivalence evidence.

Each contribution retains its own norm, units, estimator assumptions, scope, and provenance. The system does not add dimensionally or statistically incompatible values into a decorative “total error.” It instead evaluates a typed acceptance predicate, identifies the governing unmet criterion, and distinguishes: `Satisfied`: every mandatory criterion has passing evidence; `NotSatisfied`: at least one mandatory criterion failed; `Indeterminate`: required evidence is unavailable or does not bound the requested quantity; and `NotApplicable`: a contribution is provably irrelevant to this procedure. Publication requires `Satisfied`, or `Indeterminate` under an explicit markIndeterminate policy with visible evidence. `Indeterminate` cannot silently pass because the solver residual is small, and `NotSatisfied` always blocks publication. Accuracy planning is staged. Before meshing it can choose a formulation, order, initial mesh policy, time/frequency sampling, modal range, and solver class. After topology projection it updates resource and error estimates. During solve it may perform bounded, checkpointed refinement or tolerance changes when the authored policy permits them. It may never relax a requested criterion to fit resources. If the goal is infeasible under the resource ceiling, planning or execution returns an attributable failure.

Target-quantity accuracy integrates with typed observations. A target must be computable on the current formulation and carry a valid recovery and sampling policy. Adaptive analysis consumes the same accuracy plan rather than defining a parallel convergence authority. Coupled studies retain both per-family contributions and interface/global closure; one passing component cannot hide another failing component. Accuracy identity includes target quantities, tolerances, estimators, refinement/tightening actions, stopping policy, and any numerical choices capable of changing the accepted result. Placement and worker layout remain evidence unless the authored numerical-equivalence policy makes them mathematically relevant. Required governed cases include: a tight algebraic solve on an under-resolved mesh being rejected or refined rather than accepted; spatial refinement reducing a validated estimator and target-quantity change at the expected rate; time-step, frequency-grid, modal-basis, and coupling tolerances independently governing acceptance; interpolation or transfer error blocking an otherwise converged coupled result; `Indeterminate` when a requested quantity lacks a valid estimator or convergence study; bounded automatic refinement respecting cancellation, checkpoint, retry, and resource ceilings; and equivalent acceptance decisions across inline, remote, partitioned, CPU, and claimed GPU execution.

requirements.title: Truthful future derivative and compiled-law seams
requirements.acceptance: Truthful future derivative and compiled-law seams requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: The completion scope does not include general optimization, inverse analysis, uncertainty quantification, topology optimization, arbitrary user elements, or arbitrary executable constitutive laws. The architecture must nevertheless avoid closing off two valuable RunMat integrations. First, authored models and observations retain a typed parameter-dependency graph. A future design-study layer can identify bounded design variables, uncertain inputs, response functions, objectives, and design constraints without parsing strings or inspecting solver internals. Each operator, state transition, and observation may declare derivative support as an enum such as analytic tangent, automatic differentiation compatible, governed numerical difference, or unavailable. This is capability metadata, not a claim that gradients or optimization are implemented. Ordinary sweeps and independent parameter samples remain in the present production scope and reuse the existing task, artifact, cache, and cluster infrastructure. Second, state-dependent executable laws retain the separate compiled-law boundary described above. Their future ABI must make typed state, outputs, consistent derivatives, purity/effects, checkpointing, CPU/GPU/distributed capability, and verification explicit. Neither future seam permits a live RunMat callback inside assembly, recovery, an iterative solve, or a distributed rank.

requirements.title: Exact pre-solve admission and truthful realization identity
requirements.acceptance: Exact pre-solve admission and truthful realization identity requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: Fix standalone thermal persistence classification. Fix backend/device provenance and typed fallback reporting. Correct misleading field names and semantics. Separate the admitted formulation from numerical quality and publication status. Centralize pre-assembly formulation admission. Resolve the typed family, procedure, solution space, model, and mesh through one registry into an opaque admitted formulation receipt. Only that receipt may construct persisted run identity; callers cannot manufacture or mutate an identity. Record the exact realization that executed, including spatial element/operator formulation, temporal integration, constitutive update, coupling transfer, field recovery, topology source, source projection, and boundary projection. Distinguish Tet4, Tet10, beam, shell, synthetic structural operators, inferred lattices, generated graphs, reduced channels, adjacency recovery, and resampled/profile transfers rather than hiding them behind broad family labels. Add typed admission failures for unregistered formulations, noncanonical topology or projection, malformed/unsupported connectivity, unsupported mixed-dimensional assembly, unmapped sources, missing interfaces, incompatible procedures, and unqualified recovery or transfer.
