Reject before solver progress or artifact publication.

Replace the conflated profile/run-kind model with clean family and procedure contracts. A typed per-procedure-step execution plan selects backend and solver options; it does not duplicate the step's family/procedure/solution-space identity or derive solver identity from a model template. Split constraints, natural/Robin boundaries, connectors, interfaces, and gauges into their typed authored models. Add typed region targets, reference points, coordinate frames, family DOFs, dimensioned values, and schedules. Add typed signal, excitation, excitation-case, initial-condition, response-spectrum, and combination contracts; distinguish modal extraction from every forced-response procedure. Add typed analysis-sequence, procedure-step, state-input/output, transition, activation, branch, and restart contracts; keep them distinct from execution tasks. Add typed field, history, probe, reduction, monitor, diagnostic, sampling, retention, and accuracy contracts. Replace duplicated family time profiles and embedded amplitude/phase conventions in the target schema; define the clean breaking migration rather than retaining parallel authorities. Replace the YAML authoring surface with the `.fea` language in the canonical typed declarative language contract as one clean breaking migration. Reconcile that schema field by field against the true document, core, runtime, CLI, Desktop, identity, execution, result, persistence, and evidence surfaces before removing any current behavior. Remove obsolete compatibility code and string-dispatched domain choices. Every current operation identifies its formulation truthfully. No proxy can be mistaken for a physical discretization.

Admission either returns a registry-issued exact formulation receipt or fails before solve; a forged, incompatible, or unregistered identity is rejected on decode and persistence. Numerical acceptance and publication are distinct. Physical-discretization receipts cannot contain inferred lattices, generated graphs, implicit channels, synthetic profiles/operators, DOF-adjacency recovery, pair-spring shells, ordinal source placement, or heuristic/resampled interface transfer. Persistence and trend grouping use correct identities. Invalid cross-family, DOF, value-dimension, frame, and target combinations fail at the typed boundary. Invalid signal domains, physical quantities, units, interpolation policies, excitation targets, modal/SRS combinations, and nonportable generator declarations fail at the typed boundary. Invalid procedure transitions, upstream state kinds, step activation, observation locations/reductions, and dimensional accuracy requests fail at the typed boundary. Existing supported documents are migrated through one clean schema path, without dual old/new runtime implementations. The prerequisite platform baseline remains intact and Stage 0 introduces no copied or partially merged RM-1064 implementation.

requirements.title: One shared topology, numerical and property authority
requirements.acceptance: One shared topology, numerical and property authority requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: Implement and test the shared analysis projection. Implement one canonical property compiler from authored, geometry-resolved material/composite, section, layup, and orientation intent to an element-complete compiled property map. Bind its semantic digest to geometry revision and topology, keep audit evidence separate, and expose role/capability-specific immutable views rather than family-private lookup inventories. Implement typed constraint-target resolution and canonical constraint-plan compilation. Implement shared signal interpolation, breakpoint/extrapolation rules, derivative-consistent kinematics, spatial excitation realization, projection/conservation evidence, and family admissibility validation. Implement shared sparse constraint rows, affine reduction, multiplier, null-space, rank, and reaction mappings. Replace family-private matrix representations with the canonical sparse pattern, values, contribution, and operator contracts. Add typed operator properties and solver/preconditioner compatibility validation. Extend the generic accelerator API with sparse descriptors, opaque handles, feasibility, operations, and costs; unsupported remains the default. Implement and verify the serial CPU reference backend before any accelerator or distributed promotion. Implement shared observation target resolution, sampling, typed derived-operation validation, partition-local reduction, bounded history, and canonical publication contracts. Implement the study-level accuracy plan, contribution evidence, acceptance states, and family extension hooks without creating a second adaptive-convergence authority. Add post-projection numerical/resource planning and early admission or repartition decisions, including observation and bounded-accuracy work.

Move flow topology from runtime into analysis. Move acoustic, CFD, CHT, and FSI kernels out of runtime. Split runtime operations, documents, persistence, presentation, and policy. Split FEA topology, algebra, constraints, excitation, physics, orchestration, execution, results, and diagnostics. Add architecture tests for dependency direction, prohibited physics ownership in runtime, and prohibited runtime callable/value dependencies in analysis solvers. Remove superseded modules and duplicate rules, including family-private property lookup, coefficient averaging, schedule, and time-profile implementations. All geometry-dependent families consume the same projection. Runtime contains no element, cell, flux, constitutive, or coupling kernels. Region and boundary resolution has one implementation. Property selection and coverage have one compiler. Every active material-bearing element has one compatible homogeneous or composite constitutive owner plus every required section and orientation; gaps, overlaps, stale/empty scopes, wrong roles, missing capabilities, and geometry/topology substitution fail before assembly. No promoted operator, recovery path, coupling, or diagnostic derives constitutive coefficients from declaration order, global material averages, implicit defaults, importer confidence, or a family-private region matcher. Compiled property semantics and coefficients are invariant under authored ordering, partitioning, serialization, and supported execution placement. Constraint kinds, DOFs, frames, pairing, and enforcement are typed through the solver boundary. Signals, excitation targets, quantities, units, interpolation, activation, and spatial realization are typed through the solver boundary, with no live callback or duplicated family schedule authority.

Empty, conflicting, redundant, overconstrained, and underconstrained plans produce attributable diagnostics. Every promoted solver consumes the same canonical operator contract and rejects algebraically incompatible algorithms. Runtime sparse values, execution sparse values, and analysis operators have explicit one-way adapters and no ownership leakage. Field recovery, observation evaluation, plotting, and accuracy acceptance have distinct owners and no duplicated quantity/reduction logic. Distributed observations use partition ownership and governed collectives rather than driver-side full-field gathering. Resource estimates are checked against actual allocations before assembly begins. Structural preflight distinguishes topology-only stiffness upper bounds from the exact prepared operator: exhaustion of a bounded coercivity proof on the upper-bound pattern is indeterminate, not proof that the prepared operator is inadmissible. A supported envelope needs separately justified early admission and exact-operator solve evidence; neither a false-negative symbolic gate nor a silent post-assembly failure satisfies this gate. Module size and dependency checks prevent the known god-file structure from returning.

requirements.title: Physical linear solid operators, loads and assigned-material recovery
requirements.acceptance: Physical linear solid operators, loads and assigned-material recovery must satisfy all applicable supported-envelope criteria. Independent physical, semantic, accuracy, resource and publication evidence are separate; missing, failed or indeterminate mandatory evidence prevents acceptance.

obligations.criterion: Complete Tet4 verification and retain it as the initial serial reference. Complete Tet10 volume and face quadrature, recovery, stress extrapolation/projection, pressure loading, and estimator support. Assemble consistent mass and a documented optional lumped mass from density and geometry.

Implement documented damping inputs, initially Rayleigh damping where applicable. Integrate body forces by region, material density, shape function, and volume. Implement nonzero prescribed displacement with correct elimination or lifting and reaction recovery.

Make stress, strain, energy, and derived-field recovery use each element's assigned material. Define treatment of discontinuous stress at material interfaces. Preserve exact force and moment resultants for distributed surface and wrench loads.

Realize constant and parameterized static excitations through the shared signal/excitation path rather than a formulation-private load vector. Detect rigid modes, inadequate constraint, inversion, poor conditioning, and unsupported element types with typed diagnostics.

dependencies: Shared typed authoring, canonical topology/material/constraint/excitation authorities; governed resources and execution; independently qualified accuracy and semantic publication.

requirements.title: Physical three-dimensional beams and explicit mixed-model coupling
requirements.acceptance: Physical three-dimensional beams and explicit mixed-model coupling must satisfy all applicable supported-envelope criteria. Independent physical, semantic, accuracy, resource and publication evidence are separate; missing, failed or indeterminate mandatory evidence prevents acceptance.

obligations.criterion: Retain the real three-dimensional beam formulation and verify transformation, shear/bending assumptions, mass, and section recovery. Define explicit node/constraint coupling between beams, shells, and solids. Assemble mixed models into one global degree-of-freedom system.
Reject incompatible or disconnected couplings. Add frame, cantilever, torsion, and mixed solid-beam benchmarks.

dependencies: Shared typed authoring, canonical topology/material/constraint/excitation authorities; governed resources and execution; independently qualified accuracy and semantic publication.

requirements.title: Physical membrane and bending shells

Frequency fanout is not distributed linear algebra and host fallback is not accelerator execution. Publish supported envelopes, documentation, examples and release evidence.

obligations.criterion: Exact frequency fan-in preserves all original entries, roots, pressure/velocity fields and metadata independent of completion order or chunking, rejecting missing, duplicate or substituted entries.

Cold full/partial complex reads use exact sample and original partitions without solver reruns, nearest-frequency selection or aggregate-as-single-state substitution; corruption and incomplete roots reject.

Worker rederivation rejects altered workload/uniqueness controls or understated storage/work plans before work; original authored ceilings remain enforced. Whole-task measured peak usage, cancellation and terminal accounting match claimed envelopes.

Every claimed execution placement has actual end-to-end equivalence, failure/cancellation and resource evidence. Durable producer termination, encrypted remote and partitioned/GPU behavior receive separate proof rather than local transport/fanout credit.
Release evidence and usable examples document supported boundaries, sources, material/mesh/frequency limits, diagnostics and accuracy; all blocking release criteria pass before advertisement.

dependencies: Shared execution, immutable objects, authenticated completion, bounded readers and release gates remain mandatory.

requirements.title: Canonical conservative finite-volume projection
requirements.acceptance: Flow uses complete canonical tetrahedral control-volume geometry and exact cell/face authority. Meshes outside validated geometry and quality limits are rejected; no channel reduction substitutes for the original domain.

obligations.criterion: Retain canonical cell identities, complete reciprocal cell-face incidence, owner/neighbour, oriented area vectors, cell volumes/centroids, centroid distances, interpolation weights, non-orthogonality/skewness metrics and exact original boundary provenance.

Projection is deterministic under reordered source access and placement; oriented surfaces satisfy the divergence theorem and exact source/region ownership. Cache identity binds the original mesh and projection policy.

Admit supported tetrahedral order/geometry and governed non-orthogonality/skewness limits before work. Reject inversion, degeneracy, unsupported curvature, nonmanifold/missing/ambiguous boundaries or mutated source geometry; never silently reduce the model.
Count construction inventory and checked scratch/traversal work before allocation; exact ceilings, overflow and cancellation govern topology work.

requirements.title: Original incompressible laminar mass and momentum equations
requirements.acceptance: The supported initial flow envelope is incompressible, Newtonian, laminar and single phase. Steady and transient operators conserve original mass and momentum, use documented interpolation/stabilization and governed skew/non-orthogonal corrections, and solve pressure-velocity coupling with admissible shared nonsymmetric algebra.

obligations.criterion: Evaluate one original oriented owner-face mass flux and conservative advective, viscous and pressure momentum actions with equal/opposite internal-face contributions. Document interpolation, stabilization and non-orthogonal/skewness corrections within validated mesh limits.

Pressure-velocity coupling solves original incompressibility and momentum equations. Component gauges/nullspaces are explicit, invalid or incompatible references reject, and physical residual checks cannot be replaced by solver convergence. Incompressibility is part of the mixed fluid formulation, never a generic user-authored equality constraint.

Keep original reference-relative pressure as governing state through iteration, recovery and cold execution. Absolute pressure is a projection; converting it back must not erase fluctuations. Bind pressure references and retain owner-face flux rather than reconstructing missing original state.

dependencies: Shared canonical topology, exact material assignment and general sparse solver/resource authorities.

requirements.title: Exact typed fluid boundaries, sources and initial conditions
requirements.acceptance: Fluid cell domains, exact boundary regions, material laws, constraints, sources and initial fields are typed original authority. Shared spatial/time signal realization preserves declared flow and momentum resultants and rejects wrong-dimensional, absent, ambiguous, conflicting or incompatible bindings.

obligations.criterion: Implement component velocity, tangential moving-wall, symmetry, periodic and pressure-reference constraints plus inlet velocity, outlet pressure and mass-flow boundaries on exact regions. Reject unsupported normal wall motion unless a qualified ALE formulation governs it.

Use shared typed signals for inlet velocity, pressure, mass flow, wall motion and body acceleration. Realize space/time dependence conservatively, preserving declared mass/momentum resultants over whole boundaries, cells and partitions with explicit sign/frame conventions and event sidedness.

Resolve model-owned reusable initial velocity and pressure/reference fields on exact cell scope from one typed finite uniform value, exact non-frequency signal sample with coordinate/discontinuity side, or immutable complete field artifact. Check content, topology, quantity, shape and explicit vector frame. Study binding selects the consuming step; compatible upstream state takes precedence unless a typed replacement policy applies, and conflicts reject. Validate face flux and constraint/gauge consistency before transient execution; no fabricated terminal profile or inferred extremal boundary authority.
Reject missing/multiply matched/wrong-dimension material, cell, source or boundary authority, quantity conflicts, stale input and exceeded input realization budgets before numerical execution.

dependencies: Shared typed materials, cell-domain realization, constraints, excitations and initial-condition authority.

requirements.title: Physical transient integration and original cold chronology
requirements.acceptance: Transient flow integrates original fluid inertia and pressure-velocity evolution over actual intervals. Immutable original cell velocity, pressure reference/fluctuation and owner-face flux govern cold continuation; schedules, events, work limits and outputs retain their original chronology.

obligations.criterion: Integrate actual momentum time derivatives rather than return a terminal steady profile; initial state and step interval bind the original inertial operator.
Show temporal convergence independently of spatial error on a nontrivial transient reference, including a transient vortex; report field error and conservative balance.

Preserve complete original interval state, scheduled observations, one-sided discontinuities, predecessor order and cumulative admitted work. Reject reordered/substituted state, invalid intervals, budgets and cancellation without accepting a suffix.

After actual native producer termination a fresh consumer resumes original transient fields and outputs without producer memory; split and uninterrupted histories agree within the governed accuracy envelope.

dependencies: Mandatory independent transient accuracy, admitted task resources and compatible complete state publication.

requirements.title: Original fluid fields and physical conservation recovery
requirements.acceptance: Recover original cell and face pressure, velocity, flux, stress and wall quantities consistently, retaining exact boundary ownership and signed mass/momentum balance. Acceptance includes original equation residual, continuity, constitutive face-flux closure and global/per-cell/per-boundary physical balance.

obligations.criterion: Retain original cell fields and owner-face flux; recover face traces, stresses and wall quantities with declared location, units, frames and sign conventions. Cold consumers validate original source and reject changed fields/tractions rather than silently re-solving them.

Report global, per-cell and per-boundary signed mass and momentum components from original forces/fluxes with physical normalization. Algebraic residual convergence alone cannot pass physical acceptance.

requirements.title: Independent flow benchmark and convergence acceptance
requirements.acceptance: Flow requires independent Poiseuille, Couette, lid-driven cavity, backward-facing-step references within the declared Reynolds range, a transient vortex, spatial/time convergence and conservation. Every mandatory accuracy criterion must be satisfied by applicable current evidence before publication; a missing independent discretization bound remains open.

obligations.criterion: Validate Poiseuille and Couette plus lid-driven cavity and backward-facing step across the documented Reynolds range, with velocity/pressure/flow/wall quantities and conservative closure.

Demonstrate spatial convergence and absolute error for non-affine flow, pressure, integrated flow and wall stress within the documented quality/Reynolds envelope; affine exactness alone does not establish convergence.

Shared accuracy assessment consumes original result, receipts and applicable independent spatial/time evidence. Missing, failed or indeterminate mandatory criteria block completed semantic publication; imported provenance cannot create numerical proof.

dependencies: References are independent of the operator under test; original meshes, tolerances and caps remain mandatory.

requirements.title: Governed fluid execution and semantic publication
requirements.acceptance: Fluid execution retains original equations and fields across supported placement, admitted resources and immutable publication. Serial correctness precedes partitioned cell assembly and distributed linear algebra. Every remote, distributed or accelerator claim requires direct applicable execution and equivalence evidence; host fallback or fanout is not that evidence.

obligations.criterion: Admit original projection, source/initial realization, pressure/momentum operators, solver work, retained histories/outputs and transport before execution; cancellation and exact ceilings reject safely. Measured whole-process/backend usage must support claimed resource envelopes; requested bytes are not RSS.

Implement partitioned cell assembly after verified serial equations, then distributed linear algebra. Preserve original boundary/source flow and momentum resultants and numerical fields across serial/native/durable/encrypted-remote/partitioned/claimed-accelerator execution with supported precision and authenticated lifecycle.

Publish original complete state, observations, receipts and mandatory accuracy evidence atomically under exact source/phase lineage. Failed or partial imports cannot install completed authority. Include supported-envelope documentation and reproducible release evidence; no implicit channel fallback.

dependencies: Shared immutable artifacts, task admission, state/observation/accuracy authorities and attested release/documentation.
Conjugate heat transfer requires separately qualified thermal and fluid operators and conservative exact-interface closure; fluid evidence alone cannot qualify the coupled system.

requirements.title: Typed physical interfaces and conservative transfers
requirements.acceptance: Coupled procedures retain each domain equation, exact admitted geometry identity and revision, distinct conservation law and explicit physical interface law. Numerical enforcement and relaxation belong to typed procedure/solver policy.

obligations.criterion: Resolve exact interface sides with original geometry/revision and deterministic mapping; CHT declares exactly one perfect-transfer, conductance or resistance law; FSI declares physical kinematics. Do not infer terminals or interfaces from coordinate extrema.

Validate matching or nonmatching transfer maps, conservation, error, frame/orientation, units, source/target lineage and state compatibility before consumption. Preserve each side conservation law and original interface evidence.

Two-way policies, executable constitutive laws and future derivative/optimization capability remain explicitly bounded; capability metadata cannot imply implemented coupling, gradients or user-law callbacks inside assembly, recovery, iterative solves or distributed ranks.

requirements.title: Solved-temperature thermoelastic transitions and closure
requirements.acceptance: One-way thermoelasticity consumes a solved thermal field on the same mesh or through a validated map as an explicit typed sequence transition. Temperature reference, projection, thermal strain and complete state lineage remain attributable.

obligations.criterion: Evaluate temperature-dependent properties and thermal strain at integration points using the declared reference temperature and original thermal field; retain transfer error and mechanical equilibrium with thermal balance.

Thermal preload may feed only supported prestressed modal, harmonic and buckling branches after complete physical state, constraints, tangent, transition and mandatory accuracy evidence pass. An initial guess or incomplete checkpoint is not a base state.

Name one-way and two-way policies explicitly. Implement two-way deformation-dependent thermal exchange only inside its supported envelope and iterate to field and energy closure; reject unsupported feedback.

requirements.title: Thermal stress over a time history (thermomechanical transient)
requirements.acceptance: A transient thermal analysis drives the structure at every stored time: stress, strain and displacement publish as a time history from the solved temperature of each step (for example one braking stop), with the thermal and structural time axes and state lineage attributable.

obligations.criterion: Each structural step consumes the solved temperature of the matching thermal time (quasi-static, or with inertia in a structural transient); a uniform temperature ramp in a free bar reproduces alpha * dT expansion at every stored time, and a clamped bar reproduces -E * alpha * dT stress.

Thermal stress under a surface heat pulse on a slab agrees with the classical one-dimensional transient thermoelastic solution (peak surface stress and its time) within the declared tolerance under refinement in space and time.

`thermomechanical transient` checks and runs from `runmat run`, publishes temperature, displacement and stress fields at every stored time, supports peak-over-time outputs and assessments, and snapshots select a time.

dependencies: FEA-COUPLING-THERMOELASTIC-001 (solved-temperature transition) and the thermal transient time axis remain mandatory.

requirements.title: Original Joule-heat transfer and electrical/thermal iteration
requirements.acceptance: Compute Joule heat from solved conduction or electromagnetic fields at elements/integration points and feed the real thermal operator. Resolve authored terminals; iterate temperature-dependent conductivity through a documented policy to electrical residual, thermal residual, field-change and energy closure.

obligations.criterion: Transfer original solved-field Joule density and total power with exact point/element topology, units and authenticated source/target lineage; terminal electrical power and supplied thermal power agree.

Update temperature-dependent conductivity and re-solve the actual electrical and thermal equations under documented iteration controls; retain electrical residual, thermal residual, field change and energy closure for every accepted coupled state.

Cold transfer authenticates the complete original electrical result and intended thermal consumer before use; reject foreign lineage, altered power/inventory, unsupported equations, feedback and release intent.

requirements.title: Thermal/fluid conjugate heat transfer
requirements.acceptance: CHT requires independently complete thermal and fluid operators and exact solid/fluid interfaces. Re-solve both domains until interface and global energy closure pass rather than reporting an inferred terminal heat profile.

obligations.criterion: Conservatively transfer temperature and heat flux on exact solid/fluid sides under documented perfect-transfer, conductance or contact-resistance law and numerical relaxation policy.
Re-solve both physical domains to interface and global energy closure, retaining per-iteration interface evidence, failure/cutback chronology and validated spatial/temporal/coupling convergence.
Reject CHT while either standalone operator, transfer, state/resource admission or mandatory accuracy is unqualified; shared signal/source and boundary energy attribution remain intact.

requirements.title: Dynamics/fluid interaction with stable conservative ALE execution
requirements.acceptance: FSI depends on independently complete structural dynamics and CFD. Exact interface mapping conserves traction, velocity and work while a documented mesh-motion/ALE and partitioned iteration policy governs moving domains.

obligations.criterion: Resolve exact interface sides and conservatively transfer traction and velocity with interface action/reaction and work balances; original structural and fluid equations must actually be re-solved.
Document supported mesh-motion/ALE and quality-triggered remeshing, validate transferred temporal/interface state and reject unsupported large motion or topology change explicitly.

Use documented stable partitioned iteration, relaxation and added-mass stabilization; qualify spatial, temporal and coupling-iteration convergence and added-mass-sensitive independent reference cases.

Checkpoint distributed coupling orchestration with whole-task resource admission, cancellation, bounded retry, interface history and publication fencing; release evidence and documentation describe the actually qualified envelope.

requirements.title: Family-appropriate adaptive loops and separately qualified transfer
requirements.acceptance: Family-appropriate adaptive loops and separately qualified transfer must satisfy all applicable supported-envelope criteria. Independent physical, semantic, accuracy, resource and publication evidence are separate; missing, failed or indeterminate mandatory evidence prevents acceptance.

obligations.criterion: Estimators must be formulation-appropriate and validated; a structural stress estimator is not a universal estimator. Adaptation decisions use stable identities and canonical evidence. Tet4/Tet10 order changes preserve correct field and integration-point state.

Plastic, contact, coupled-interface, and temporal state transfer must be separately validated before adaptation is enabled for those families. Topology change alone never constitutes convergence. Iteration limits, resource budgets, cancellation, retry, and publication fencing apply to the full loop.

Compose solve, family recovery, estimation, canonical marking, h/p adaptation, new mesh/lineage validation, primary field/history transfer, measured transfer error, resolve and estimator/target convergence into a governed continue/converge/reject orchestrator.

dependencies: Shared typed authoring, canonical topology/material/constraint/excitation authorities; governed resources and execution; independently qualified accuracy and semantic publication.

requirements.title: Accuracy-driven adaptation, persistent constraints and durable lineage
requirements.acceptance: Accuracy-driven adaptation, persistent constraints and durable lineage must satisfy all applicable supported-envelope criteria. Independent physical, semantic, accuracy, resource and publication evidence are separate; missing, failed or indeterminate mandatory evidence prevents acceptance.

obligations.criterion: Compose adaptive loops for each formulation with a validated estimator. Validate field and state transfer. Rebuild constraint plans from persistent identities and validate constraint-plan lineage after every h- or p-change.

Integrate adaptation graphs with durable and remote execution. Publish iteration lineage and target-quantity convergence in results. Drive stopping and acceptance through the shared accuracy plan, preserving family estimator evidence rather than inventing a separate adaptive tolerance model.
Add release evidence and documentation. Adaptation reduces the governed estimator and converges the selected target quantity. Transfer error remains below family-specific limits.
Constraint targets, relations, reactions, and state remain valid across adaptation. Cancellation, retry, restart, and replay preserve valid iteration lineage.

Constraints bind to persistent geometry and topology identities rather than incidental node numbers. After h- or p-adaptation, the analysis projection rebuilds the canonical constraint plan, checks target coverage and pairing, transfers necessary state, and records old/new plan lineage.

dependencies: Shared typed authoring, canonical topology/material/constraint/excitation authorities; governed resources and execution; independently qualified accuracy and semantic publication.

requirements.title: Complete supported surface and dependency promotion
requirements.acceptance: All named formulations complete their full acceptance gates within documented supported envelopes, using the required dependency and promotion order.

obligations.criterion: The supported surface comprises Tet4/Tet10 linear solids, three-dimensional beams, membrane/bending shells and deliberate mixed assembly; eigenmodes and prestressed modes; modal transient/harmonic, response-spectrum correlation/missing-mass and random PSD/cross-PSD response; eigenvalue buckling and prestressed direct/modal harmonic response from compatible converged state; direct transient/harmonic dynamics; geometric nonlinearity, supported plastic laws and frictionless/frictional contact; steady/transient conduction with supported sources and radiation; electrostatics, conduction, magnetostatics, harmonic multi-frequency and transient Maxwell and saturating magnetics; harmonic, modal and transient acoustics with impedance, radiation, transmission loss, intensity and structure-borne sound; steady/transient incompressible laminar flow with generalized-Newtonian, viscoelastic, porous, species, free-surface, rotating-frame, lubrication, electrokinetic, particle, low-Mach, compressible laminar and network physics; thermoelastic, electrothermal, conjugate heat transfer and two-way FSI; adaptation with validated family estimators and transfer. Every formulation runs through one thread plan, remotely and with domain decomposition, and independently satisfies all shared and family acceptance. No unsupported combination silently selects a reduced model.

Turbulence (RANS, LES, DES), perfectly matched layers, boundary elements, acoustic mean flow, antennas, waveguide ports, motors, piezoelectricity, fracture, fatigue, hexahedral, wedge and pyramid elements, view-factor radiation and arbitrary material models are outside the supported surface. They are rejected with typed diagnostics and the site makes no claim about them. Advertising any of them requires a new requirement with its own envelope and independent qualification; a future extension seam grants no implemented capability.

Each family follows authored-contract validation, frozen generated-input materialization, canonical mesh projection, typed property/constraint/source compilation, physical discretization and assembly, compatible numerical solution, physical field recovery, typed observation evaluation, accuracy evidence, governed publication and persistence. No stage has duplicate authoritative implementations or reaches backward into private host/syntax structures.

Converge the public platform baseline first and establish truthful contracts before parallel nonoverlapping work. Shared topology and algebra precede physical families. Linear structures plus semantic state transitions precede base-state linearization, buckling and prestressed modal/harmonic work. Constituent solvers meet their own gates before thermoelastic, electrothermal, conjugate heat transfer or FSI qualification. FSI additionally requires structural dynamics. Observations and shared accuracy acceptance precede final family promotion. Each adaptive family requires its validated estimator and state transfer. Duplicate ownership blocks family promotion even when numerical work begins behind stable interfaces.

Canonical topology and constraints precede canonical sparse operators/patterns, a verified serial CPU reference, resource-aware shared-memory execution, whole-study remote/independent task distribution, qualified single-accelerator sparse execution, cooperative worker-group/collective contracts, family-specific distributed algebra and justified multi-accelerator promotion. Scaling contracts arrive early; partitioned numerical work starts only after a correct serial operator. Fanout, host fallback, data transfers and metadata alone establish none of the downstream numerical gates.

Implementation work stays in the analysis checkout and uses the private platform checkout only for required Desktop/Server integration. The separately owned active general RunMat checkout must not be read, modified, built, formatted, tested, committed or otherwise disturbed. Unrelated private-platform changes are never included in an FEA slice.

dependencies: Each registered family and shared authority is independently mandatory; no aggregate pass count closes this requirement.

requirements.title: Preserved public platform lineage and qualification gates
requirements.acceptance: Preserved public platform lineage and qualification gates requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: No Stage 0 implementation begins until this prerequisite is complete. Fetch and merge the current public `origin/dev` into the FEA implementation branch. Resolve overlaps by composing both products: retain the complete `origin/dev` CI/release job set, including its job IDs, display names, matrices, dependencies, action versions, and existing steps; preserve all meshing test and release gates; and preserve the strongest native framed-read, cancellation, and request-lifetime semantics. Do not rename jobs or introduce branch-specific job variants. Add or extend only the lanes required by FEA and meshing, and keep them integrated with the dev release graph. Run formatting, architecture checks, the affected native-runner and meshing integration suites, and the release lane. Fix merge regressions before proceeding. Record the merge commit as the FEA platform baseline. Inventory the platform contracts present at that commit and record which RM-1064 contracts are still pending. Use the existing `runmat-types` numeric, shape, storage, layout, and residency vocabulary wherever its current semantics are already exact. Never read or disturb the separately owned active checkout. Use public dev lineage and owner-published contract facts; do not merge or cherry-pick unpublished platform work merely to obtain typed value, parallel, distributed or accelerator capabilities. If FEA later reaches a dependency on unpublished RM-1064 behavior, first look for independent analysis work. Only consider a direct integration checkpoint when its owning workstream declares it green and stable, confirms ancestry-preserving delivery to `dev`, and agrees on the shared contract surface.

Establish recurring convergence gates: fetch and inspect `origin/dev` before each platform-facing Stage 1 or Stage 2 slice, and perform the mandatory final `dev` convergence before distributed or GPU promotion. the FEA implementation branch contains the current public `dev` lineage in a dedicated merge commit. Meshing behavior and release coverage remain intact on the merged platform. CI/release retains the complete `origin/dev` job topology and coverage, with only reviewed, purpose-specific FEA or meshing additions; a workflow diff audit proves no incidental job rename, removal, matrix change, dependency change, action-version drift, or branch-specific variant. The affected workspace, native-runner, meshing integration, architecture, and release checks pass. Shared type, value, execution, artifact, runner, distributed, and accelerator authorities are inventoried with one owner each. No source, patch, dependency, or worktree mutation has been taken from the separate active `./runmat` checkout. Work that depends on pending RM-1064 contracts is identified explicitly and cannot silently create a temporary competing authority.

requirements.title: Independent formulation evidence and truthful claims
requirements.acceptance: Independent formulation evidence and truthful claims requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: Verification is implemented with each family, not postponed until all solvers exist.

Unit and dimensional consistency tests. Element/cell-level operator tests. Rigid-body, null-space, symmetry, definiteness, or conservation invariants as applicable. Analytic or manufactured solutions. Patch tests where applicable. h-, p-, frequency-, nonlinear-step-, or time-step-convergence studies with expected behavior. Boundary/load/source resultant checks. Global and local balance checks. Invalid, ambiguous, degenerate, and unsupported cases. At least one independent solver, trusted literature, standard benchmark, or measured comparison. Local/durable/remote equivalence for any claimed execution shape. Performance and resource evidence over governed representative cases. Typed observation correctness, including location, frame, recovery, sampling, reduction, and partition equivalence. Procedure-sequence and state-transition evidence for any formulation that consumes upstream state. An accuracy report whose mandatory criteria are satisfied, with no unavailable contribution silently accepted. RunMat output cannot be its own independent reference. Existing self-derived “external” baselines must be renamed as regression baselines or replaced with traceable independent data.

Each formulation's evidence is tracked independently: `verified`: governing discretization and internal numerical evidence pass; `validated`: independent comparison passes within the documented use class; `release-gated`: verified, validated, documented, and supported across its claimed execution shapes. Do not claim evidence for an entire broad family when only one formulation has it.

requirements.title: Blocking attested evidence in the existing release graph
requirements.acceptance: Blocking attested evidence in the existing release graph requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: Treat the current `origin/dev` CI and release job set as the baseline. Preserve its job IDs, display names, matrices, dependencies, action versions, and existing coverage; this feature branch must not cause job renames or parallel branch-specific workflow topology. Compose FEA and meshing checks into the appropriate existing jobs. Add a job only when it has a distinct runner, resource, evidence-attestation, or release-blocking responsibility that cannot be expressed safely in an existing lane. Any such addition must depend on and integrate with the dev release graph rather than replace it. Keep fast contract, unit, and small benchmark checks in normal CI. Keep governed integration cases in the existing FEA conformance job, but make its reports family- and formulation-specific. Add a blocking FEA release-evidence job incrementally as formulations reach completion. Make release promotion depend on that job just as it depends on meshing release evidence. Generate, validate, upload, and attest family evidence. Include sequence/state-transition, observation, and accuracy reports in the blocking evidence for every formulation that uses them. Do not add a nightly lane. Avoid a single opaque readiness score. A failed mandatory case blocks only the relevant formulation and any coupled formulation that depends on it, but it blocks their claim completely.

Run the complete governed family corpus. Run all coupling dependency and interface cases. Run the complete cross-family constraint, gauge, reaction, and connector corpus. Run the complete signal, excitation, callable-materialization, SRS/response-spectrum, identity, effect-policy, and spatial-realization corpus. Run the complete semantic sequence, state-transition, activation, branch, continuation, restart, prestress, and buckling corpus. Run the complete field/history/probe/reduction/monitor, sampling, retention, partial-access, and distributed-observation corpus. Run the complete accuracy contribution, acceptance, indeterminate-evidence, bounded-refinement, and resource-ceiling corpus. Run inline, local-process, durable, remote, CPU, and claimed GPU conformance. Run independent-task, cooperative-distributed, and any claimed multi-accelerator conformance separately. Run stable performance, transfer, synchronization, collective, and resource gates. Audit public documentation and capability claims against evidence. Make FEA release evidence a mandatory release dependency. Remove temporary migration tooling, obsolete fixtures, proxy code, and stale documentation. Every planned formulation meets the complete acceptance criteria. The full release lane is green and produces attested evidence. No string-dispatched constraint behavior or boolean-mask-only constraint authority remains. No live solver callback, family-private time-profile authority, or ambiguous modal/SRS procedure remains. No semantic procedure dependency exists only as an execution edge, and no checkpoint, initial guess, or incomplete field can be presented as a completed physical state.

No full field is gathered merely to answer a distributable observation, and no visualization operation chooses result recovery semantics. No result is published with a failed mandatory accuracy criterion, or with an indeterminate one outside an explicit markIndeterminate policy. No advertised operation silently selects a reduced model. No caller-authored flag can bypass the formulation registry, and no numerical acceptance flag can be interpreted as publication without a valid admitted receipt.

requirements.title: Runnable exact public documentation and limitations
requirements.acceptance: Runnable exact public documentation and limitations requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: Each formulation must document: supported equations and assumptions; supported element/cell types and order; material models and units; boundary conditions, loads, and sources; available typed constraints, relations, connectors, frames, schedules, enforcement behavior, reactions, and conflict diagnostics; typed signals, excitations, initial conditions, standard waveforms, generated-input callables, interpolation, effects, provenance, and materialization behavior; analysis sequences, step activation, state transitions, preload/prestress, branching, restart, and rejected transitions; typed field, history, probe, reduction, monitor, diagnostic, sampling, precision, and retention requests; field selection and derived observation APIs separately from ordinary `plot` and `mesh` rendering; modal extraction versus modal forced response, SRS construction, response-spectrum metadata and combination policy, and random-response scope where supported; eigenvalue buckling, prestressed modal/harmonic assumptions, base-state requirements, and explicit exclusion of nonlinear post-buckling where applicable; accuracy goals, contribution evidence, acceptance states, automatic refinement limits, and the meaning of indeterminate evidence; solver and convergence controls; field locations and recovery meaning; quality and balance diagnostics; CPU/GPU and local/cluster execution behavior; the canonical sparse/operator model, solver and preconditioner compatibility, and reuse/invalidation rules; the distinction between whole-study remote execution, independent task distribution, cooperative distributed solves, and multi-accelerator execution; numerical artifact chunking, partial result access, checkpointing, and resource admission;

partition-local observation evaluation, global reduction attribution, bounded history streaming, and observation cost admission; adaptive behavior where supported; limitations and explicit rejection cases; runnable examples; and benchmark provenance. The central FEA documentation should connect geometry loading, declarative construction, immutable derivation, `.m` generation, AP242 parameter/property exchange, meshing, study construction, signal generation with ordinary RunMat numerical/signal/control functions, callable and `.fea` input materialization, execution placement, field extraction, ordinary `plot`/`mesh` visualization, quality statistics, persistence, replay, and cluster scheduling without duplicating family formulation documentation. The `.fea` language has a dedicated `docs/simulation/language/` section covering files/modules/imports, types/units/expressions, geometry/models/assignments, geometry features and AP242 exchange, studies/analyses/state, inputs/sweeps/cases, outputs/observations, execution/scaling, RunMat-function integration, diagnostics/tooling, and a mechanically checked language reference. The output-operation reference is derived from the canonical operation catalog and documents typed overloads, units, topology/location rules, attributed results, distribution behavior, and costs. Guides cover a first static study, reusable parameterized models, generated transient inputs, modal and response-spectrum work, sweeps, local-to-cluster scaling, and bounded access to large results. Documentation code blocks are parsed and type-checked; runnable guides use checked-in STEP assets. The scaling material explicitly distinguishes local parallelism, independent task fanout, and cooperative distributed numerical work.

Optimization, sensitivity analysis, uncertainty quantification, topology optimization, nonlinear post-buckling, arbitrary user elements, and executable constitutive laws must be documented as future envelopes rather than implied capabilities. Documentation may describe the typed dependency and extension seams, but it must not present capability metadata as an implemented solver feature.

requirements.title: Per-formulation complete acceptance
requirements.acceptance: Per-formulation complete acceptance requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: A formulation is complete only when all of the following are true: Its public contract names the actual equations, procedure, assumptions, and supported envelope. Its identity is constructed only from a qualified pre-solve admission receipt and records exact spatial, temporal, constitutive, coupling, recovery, topology, source, and boundary realizations; identity validity is rechecked at persistence and decode boundaries. Canonical geometry, regions, materials, sources, boundaries, contacts, and interfaces are realized without heuristic substitution. Constraint kinds, targets, DOFs, values, frames, schedules, relations, and enforcement are strongly typed after document parsing. Signals, physical quantities, units, domains, interpolation, excitations, initial conditions, response spectra, and combination policies are strongly typed after document parsing or runtime-value admission. Every dependent procedure consumes an immutable compatible state through a typed semantic transition; step activation, continuation, branching, restart, and retry retain distinct meanings and identities. Prestressed and buckling procedures retain their converged base state, tangent/geometric-stiffness, load-pattern, constraint, contact, and linearization provenance. Callable-backed inputs are frozen, effect-checked, materialized, validated, content-addressed, and evidenced before solve; no live language callback executes inside assembly, solver iteration, or distributed rank logic. Explicit and generated inputs satisfy the same realization, conservation, identity, retry, placement-equivalence, and publication contracts. Constraint rank, null spaces, violations, reactions, work, and conflicts are verified and attributable to authored objects.

Its discrete formulation is implemented in one analysis-owned module hierarchy. All fields have correct units, locations, topology, and recovery semantics. Field, history, probe, reduction, monitor, and diagnostic requests have correct quantities, targets, locations, frames, sampling, retention, and cost admission. Result-field selection and observation evaluation remain separate from ordinary `plot` and `mesh` rendering. Its solver reports real residuals, increments, balances, and convergence. CPU and any claimed accelerator path execute the intended operator with honest fallback provenance. Numerical algorithms and preconditioners are selected from typed operator properties and reject incompatible combinations. Sparse pattern, numeric values, preparation, and reuse have separate validated identities and invalidation rules. Analytic/manufactured, patch, convergence, conservation, invalid-case, and independent-reference evidence passes governed tolerances. Coupled or adaptive variants demonstrate closure or target-quantity convergence. Every result has a satisfied typed accuracy report; failed or indeterminate mandatory evidence blocks publication. Progress, cancellation, retry, restart, replay, persistence, and result queries work. Inline, isolated-process, durable, and claimed remote execution meet the declared equivalence policy. Independent task distribution and cooperative distributed algebra have distinct lifecycle, retry, checkpoint, and failure semantics. Constraint-plan identity and mathematical behavior remain independent of mesh storage order, task partitioning, worker count, and placement.

Signal interpolation and excitation realization remain independent of task partitioning, worker count, and placement within the declared numerical-equivalence policy. Large numerical inputs, outputs, and checkpoints are chunked content-addressed artifacts with partial access; they are not gathered through the driver. Partitioned observations and reductions preserve values, locations, attribution, deterministic/tolerance policy, and bounded history semantics without unnecessary global field gathering. Resource-aware local execution does not oversubscribe its CPU, memory, or accelerator lease. Claimed GPU execution meets operation-level native-work, transfer, synchronization, precision, memory, and convergence gates. Performance and resource use satisfy the governed supported envelope. Public documentation contains runnable examples and exact limitations. Future parameter/sensitivity and compiled-law capability metadata is truthful and is not presented as implemented optimization, uncertainty, post-buckling, arbitrary-element, or arbitrary-material functionality. Blocking release evidence covers the formulation. The overall plan is complete only when every formulation in the planned production surface satisfies this definition and all obsolete proxy paths have been removed.

requirements.title: Coherent tested modular implementation slices
requirements.acceptance: Coherent tested modular implementation slices requires every listed criterion in its declared supported scope. A passing component witness does not discharge unrelated criteria or broader execution envelopes.

obligations.criterion: For each implementation slice: Re-read the relevant section of the standing FEA acceptance specification and the current owning modules. State the intended domain owner and dependency direction before editing. Add or update a failing focused test or executable benchmark that expresses the required behavior. Implement the largest coherent vertical slice that can be designed, reviewed, and verified safely and productively; split only at a real domain, evidence, or risk boundary, and do not leave duplicate old/new behavior. Run formatting, focused tests, architecture checks, and relevant integration evidence. Use development telemetry for long-running or distributed work so progress and failures are inspected while execution is active. Review the diff for god-file growth, duplicate rules, misleading names, dead code, lint suppression, unrelated changes, and accidental work outside scope. Commit the measurable slice with a message describing the delivered behavior. Update the standing FEA acceptance specification only when evidence changes the dependency order, scope, or exit criteria. Never include unrelated changes from `runmat-private`, and never touch the separate active `runmat` checkout.

requirements.title: Acoustic cavity modal analysis
requirements.acceptance: Natural frequencies and pressure mode shapes of an enclosed air volume with rigid and impedance walls publish from an `acoustic modal` study through `runmat run` with eigen-residuals, mass normalization and resource admission that accepts real models.

obligations.criterion: Rigid box modes equal c/2 sqrt((l/Lx)^2 + (m/Ly)^2 + (n/Lz)^2); the first 10 modes agree within 0.5 percent on Tet10.
Modal studies with impedance walls (headliner 1200 Pa s/m, rigid glazing) return complex or damped modes consistent with the harmonic response peak positions.

Modal runs publish frequency, pressure mode shape fields (one view per mode), residuals and normalization, pass resource admission on a cabin-sized model (3 cubic metre air volume, 12 modes), and the cabin study's first mode is reported.

requirements.title: Acoustic transient analysis
requirements.acceptance: Time-domain pressure from a time-history source publishes from an `acoustic transient` study with an energy balance.

obligations.criterion: A one-dimensional pulse in a rigid duct matches d'Alembert travel time and amplitude to the declared tolerance.

An `acoustic transient` run publishes the complete ordered time history (time axis and one pressure snapshot per step including the initial state) as retained fields that are finite, bounded by the authored end time and readable cold, with the prescribed boundary carrying the authored pulse exactly.
The transient energy balance (stored plus radiated plus dissipated minus supplied) closes to the declared tolerance, and time-step convergence is demonstrated.

requirements.title: Sound pressure level, transmission loss, intensity and power
requirements.acceptance: Acoustic studies publish the engineering outputs the pages quote: sound pressure level as an output and field, transmission and insertion loss of a duct element over a frequency sweep, active intensity and sound power through named surfaces, per frequency and per one-third-octave band.

obligations.criterion: The `level` output and an SPL field (dB re 20 micropascal, rms, optional A-weighting) publish per frequency from a harmonic study; a plane wave of 1 Pa amplitude reads 91.0 dB; point outputs interpolate the field at an authored position.

`transmission_loss` from incident and transmitted power (two-port) over a one-third-octave sweep 50 Hz to 2 kHz reproduces the simple expansion chamber TL = 10 log10(1 + 1/4 (m - 1/m)^2 sin^2(kL)) up to the first cross mode; the muffler study reports peak TL, its band, the lowest TL above the first peak and the bands below 15 dB.
The active intensity field and `sound_power` through a named surface publish; power through a sphere around a monopole equals rho c k^2 Q^2 / (8 pi) within 1 percent.
A study generates one-third-octave band centers (and other authored frequency sets), runs each frequency, and publishes outputs in authored order with per-frequency status.
Outputs of two analyses in one study (treated and bare room) combine into a difference output such as the SPL reduction at the operator position.

requirements.title: Radiation, frequency-dependent impedance and air damping
requirements.acceptance: Acoustic boundaries and media beyond constant real impedance run: spherical radiation on an outer sphere or hemisphere, complex and frequency-dependent impedance from a table or a porous-layer model, region damping, and periodic cells for band gaps.

obligations.criterion: A spherical radiation boundary on an outer sphere or hemisphere converges toward the exact impedance: a pulsating sphere's surface pressure is within 2 percent of rho c u i k a / (1 + i k a) at ka = 1.

An impedance boundary takes a complex value and a frequency table, and a `delany_bazley` porous layer (flow resistivity, thickness); normal-incidence absorption of a 50 mm layer matches the Delany-Bazley closed form; the room study's treated and bare ceilings run.
Loss factor or complex sound speed per region is accepted at assembly (now rejected) and a damped duct resonance peak width matches the closed form.
A periodic unit cell with Bloch boundaries yields the band gap of a rod array, compared against an independent plane-wave expansion.

requirements.title: One-way structure-borne sound
requirements.acceptance: The normal velocity of a structural harmonic or modal result drives an acoustic study through a retained state, with conservative surface transfer.

obligations.criterion: An acoustic step reads a retained structural velocity state on a wetted surface (`normal_velocity on face = analysis.s.state.velocity` with `retain velocity`); a baffled piston matches the Rayleigh integral on axis, and the speaker study (cone harmonic, then 200 Hz, 1 kHz and 4 kHz radiation) reports on-axis SPL and directivity.
Volume velocity is conserved through the transfer between non-matching structural and acoustic surface meshes.

requirements.title: Chained thermal-structural studies
requirements.acceptance: Thermal studies chain into preload, prestressed modal, harmonic and buckling studies from one `.fea` file, with the thermomechanical references the page quotes.

obligations.criterion: A study runs thermal, then preload, then buckling or prestressed modal in sequence on one mesh without the mixed-sequence rejection, with the retained states typed and checked.

A uniformly heated constrained bar (80 K rise) gives axial stress -E alpha deltaT (-192 MPa for the page's bar); the first bending frequency of a bar heated 200 K over unheated is 0.963 within the declared tolerance.

requirements.title: Adaptive analysis from the language and CLI
requirements.acceptance: Estimator-driven adaptive analysis is authored in the study language and runs from the public command, with the accuracy target and refinement history published.

obligations.criterion: An adaptive analysis is declared in a `.fea` study with its target quantity and tolerance, admitted by check, run from the public command, and publishes the estimator, refinement history and final verdict.

requirements.title: Transient electromagnetics
requirements.acceptance: Time-domain eddy currents (A-V formulation) run from time-history drives, including switching and pulse loads, with the loss passed to heat, from an `electromagnetic transient` study through `runmat run`.

obligations.criterion: A step current into a conducting slab diffuses with the analytic error-function series (field and current density) within the declared tolerance, converging in time step and mesh.
Pulsed and switched voltage or current drives from authored time signals run and conserve energy: supplied equals stored magnetic energy plus Joule loss plus work.
The Joule loss history is available to a thermal transient as a conservative heat source without remeshing.

requirements.title: Saturating iron
requirements.acceptance: Nonlinear B-H curves (tabulated, monotone spline) run in magnetostatics, in harmonic analysis through an effective permeability, and in transient analysis, with Newton and line search.

obligations.criterion: Tabulated B-H data is validated monotone and dimensioned, evaluated with a monotone spline, and extrapolated to the vacuum slope above the last point; non-monotone or non-physical data is rejected.
The nonlinear magnetic solve converges with Newton and line search, publishes iteration history, and fails typed when it stagnates.

A saturating toroid reproduces the analytic B(H) relation (H = N I / l) within the declared tolerance in magnetostatic, harmonic effective-permeability and transient forms, and a current-sensor core near saturation reports flux through iron and gap.

requirements.title: Every declared electromagnetic input runs
requirements.acceptance: Every electromagnetic input the language declares runs and is documented: terminal_voltage, electric_current terminals, electric_charge, current_density, magnetic_vector_potential, magnetic.insulation, equipotential, floating, integral-current and periodic constraints.

obligations.criterion: terminal_voltage, electric current terminals, electric_charge, equipotential, floating and integral-current constraints run for electrostatics and steady conduction, with total current and charge balances closed.
current_density, magnetic_vector_potential, magnetic.insulation and periodic constraints run for magnetostatics and harmonic Maxwell with typed rank-correct constraints.

requirements.title: Multi-frequency harmonic electromagnetics and fields
requirements.acceptance: Harmonic Maxwell runs several frequencies in one study through the executor with skin effect resolved, AC loss computed, outer air boundaries that do not corrupt the interior field, and the fields and terminal quantities the pages quote.

obligations.criterion: A single study runs 3, 10 and 30 kHz (or any authored frequency set) as one analysis with per-frequency fields and status in authored order.

Conductor current density and AC resistance reproduce the skin-depth reference delta = sqrt(2 / (omega mu sigma)) for a round conductor or slab within the declared tolerance on a mesh that resolves delta.
Interior fields and coil loss change by less than the declared tolerance when the surrounding air domain is enlarged, so the outer boundary choice is documented as adequate.
Cycle-averaged loss in a body (the induction-hardening gear at 10 kHz) equals the integral of J dot E over the body and matches terminal power minus stored-energy exchange.

requirements.title: Electromagnetic outputs and fields
requirements.acceptance: Electromagnetic studies publish the derived values and fields the pages show: terminal voltage drop, resistance, current, loss power and field maxima, and current density, flux density and electric field with magnitudes (and phases for AC).

obligations.criterion: Voltage drop between named faces, terminal current, resistance and loss power publish and agree with V = I R for the busbar and with energy balances; a high-voltage electrode reports peak field and an assessment against its limit, sharp versus rounded.

Current density, magnetic flux density and electric field publish as element or node vector fields with magnitudes (and phasors for AC) in the form the viewer reads for cut planes, field lines, arrows and isosurfaces.

requirements.title: Trace impedance from board cross-sections
requirements.acceptance: A board cross-section built from a stackup (layer thicknesses and Dk, copper thickness, trace width and etch angle, conformal solder mask, reference planes and coplanar ground) solves two 2D electrostatic problems, with the dielectrics and in vacuum, and publishes per-length C and L matrices, Z0, εeff and delay per signal conductor and, for a pair, Zdiff, Zcommon, odd- and even-mode impedance and εeff, and near- and far-end coupling coefficients. Each value agrees with its published reference within the stated tolerance and converges under mesh refinement. Lossless; R and G per length are a separate requirement.

obligations.criterion: Single lines: Z0, εeff, delay, C and L of surface microstrip and stripline agree with Hammerstad–Jensen (zero-thickness microstrip, within 0.5 %), Cohn's exact stripline form (within 0.3 %) and the IPC-2141A microstrip and stripline forms inside their stated ranges (within 5 %). A homogeneous dielectric gives εeff = εr exactly.

Pairs: the 2×2 per-length C and L matrices are symmetric; odd- and even-mode impedances of edge-coupled stripline agree with Cohn's exact coupled-strip forms within 0.3 %; Zdiff = 2 Zodd and Zcommon = Zeven / 2 for a symmetric pair; a homogeneous dielectric gives zero far-end coupling; a microstrip pair has distinct modal εeff and negative far-end coupling.
Halving the edge element size three times changes Z0 of a thick-copper microstrip by successively smaller amounts, the last below 0.1 %; doubling the open-region enclosure changes Z0 by under 0.05 %.

The stackup inputs act physically: conformal solder mask and coplanar ground lower Z0, a sloped etch sidewall raises it; malformed sections (overlapping traces, no return conductor, an etch angle with no far face, a missing or non-signal layer, εr below 1, a growth ratio outside (1, 2]) are rejected with the reason.

A `.fea` study with a `cross_section` geometry, a triangle mesh and an `electromagnetic line_parameters` analysis checks and runs through `runmat check` and `runmat run`, takes its stackup inline or from a `.circuit.layout`, and publishes every output of this requirement; the 50 Ω microstrip and 100 Ω pair example runs with receipts.

requirements.title: Two-way and transient Joule and AC-loss heating
requirements.acceptance: Electrothermal studies run from a `.fea` study with temperature-dependent conductivity iterated to convergence, transient heating, and harmonic AC loss chained into a transient heat analysis.

obligations.criterion: `electrothermal steady` with sigma(T) = sigma0 / (1 + alpha (T - T0)) iterates to a converged fixed point; the busbar with alpha = 0.00393 per K reproduces power equal to V times I.
`electrothermal transient` runs with the same coupling and matches a lumped adiabatic heating reference over a short time and steady state over a long time.
Cycle-averaged harmonic loss from the gear and inductor drives a 3 s transient heat step with the loss field mapped conservatively (total power preserved), reporting peak gear surface temperature.
Electrothermal studies are admitted at `runmat run` and run remotely.

requirements.title: Robust, scalable and accurate laminar flow solvers
requirements.acceptance: Non-turbulent flow solves robustly at every Reynolds number the laminar scope covers: a coupled Newton solver with pseudo-transient and Reynolds continuation, scalable block-preconditioned linear solvers, second-order time integration, and second-order accurate discretization on CAD tetrahedra, from `runmat run`.

obligations.criterion: A fully coupled pressure-based Newton solver with pseudo-transient continuation, Reynolds and rheology continuation and line search converges the Ghia lid-driven cavity at Re 1000 from rest in at most 15 Newton steps, with psi_min 0.1189366 at (0.5308, 0.5652) against the Botella-Peyret reference; stagnation is reported in the run evidence.
Per-iteration residual history and nonlinear and linear iteration counts publish as results for every flow run.

Flow linear systems solve with FGMRES using block-triangular preconditioning (PCD or LSC Schur approximations, augmented Lagrangian at high Reynolds number) and AMG on velocity and pressure blocks, through the shared sparse layer including its GPU path; linear iterations stay within 1.5 times from 100 thousand to 10 million cells on the 3D cavity.

BDF2 with adaptive steps is the default transient scheme and a rotational pressure-correction projection scheme serves long transients: Schafer-Turek 2D-2 (Re 100) gives c_D,max 3.22 to 3.24, c_L,max 0.99 to 1.01 and Strouhal number 0.295 to 0.305; 2D-3 gives c_D,max 2.950921 and c_L,max 0.47795 (references checked against the paper before use).

Second-order coupled finite volume with non-orthogonal correction and polyhedral dual, and P2-P1 or VMS finite elements on Tet10, reach design order on Kovasznay flow at Re 40 and reproduce Schafer-Turek 2D-1 (c_D 5.579535, c_L 0.0106189, pressure drop 0.1175201) and 3D-1Z (c_D 6.185333, c_L 0.009401, pressure drop 0.171007).

requirements.title: Complete fluid boundary and excitation set
requirements.acceptance: Every flow boundary condition and excitation the language declares runs: velocity profiles (function, table, fully developed), inlet_velocity and wall_motion excitations, pressure inlets, open outlets with backflow stabilization, Navier slip and symmetry, periodic with imposed pressure drop or flow rate, rotating walls, fan curves, screens and porous jumps, and inlet temperature and wall heat conditions. Backflow at outlets is stabilized, not rejected.

obligations.criterion: Velocity profiles (function, table, fully developed, periodic-spline sampled pulsatile waveforms from a CSV) and the `inlet_velocity` and `wall_motion` excitations run; square duct reproduces fRe 56.91 and circular Hagen-Poiseuille fRe 64.

Pressure inlets and directional do-nothing open outlets with backflow stabilization run with flow reversing at the outlet; a closed pressure reference removes the null space without changing the solution.
Navier slip, symmetry, periodic boundaries with imposed pressure drop or flow rate, and rotating walls run: periodic channel flow rate is exact, Taylor-Couette torque matches u_theta = A r + B / r.
Fan curves, screens and porous jumps apply a pressure jump consistent with their authored law and conserve mass.
Inlet temperature, wall temperature, wall heat flux and convective wall conditions apply to the fluid energy equation and conserve energy.

requirements.title: Heat in the fluid: forced and natural convection, CHT and low-Mach flow
requirements.acceptance: The energy equation runs in the fluid with forced convection, two-way Boussinesq natural convection, viscous heating and temperature-dependent properties, two-way conjugate heat transfer with thermal solids over perfect and resistive interfaces, radiation coupling, and low-Mach variable-density flow.

obligations.criterion: Fluid energy transport reproduces the pipe Nusselt numbers 3.66 (constant wall temperature) and 4.364 (constant heat flux), and the Graetz thermal entry length.

Two-way Boussinesq natural convection reproduces the de Vahl Davis differentially heated cavity Nusselt numbers 1.118, 2.243, 4.519 and 8.800 at Ra 1e3 to 1e6 within 1 percent, the Tric cube values 1.0700, 2.0542, 4.3371 and 8.6407, and Rayleigh-Benard onset at Ra_c 1707.76; `conjugate_heat_transfer steady { buoyancy = boussinesq; gravity = ... }` runs the sealed enclosure study.
Viscous heating and temperature-dependent density, viscosity, conductivity and specific heat run and close the energy balance to the declared tolerance.

Two-way conjugate heat transfer with thermal solids converges with conservative interface flux continuity (residual published) and reproduces series conduction and plug-flow references; the liquid cold plate study reports pressure drop and peak plate temperature at 0.03 kg/s and 1.2 kW.
Surface radiation couples to the fluid and solid energy balances with emissivity and ambient or enclosure temperature and closes the balance.
Low-Mach flow with density from temperature and pressure reproduces the heated vertical channel variable-density closed form.

requirements.title: Rheology, porous media and species transport
requirements.acceptance: Fluid material behavior runs: generalized-Newtonian, viscoelastic, porous and passive-scalar models with their typed input forms and the shear-rate, apparent-viscosity and concentration fields.

obligations.criterion: Power law, Carreau and Carreau-Yasuda, Cross, Casson, regularized Bingham and Herschel-Bulkley with Arrhenius and WLF temperature dependence run, publish shear-rate and apparent-viscosity fields, reproduce the power-law channel profile and the Buckingham-Reiner pipe flow rate.
Oldroyd-B, Giesekus and PTT with log-conformation run, and the Oldroyd-B cylinder-in-channel drag against Weissenberg number matches Alves et al.

Darcy, Brinkman and Forchheimer porous zones with anisotropic permeability and local thermal equilibrium run: Darcy u = (K/mu) G, the Brinkman channel profile and the Ergun packed-bed pressure drop; the filter study reports its housing-plus-cartridge pressure drop.

Passive scalar advection-diffusion, mass-action and Arrhenius reactions, residence time and a mixing index run: Graetz-type mass transfer and laminar tubular reactor conversion match their closed forms; the static mixer reports outlet concentration coefficient of variation and pressure drop.

requirements.title: Free surface, rotating frames, lubrication, electrokinetics, particles, compressibility and reduced dimensions
requirements.acceptance: The remaining non-turbulent flow physics run: free surface and two-phase flow, rotating frames and sliding mesh, thin-film lubrication, electrokinetics, particle tracing, compressible laminar flow with rarefied slip, one-dimensional pipe networks coupled to three-dimensional flow, and two-dimensional and axisymmetric studies.

obligations.criterion: Volume-of-fluid or level-set free surface with surface tension, contact angle and Marangoni stress reproduces the static drop Laplace pressure 2 sigma / R with bounded spurious currents and Jurin capillary rise.
Rotating reference frames (MRF and SRF) and sliding mesh reproduce solid-body rotation in a rotating annulus and Taylor vortex onset at Re_c about 68.2 for radius ratio 0.5.

The Reynolds equation with Elrod-JFO cavitation, journal and thrust bearings, squeeze film and coupling to structural deformation reproduces long and short journal bearing load and attitude angle (Sommerfeld); the journal bearing study reports load capacity at 3000 rpm and eccentricity ratio 0.6.
Electroosmotic slip (Helmholtz-Smoluchowski), Poisson-Nernst-Planck and dielectrophoresis run; electroosmotic plug flow equals -epsilon zeta E / mu.
Massless particles (residence time, mixing) and inertial particles with drag are traced one-way through a solved flow, and Stokes settling velocity is reproduced.

Compressible laminar flow and rarefied slip reproduce microchannel gas flow with slip against the closed form, and one-dimensional pipe networks coupled to three-dimensional regions reproduce Darcy-Weisbach network pressure drop.
Two-dimensional and axisymmetric studies run through the same study language and reproduce the three-dimensional pipe and sphere results.

requirements.title: Flow outputs engineers ask for
requirements.acceptance: Flow results publish the derived quantities designs are judged on, with correct dimensions, location and conservation: forces, moments and coefficients on named surfaces, wall shear stress and its time statistics, pressure drop and flow rate between named faces, heat-transfer quantities, vorticity and Q-criterion, and nodal velocity for streamlines.

obligations.criterion: Forces, moments and drag and lift coefficients on named surfaces reproduce sphere Stokes drag 6 pi mu a U and C_D about 1.09 at Re 100, and cylinder C_D about 1.52 and wake length L/D about 2.3 at Re 40.
A wall shear stress field, time-averaged wall shear stress and the oscillatory shear index publish for pulsatile flow; the carotid study reports minimum time-averaged wall shear stress in the sinus.
`pressure_drop` between named faces and flow rate through named faces publish and satisfy mass conservation to the declared tolerance.
Nusselt number, heat-transfer coefficient and bulk temperature publish for heated walls and agree with the energy balance.
Vorticity, Q-criterion and nodal velocity (for streamlines) publish with the declared shapes and locations.

requirements.title: Published flow verification suite
requirements.acceptance: Every flow witness is published as a suite page with mesh-convergence plots, wall time, memory and iteration counts, generated from runs, with the literature values checked against the source papers before use and misses published.

obligations.criterion: The suite at docs/simulation/validation/fluid contains the lid-driven cavity, Schafer-Turek 2D and 3D cases, Kovasznay, de Vahl Davis and Tric natural convection, duct and pipe references, Taylor-Couette, Turek-Hron FSI and the physics rows above, each with convergence, wall time, memory and iteration counts, regenerated from runs.
