requirements.title: Fluid loads on structures and two-way FSI
requirements.acceptance: Fluid pressure and wall shear drive structural studies one-way, two-way partitioned FSI with ALE mesh motion and large-deformation solids runs from the public command, and compliant-channel FSI matches lubrication theory.

obligations.criterion: Pressure and wall shear stress from a solved flow map conservatively into a structural study as loads (total force and moment preserved), including wind-pressure-style mapped loads.

Two-way partitioned FSI with Aitken relaxation, Laplace ALE mesh motion with geometric conservation and Newmark structure reproduces the Turek-Hron FSI1, FSI2 and FSI3 tip displacements and forces within the published scatter.
A compliant channel reproduces lubrication-theory deflection within 5 percent and conserves interface work.
The structural side of FSI accepts large-deformation solids with the same coupling residuals and conservation.

requirements.title: Exact CAD import of real parts and assemblies
requirements.acceptance: STEP (including AP242 product, assembly, parameter and material data), IGES and BREP import preserve the authoritative B-rep topology, mass properties, units, part structure and authored names, or fail with a typed rejection. Imported geometry that the public examples and website studies use resolves by authored name at check, plan and run alike.

obligations.criterion: Exact STEP, IGES and BREP import keeps authoritative B-rep topology and mass properties, or fails typed; tessellated formats (STL, OBJ, PLY, glTF) are rejected for solver meshing with a typed diagnostic. A governed corpus of at least the verification/meshing/corpus.json fixtures passes with recorded hashes, topology counts and mass properties.

Assemblies with touching, imprinted or nested bodies import as named parts with explicit interfaces and without failing on shared faces: a gear, an inductor and the surrounding air; a core, primary and air; a plate and its coolant volume. Each part keeps its own solid, shell and face identities and the assembly keeps the interface lineage the study selects against.

Face, edge, solid and assembly names authored in the STEP file (for example Beam, Fixed end, Loaded end, Heat sink, Mounting face, Coil terminal in, Coil terminal out, Outer boundary, Inlet, Outlet, Walls) are read from the file and resolve with `select name` at check and at run to the same entities. Unnamed or ambiguous selections fail with a located diagnostic; no run silently selects zero or the wrong entities.

`select id` on constructed geometry, `select result` and `select name` for fluid `cell` regions on CAD, and every other selector form the language admits resolve identically at check and at run; a selector that check accepts cannot fail at run for lack of an entity.

Exact import validation of curved parts (coaxial pipes with chamber and baffle, a 1.5 m hemisphere, spherical sinuses) completes within a stated allocation and time budget and either passes or fails with a typed diagnostic naming the entity; `EXACT_VALIDATION_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` on a valid part is a defect, and the budget accounts allocation consumption in every validation stage.
The `geometry.load` units option and the `units` declaration of a geometry block scale imported coordinates consistently and reject mixed or missing units with a typed diagnostic before meshing.

requirements.title: Valid tetrahedral meshes on exact geometry
requirements.acceptance: One metric size field drives curve, surface and volume discretization on exact geometry, producing conforming Tet4 and curved Tet10 meshes with valid elements, exact boundary and interface faces and recorded quality evidence, inside the authored work, memory and time budgets. Mesh acceptance includes solver relevance, not only element quality.

obligations.criterion: Curve discretization respects exact edge and pcurve domains, tiny edges, periodic curves and seams on real parts, within the declared chordal deviation.

Constructive trimmed-surface triangulation handles seams, poles, many trims and dense faces within the memory budget, and a dense surface of at least 90,000 nodes and 180,000 triangles is retained and published within cache-entry and codec limits.

Three-dimensional constrained Delaunay recovers segments and facets, carves exterior, nested voids and regions, and preserves conformal interfaces and contact pairs; the exact boundary is matched to the declared tolerance, with a real-part corpus beside the fixtures.

Volume quality refinement terminates within the authored work and time budget on the bracket, heat sink and tuning fork, ending with every element at or above the declared quality floor, and refinement yields to coupled repair fairly with stale rejections invalidated and true global exhaustion detected.

Surface meshing handles every analytic surface kind including spheres, tori, cones and cylinders with poles, seams and umbilic points: a plain sphere, a hemisphere, spherical fillets and domes, and a carotid bulb and sinus mesh with the directional curvature metric defined at umbilic points.

Tet10 elevation yields valid curved elements without near-slivers: positive curved Jacobian everywhere and a scaled-Jacobian floor stated per part, including thin airfoil sections and the tuning fork.

Global, regional, face, edge and feature-based size controls and graded sizing are exposed in the `.fea` mesh block and drive the one metric field; a graded heat-sink surface and a channel-resolving cold-plate mesh are produced from authored controls without manual partitioning.

Mesh acceptance includes solver patch and convergence relevance on real parts: a recorded refinement series shows the target quantity converging, so coarse Tet4 meshes are flagged where stiffness is not credible.

Every mesh ships an evidence artifact with per-stage counters, invariants, quality distributions (minimum, mean, p95, p99, maximum of chordal deviation, normal deviation, metric edge length, radius-edge ratio and scaled Jacobian), peak memory and the seed and digest.
A differential comparison against an independent mesher (OCCT incremental mesh) on a box, a curved part and a real part records volume, gradient energy and mismatches with their dispositions.

requirements.title: Real parts mesh with a published success rate
requirements.acceptance: A stated corpus of real parts and every website hero part meshes through the public command on the release build with defaults, with a published success rate and time distribution on stated hardware. Misses are published, not hidden.

obligations.criterion: A named corpus (bracket, heat sink, tuning fork, cantilever, blade, lugs, tower, and the website fixtures) meshes on the release build; the success rate and the wall-time and memory distributions are generated from the run and published with hardware, including failures.

`runmat mesh bracket.stp` with bare defaults is accepted; the KiCad heat sink meshes and its steady study closes the ~10 W balance; the tuning fork meshes with Tet10 and returns two modes with eigen-residuals; each stays inside the authored 512 MiB and one hour envelope with whole-task resources measured.

Every STEP fixture the website studies use meshes and passes quality acceptance at the authored size: cold plate (6 x 3 mm channels), enclosure, carotid bifurcation, static mixer, journal bearing, filter, muffler, cabin, speaker hemisphere with diaphragm, room, induction gear with inductor and air, busbar, current sensor, electrode.
Twisted or extruded blades, lugs and towers, fused pcurve tolerances, planar curve ranges and booleans on curved STEP mesh without hangs or invalid curved elements.
`runmat mesh` accepts defaults and writes the mesh and its evidence artifact; failures are typed and name the stage.

Acoustic and electromagnetic meshes are checked against wavelength or skin-depth targets at check or plan time, and a mesh coarser than the declared elements-per-wavelength rule produces a located diagnostic rather than a silent accuracy loss.

requirements.title: Deterministic, distributed and bounded meshing
requirements.acceptance: Meshing runs on the same execution layer as studies: independent curve, face and volume batches fan out over worker processes, a single connected volume partitions across workers, results are identical across backends, worker counts and platforms, and every stage enforces its budgets and cancellation. The browser never meshes silently.

obligations.criterion: Deterministic edge and face batches execute on worker processes without manual partitioning, and the same artifact results from one or many workers.
Serial, local-process, durable-local and remote pool runs return the same canonical topology and digest.

A single connected body's volume mesh partitions across workers with owned and ghost regions, and the assembled mesh has the same validity and quality guarantees as the serial mesh and a stated speedup on at least 4 workers.
Meshing saturates the admitted CPU threads of one machine under the single thread plan, with identical output at 1, 2 and 4 threads.
Worker loss retries once with fencing, transfers are resumable and encrypted end to end, stale results never evict inputs, and durable supervisor restart and durable cancellation recover.
Canonical topology and digest are identical across worker counts, partition layouts and the supported platforms, on a matrix that includes macOS and Linux.
Element, memory, scratch, search, recursion and time budgets and cooperative cancellation are enforced inside every stage with typed failures.
Mesh publication and cold materialization are bounded and compact at representative scale (millions of elements) and never exceed declared codec or cache caps.
Meshing reuses the execution configuration with no second scheduler, and the browser either selects a native or remote mesher or fails explicitly, never meshing silently.

A versioned performance and resource SLO covers the corpus parts, current reports are regenerated each release, and the meshing governance validators (corpus, conformance, differential, reliability, release evidence) pass.

requirements.title: Published studies run from the public command
requirements.acceptance: Every published example and website study runs end to end from `runmat check|plan|run <file>.fea` on the release build, locally and, for every physics family, remotely, publishing the fields and outputs the page shows, with no maturity switch, no hidden preparation step and no family rejected as unsupported.

obligations.criterion: Every file in docs/simulation/examples and docs/fea/examples completes with `runmat run` on the release build; the generated catalog records pass and wall time for each.
For each physics family named on the site, its worked example runs locally and with `--cluster` and publishes the same fields.

Each hero study in oct-13-2026/website/physics/studies (structural cantilever and fork, heat sink, induction hardening, busbar, current sensor, electrode, muffler, cabin modes, speaker, room, cold plate and its sweep, enclosure, carotid, static mixer, journal bearing, filter) runs from its full `.fea` file, not only its `.today.fea` variant, and publishes every output its page quotes.

Thermal into preload into buckling or prestressed dynamics, electrothermal, conjugate heat transfer and fluid-structure studies are admitted and run from the public command with converged coupling and interface residuals published.

Direct and modal transient structural studies, including a study driven by a generated load, run on Tet4 and Tet10 without a transient block bound failure, a stack overflow or a codec limit at 1,001 or more signal samples.
Buckling and random-response studies run on the 4,655-node cantilever within the default publication budget, producing the load factor and RMS response the page quotes.
The published steady conduction example passes its energy gate and publishes heat flux consistent with k times the temperature difference over the length.

A study sweeps a typed input (convection film coefficient from still air to forced air; cold-plate mass flow) and evaluates an assessment per case (peak temperature below 85 C; lowest pump power meeting the limit), publishing per-case verdicts in authored order.
The demo bracket STEP with steel, 2 kN on the top face and both mounting holes fixed meshes and solves from the public command and publishes von Mises stress, peak stress and peak displacement.

requirements.title: Authored language surface the published studies rely on
requirements.acceptance: The `.fea` language accepts, checks and lowers every construct the published studies use, reports located diagnostics, and never accepts at check what run then rejects. New forms the pages show are admitted with checked dimensions and documented exactly.

obligations.criterion: `runmat check` on a `.fea` file prints `error[code]: message`, the file:line:col location, the source line with a caret underline and label, the expected and found units, trims leading indentation, suppresses cascade errors from a failed dependency, and ends with the `checked ...: N error(s), M warning(s)` summary; `--json` carries the same spans.
A model with loads and no `load_case` applies them in one default case and `runmat check` accepts it; a model with several loads and an explicit case set is unchanged.
Unit prefixes kW, MW, kA, kV, mA, MN, mN, kHz and the other SI prefixes parse with correct scale and dimension, and `degC` is accepted with the documented offset rule.
`runmat check` validates procedure members, state references and name selectors so that a study it accepts cannot fail at run for those reasons.

Output forms the pages show check with dimensions, lower and run: `pressure_drop(analysis, from =, to =)`, `transmission_loss(analysis, incident =, transmitted =)`, `sound_power(analysis, through =)`, `interpolate(output, at = [x, y, z])`, `mean(field, over = time)`, `max(field, over = region)`, field names such as `field.face.wall_shear_stress`, and arithmetic between outputs of different analyses in one study, `oscillatory_shear_index(...)`, `coefficient_of_variation(...)` over a region, and the `lubrication` outputs `film_pressure` and `friction_torque`.

`rpm` is a unit, units with fractional powers (such as Pa*s^0.45 for a power-law consistency) parse with exact dimensions, and total power on a body (`heat_generation on <body> = 2 W`) is accepted alongside W/m^3 and converts to the correct volumetric source.

Typed input forms the pages show are admitted: `input film : heat_transfer_coefficient`, frequency tables and generated one-third-octave center sets, `samples = file "...csv"` with `interpolation = periodic_spline`, impedance tables over frequency with a `delany_bazley` model, `normal_velocity` read from a retained state of another analysis, `species <name> { diffusivity }` with `fluid steady { transport = [...] }`, `porous { law = darcy_forchheimer; permeability; inertial_coefficient; porosity }`, fluid laws `carreau` and `power_law`, the `lubrication` family (`lubrication.journal`, `lubrication.pressure`, `lubrication steady { cavitation = elrod }`), and `mass_flow_rate` as a sweep input type.
`.fea` files type-check in the browser with the same diagnostics as the CLI, and the browser never runs or meshes silently.
`import function` of a MATLAB function that generates a load over time checks, solves a transient with it and returns the response shown on the runtime page.

requirements.title: Results readable, verdicted and viewable
requirements.acceptance: Results of every published study are readable from MATLAB code, carry passed, failed or indeterminate verdicts against stated criteria that can be re-assessed without re-solving, reopen cold, and capture into the saved scenes the pages show.

obligations.criterion: A MATLAB script runs a `.fea` study by path with `fea.run`, reads fields with `fea.results` and `fea.field`, and compares the peak with beam theory, printing the three differences the runtime page shows.

Each published example shows a verdict of passed, failed or indeterminate against its stated criteria with evidence in the results pane and CLI; an unconverged case returns indeterminate; `runmat reassess` re-evaluates criteria without re-solving.
The field result is shown beside a closed-form estimate for bending, torsion and conduction cases, computed from the study's own parameters.

`runmat snapshot` captures each hero study into a saved scene with the views the page shows: fields with cut planes and caps, field lines, arrows, isosurfaces, per-body transparency, AC-cycle playback, one view per frequency or mode, transient playback and streamlines, and the scene replays faithfully after save (NaN, colormaps, legends, units).
Guide and hero results save and cold-reopen in Desktop and the graphics-only web viewer with identical fields and views.
Repeated eigenvalues from symmetric sections do not degrade a modal run or block its snapshot.
Every result records the requested and actual backend, precision, solver method, preconditioner and any fallback stage, and a fallback never reports the requested backend as used.
The Desktop study editor, geometry viewer, results pane and agent pane operate on the published studies in the released app, with the same checks and results as the CLI.
The same study yields identical result digests across runs, thread counts and worker counts, with the guarantee and its scope (same build, hardware class) stated.

requirements.title: Validation published, docs true, no maturity surface
requirements.acceptance: Every closed-form and benchmark check the site quotes is filled from a run and published with misses and convergence, results are compared with an open solver on named parts, the simulation docs and status match the code, and no experimental or maturity switch remains anywhere: language, admission, kernels, examples, docs or file names.

obligations.criterion: For every physics a table of named benchmark cases (analytic, manufactured and published) is generated from runs and published with the reference value, the computed value, the difference, mesh convergence and wall time, misses included; no value is typed by hand.
Formula, RunMat and an open solver agree within stated tolerance side by side on five real parts, with the method and any disagreement published.

The simulation docs, status tables and per-physics pages are generated from or checked against the admission registry and runner gate, and every row in the docs-drift list is closed; branch features are documented in the change that adds them.
The heat-sink and tuning-fork guides publish with their projects, archives and HTTP checks from accepted runs.
Each shippable physics family has a guide with a runnable example, including electrostatics, conduction, magnetostatics, harmonic Maxwell, acoustics and flow.

No `formulation = experimental` switch, maturity gate in admission or kernels, 'production qualification unsupported' rejection, or the word experimental in docs, examples and file names remains; a finished capability simply runs.

requirements.title: The register defines done and maintains itself
requirements.acceptance: The register, its witness tags and its scope inventory are the definition of done: witnesses are declared at the tests, validated in CI, run to produce a generated evidence catalog, and every scope row the sources claim maps to an obligation or an explicit exclusion.

obligations.criterion: Every witness tag in the repository names an existing obligation, claims only envelopes that obligation requires, carries a non-empty boundary and sits on an existing test function; a stale or broken tag fails the qualification tests.

The evidence catalog (markdown and JSON, per requirement, obligation and envelope with PASS, FAIL or OPEN and the test locator) is generated by running the tagged tests, never hand-edited, and a cell is PASS only when every tagged test for it passed in that run.

Every capability the website plans, end states, claim rows and FEA scope documents state has an inventory row that maps to existing obligations or to an explicit exclusion with its reason; no row is unmapped and every mapped obligation exists.
Requirement and obligation declarations are structurally valid: unique, non-empty, with distinct required envelopes drawn from the declared vocabulary, and owning sources exist.

requirements.title: Every family saturates the machine through one thread plan
requirements.acceptance: Every physics family assembles, solves, recovers and publishes in parallel under the single thread-plan authority, so a study uses all admitted cores of one machine with no serial-only assembly, solve or recovery path, and results match the serial reference under the declared determinism policy and are identical across thread counts.

obligations.criterion: Exactly one thread-plan authority binds the admitted cores for assembly, solve, recovery and publication of every family; no family reserves cores and runs serially, and a study that requests N threads is observed to use N.

Operator assembly, boundary and excitation realization, field recovery and publication run in parallel and agree with the serial reference within the declared tolerance, bit-for-bit where the policy declares it.
Direct (Cholesky, LDLT, LU), Krylov, AMG and block-eigen solves of the family run in parallel on the shared sparse layer and reproduce the serial solution and residual history within tolerance.

The shared parallel kernels under every family agree with their serial references: element assembly into the sparse pattern is bit-identical to the serial loop at 1, 2, 3, 7 and 16 threads; scoped Krylov solves equal the serial solution and reject nested execution; pooled CSR products preserve serial bits and output shape.
The same study yields identical result digests, or differences within the stated tolerance, across 1, 2, 4 and all admitted threads.

A strong-scaling table from 1 to all cores of the stated machine, produced with the exclusive benchmark gate, is generated and published for the family's published example, with parallel efficiency and the hardware recorded.

requirements.title: Remote and cooperative execution for every family
requirements.acceptance: Every physics family runs whole-study on a remote cluster with the same results as local execution, sweep cases and frequency points fan out across workers with results in authored order, and one large problem partitions across workers through domain decomposition with a solution equal to the serial reference.

obligations.criterion: `runmat run --cluster` runs the family's published study remotely with encrypted inputs, no unsupported-physics rejection, and results equal to the local run under the equivalence policy.

Sweep cases and independent frequency points run concurrently on local workers or a cluster, overlap in time, publish per-case status and return results in authored order identical to serial execution.

One problem partitions into owned and ghost subdomains over at least 4 workers; the cooperative solve equals the serial reference within tolerance, fails collectively with epoch fencing, and is demonstrated at a model size beyond one worker's memory share.
A long run checkpoints and restarts mid-phase after worker loss or cancellation to the same final result.

The shared remote, partitioned and thread-parallel contracts are one implementation reached by every family: no family-specific placement table, and unsupported placements fail typed before result commitment.

requirements.title: Millions of degrees of freedom at stated time and memory
requirements.acceptance: Each family's published example runs at a stated model size, wall time and peak memory on stated hardware, with models of millions of degrees of freedom solved on a workstation and a cluster, and whole-task resources measured rather than inferred from component reservations.

obligations.criterion: Each family solves a model of at least one million degrees of freedom (cells for flow) through the public command within a stated wall time and memory, on stated hardware, with the result checked against the same reference as the small case.
For every physics page example the node count, degrees of freedom, wall time, peak memory and hardware are generated from the run and published.

Whole-task peak resident memory is measured across worker processes and compared with the admitted estimate; admission never over-reserves a practical small model (buckling at 3,000 nodes, modal output, blade) and never admits a model that then exceeds its bound.

The plan reports cores, memory, wall time and core hours before a run; each run records per-stage usage and classifies failures (resource, numerical, input, infrastructure) in typed form, and the stated core-hour figure per guide is measured on the release.

Steady flow on 1 million cells on a 16-core workstation completes in under 3 minutes and 4 GB, 10 million cells in under 45 minutes and 40 GB; transient flow sustains at least 2 million cell-steps per second per CPU node; strong-scaling efficiency is at least 70 percent down to 50,000 cells per core.

requirements.title: Structural capabilities the page claims
requirements.acceptance: Every structural capability the page states runs from a `.fea` study on imported geometry with its result checked against a reference: shells and beams, the full load and connection inventory, nonlinear analyses, and the references the page quotes.

obligations.criterion: A shell panel (MITC3, homogeneous and laminate layups with orthotropic plies) and a beam frame (general, rectangular, circular and tube sections) run from a `.fea` study on imported geometry and publish results; a plate matches the plate-bending formula, a frame matches beam theory, and a frame with code limits written as assessments returns verdicts.

Every structural load the docs list runs and conserves its resultant: total, distributed and remote-point forces, moments and torque, traction, pressure (wind, mapped from a fluid result, hydrostatic), gravity and body force, inertial and centrifugal acceleration, base acceleration and earthquake motion, bolt preload, bearing loads on holes, thermal expansion, line loads, harmonic amplitudes, load cases and combinations, and local coordinate systems.

Fixed supports, prescribed motion, couplings, ties, periodic constraints, equations, axial springs and dashpots, point springs to ground, elastic foundations, six-DOF bushings, rotational springs, nonlinear springs and gaps, frequency-dependent mounts and bonded interfaces run with reactions that balance the loads, and no weak spring, mass, damping, reference constraint or load case is added silently.
A `structural nonlinear` cantilever under a tip load to large rotation matches the elastica solution with Newton and load stepping.
A published J2 plasticity example (linear isotropic hardening, follower loads) runs and matches the manufactured or analytic reference including unloading.
A published frictionless and Coulomb contact example (bolted bracket) runs from the public command and matches a Hertz or sliding reference.

Cantilever tip deflection matches PL^3/(3EI) (0.199 against 0.200 mm), the first bending frequency matches Euler-Bernoulli (81.3 against 81.5 Hz), and a random-vibration study matches Miles' equation, with the coarse-mesh failure (0.1197 mm Tet4) flagged as cannot-tell rather than accepted.

Explicit spatial observations without a canonical solver mesh, duplicate recovered semantic samples and missing buckling mode-shape fields are fixed: observations resolve, samples are unique, and a buckling run publishes its mode shape field.

Independent references exist and pass for a thick-walled cylinder under pressure (Lame), torsion of a prismatic bar, multi-point constraint and rigid-body coupling cases, and Euler column and plate buckling load factors, each with a mesh-convergence record.
A random-response study driven by a PSD (GEVS-type) from modal data reports RMS and 3-sigma stress, matching an independent modal combination.

requirements.title: Thermal studies the pages run
requirements.acceptance: The thermal studies the page runs work as published: a film coefficient input swept for cooling, radiation to the surroundings, the heat sink at its balance, and power-cycle transients, each checked against a closed form or a balance.

obligations.criterion: A convection film coefficient is a typed input quantity (`heat_transfer_coefficient`), usable as a sweep parameter and on named faces with ambient temperature, and heat flux into and out of the part balances.
Gray surface-to-ambient radiation (emissivity) with convection on the same faces runs and closes its energy balance; a radiating plate matches sigma epsilon A (T^4 - T_inf^4).

The KiCad heat sink (aluminum, about 10 W on the mounting face, 35 W/m2/K convection to 25 C) solves and heater power in equals convection out within the accuracy target, with the peak temperature rise reported.
A sweep of film coefficient from still air to a fan evaluates peak temperature against 85 C per case and reports the minimum cooling that passes.
A transient power cycle runs and matches the lumped-capacitance reference for a high-conductivity body and the Fourier series for a slab.
